### 70 What the audit found (Kaveh 2026-10-22 "go on 70"): save questions chased with KEEP semantics; the binder's read set; the carries folded into the fact store
* 70.1 SAVE QUESTIONS ARE CHASED, WITH KEEP SEMANTICS. Today `_chase` admits mate / win / promote (and the king's evasions); a save question is verified by the one-ply
  keep family alone (`_parry_keeps`), which killed 2TUzC's Rxe5 twice (after Qe1: the parry Rxe1 was not a candidate; after Rf5: Rxf5 Qxf1+ Kh2 looks like a lost bishop one
  ply before Rxf1 wins the queen). A save route's SUCCESS is to keep: after every reply the balance is not below where it stood (dbal >= 0), the claim worth the stake saved
  (the piece's value) with kind "save" -- the chase's gain criterion (a route must reach >= 1) is for wins. Switch CHASE_SAVES (ON when built), at the root and the first inner
  level; the keep family stays as the cheap first verdict. Lean: nothing new -- a kept balance is `Forcing.routeLow` at 0; the claim's value is the stake by definition.
* 70.2 THE BINDER RECORDS ITS READ SET. A claim verified by the binder is stored with `claimed = (0, claim, frozenset())`: no read set, so the frame-lemma parry rule
  (a parry touches the read set) has nothing to read on binder claims and falls back to captures, checks and the named line. The binder knows what it read (the
  squares of the pattern, the replies' from/to squares, the pieces it counted): record them as the claim's reads; then the fallback goes.
* 70.3 THE CARRIES FOLDED INTO THE FACT STORE. 66.2's `carry_r` / `proofs` and 66.4's `chain_gaps` are second caches beside `ctx.facts` (52.13 / 52.19), which already
  keys closes by position and queues GAP facts with their resume marks. Carry the store's PROOF and GAP entries across tiers / pool passes and drop the dicts. Behaviour
  identical (compare the traces of eSJqH, j3ybl, the discovery position before and after).

per domain, PRODUCED -- the words, lemmas, estimates and policies: today chess's are handwritten (regress's defects and fixes, race, the binder families) and
stand as the seed and the benchmark the mined ones must reproduce (policies and estimates from the logs; lemmas mined from proved claims' frames and proved
against the axioms, the lemma generator). Layer 1 imports nothing from 2 or 3; layer 3 is replaceable module by module; a new domain = a new layer 2 and
an empty layer 3 filled by the same training. Layer 3 has two parts (Kaveh: "we might even supply the base words in the vocab for each domain"): the
BASE WORDS, supplied per domain -- the primitive predicates and measures over states, hand-written, few, each Lean-defined (chess: graph.py's attacks /
guards / pushes / distances / worth, the piece values, the terminals); and the PRODUCED vocabulary -- everything built from the base words and the axioms by the
machinery (defects, fixes, forcing words, endgame words, policies, estimates), trained or mined. 71.3's `Words` is therefore two interfaces: `BaseWords`
(supplied) and the produced-vocabulary registry; the agenda touches only the second, the second is built only from the first.

### 72 THE PRICED REACH: one word, "unit U reaches a job L within k moves at a price", and the leaf, the join question and their threats as its callers (Kaveh 2026-10-23 morning, from the loop's target 2)

THE DIAGNOSIS (loop iteration 1, three of five misses: I7k2H, 1hUBC, GWigp). Their question at the static leaf IS asked (52.13: their agenda with the move passed; 52.14: its claims become
our save roots). In all three it answered "no claim" because its vocabulary is ONE MOVE deep: a promote root exists only within 3 pushes (a count limit; GWigp's a-pawn needs 4), their
agenda never chases, and nothing in the vocabulary says "their king walks three steps to the knight that cannot move" (1hUBC's b8) or "the bishop that must take is deflected from
its pawn" (I7k2H). The miss is not the asking, it is the words. Kaveh: the leaf is not a quiescence search; it is THEIR ROOT, and the words it needs are the roll-forward of one unit.

THE WORD (Kaveh 2026-10-23: "attackable in, I love that", "nothing is illegal in chess, it just costs you something", "the natural form of cost is material and tempo").
`reach(s, U, L, k) -> (material, tempi) | None`: the cheapest way, by the exchange, for unit U to come to bear on location L within k of ITS OWNER'S moves, the other side's QUIET
moves passed and its PAYING CAPTURES assumed (Lean `Ideas.Vocabulary.attackableIn`: every landing safe by the exchange; here a landing is allowed at the exchange's price instead
of forbidden, so `attackableIn` is the price-0 case). The price is a PAIR: material (the sum of what the exchange takes on the landings) and tempi (the moves). The answer "None"
means no path at all within k. Soundness is asymmetric and that is the point: "the price exceeds the stake" is a KILL of the join question (if the unit cannot get there cheaply
enough even when they pass, it cannot get there at all); a payable price is a CANDIDATE line of k moves with no reply read -- a question, never a proof. The deflection exception
(their capture on a landing is a mistake because the capturer had a duty) is NOT read here: it is a forcing route, judged by the existing "capturing piece left a duty" word.
Kaveh's two knights: the first knight's price to the square is its own worth (it lands on an unsafe square), the second's is the first knight plus four tempi; whether either is worth
paying is the goal's stake against the price -- the judge's arithmetic, not a new one. Tempi are compared as the race does (`Ideas.Race.race_sound`, `Game.race_sound`): our k against
the tempi THEIR fastest counter-plan needs; material against the Game's `measure`.
THE CAGED PIECE IS NOT A VALUE (Kaveh 2026-10-23): a unit with no safe move still does its job where it stands (it guards; it blocks a passer). It is a LIABILITY only as the answer
"no, at any price" to "can it join THIS attack / defence" -- and a TARGET only when their unit can reach a square bearing on it at a price below its worth while it cannot run
(63.2 `can_run`). Neither needs a "caged" word; both are the reach word asked with a job.

* 72.3 THE STAKE RULE (Kaveh 2026-10-23 11:30: "tempo value depends on the situation; in certain situations we can prove that with one extra tempo we could win so and so material"). A tempo
  is worth what THE OTHER SIDE PROVES WITH THE MOVE PASSED TO IT: for one tempo that is the threat word as it stands (their claim against our pass; ours against theirs); for k tempi it is
  their fastest counter-plan within k-1 free moves, read by the same priced reach with the sides swapped (a candidate: it orders and prunes, the chase proves). A join plan STANDS when what it
  wins exceeds what their counter-plan buys with the tempi it spends; who arrives first is `Game.race_sound` (mu our tempi, nu theirs). Never a constant. GO (Kaveh 2026-10-23): build 72.3 on a
  branch by an agent; 72.5 likewise; the loop's iteration 2 only after both are merged and gated.

THE IDEA (Kaveh): we ask too many questions because we do not know the goal; the lines run into dead ends. A goal should be an ARRANGEMENT of our pieces -- a sequence of arrangements --
at the end of which a tactic wins (a mate, a piece, a promotion) and the exchange cements it. Pawns move one way and slowly, kings slowly, pinned or stuck pieces not at all: they are the FIXED
board, the SKELETON. The fast pieces (queens, rooks, bishops, knights with room) are imagined where they do the job, theirs ignored at first (a fast piece of theirs on a square we want is a
DEFLECTION sub-goal, not a wall), ours priced by the roll forward (72.1), the whole compared with their counter-plan by the race (72.3's stake rule), and the chase proves the survivor.
"If this pawn were one square forward it would do the job" is allowed (a pawn's push is a slow move it can make); "if this pawn were one square back" is not (the pawn never goes back).

THIS IS A SPECIFICATION FOR AN AGENT. Every term below is defined; build exactly this, nothing more. Stage 1 only (the LATER items at the end are not yours).

DEFINITIONS (all over a python-chess board `b` with the side `us` to move; `k` = the horizon, the reach fuse `regress.REACH_K`):
1. SLOW unit (either colour): a king; a pawn; a unit with no safe square (`regress.can_run(b, sq, other_side)[0]` is False -- read with the OTHER side as `us`, that is the side that would
   win it); a unit that is duty-bound (`regress.duty_bound(b, sq, other_side)`). FAST unit: every other unit. Print the partition once per root agenda as the trace line
   `skeleton: fixed K g1, P a2 b2 f2 g2 h2, N f3 (no safe square), B e2 (duty-bound); fast Q d1, R a1, R f1`.
2. SKELETON A, `skeleton_a(b, us)`: a copy of `b` with OUR fast units REMOVED (their units all kept). SKELETON B, `skeleton_b(b, us)`: skeleton A with THEIR fast units removed too.
   Both are counterfactual boards (`graph.with_piece` / `Board.remove_piece_at` on a copy; keep the side to move = us; drop en passant). Never push moves on a skeleton.
3. TARGET: (i) their king (goal kind `mate`); (ii) each SLOW unit of theirs that is not a king or a pawn (goal kind `win`, its square); (iii) the promotion square of each passer of ours
   (`regress.is_passer`; goal kind `promote`). No other targets.
4. PLACEMENT (mate targets only): one FAST unit of ours placed on a square from which it would give check on skeleton A (the squares aligned with their king for that piece kind, as
   `agenda._scan_reach` / `regress._aligned` read them; the placement square must be empty on the skeleton or hold a unit of theirs that a capture there could remove -- the latter is
   priced as a job whose landing is that square with bearing=False). For `win` and `promote` targets there is no placement.
5. JOBS of an arrangement: the DEFECTS of the goal read ON THE SKELETON with the placement applied, by the existing words and nothing else:
   mate: `words.CHESS_WORDS.mate_defects(skeleton_with_placement, us, placement)` -> for each defect: kind `flight` sq -> job (bear on sq); `checker takeable` -> job (bear on the placement
   square: a guard); `interposition` sq -> job (bear on sq); other kinds -> job (bear on the defect's square). win: `material_defects(skeleton, us, target)` -> `not attacked` -> job
   (bear on target); `defended` -> a DEFLECTION entry for each defender (see 7), no job. promote: `promote_defects(skeleton, pawn)` -> `path attacked` / `promo square attacked` -> job (bear on
   that square); `stopper` -> a DEFLECTION entry; `blocked` by our own unit -> that unit must step aside (a +1 tempo entry, see 6c).
   A job is `Job(square, kind, why)`. If a goal has MORE THAN 4 jobs it is dropped (a named fuse `SKELETON_MAX_JOBS = 4`, documented: the arrangement is then a plan the chase cannot verify in
   the horizon; not a limit on the engine's words).
6. THE PRICE of an arrangement = an ASSIGNMENT of our fast units to the placement (if any) and the jobs, each unit at most one job, minimising the pair (material, tempi) summed:
   a. the placement unit's cost is `reach_price(skeleton_a, unit_sq, placement_sq, k, bearing=False)` (it LANDS there); a job's cost is `reach_price(skeleton_a, unit_sq, job.square, k,
      bearing=True)` (it BEARS on it). Read on SKELETON A (our other fast units are off the board, so a path they block is open -- this is how "one knight gives way for the other" is priced).
      A unit that bears on its job already costs (0, 0).
   b. enumerate injective assignments (units <= 7, jobs + placement <= 5: at most 7*6*5*4*3 = 2520 tuples; fine) and take the least by (material, tempi); ties by the lexicographic order of
      the squares. If some job has NO unit that can reach it within k, the arrangement is UNREACHABLE (verdict `unreachable`, the job named).
   c. STEP-ASIDE: for each assigned unit, if a fast unit of ours that received no job stands on a square of the chosen path (the roll's `path` landings and the squares between consecutive
      landings on the live board `b`), add 1 tempo and record `step-aside: R a1 off the path`. (Stage 1 does not price what the stepping-aside piece does afterwards.)
   d. tempi are SUMMED across units (we move one piece per move: the arrangement is a sequence); material is summed.
7. DEFLECTIONS (skeleton B is read only to find these): for every job square (and the placement square) compute `bearing/occupancy` by THEIR units on the live board `b`: a fast unit of
   theirs that occupies or bears on a job square (so the job cannot be done as priced) is a `Deflection(their_sq, job_square)` entry. Stage 1 RECORDS deflections and marks the arrangement
   `open: deflection` when any exists -- it is not pushed as a question and is printed. (A slow unit of theirs guarding a job square makes the job as read on skeleton A: the defects already
   saw it, since skeleton A keeps their units; so deflections are exactly the FAST guards.)
8. THE STAKE RULE (72.3): `stake` = 100 for mate, the target's worth for win, `regress.STAKE_PROMOTE` for promote. `counter` = `regress.counter_value(...)` as 72.3 built it, with mu = the
   arrangement's total tempi (their counter-plan within mu-1 free moves). Verdict `refused` when `stake - material - counter < 1`, with the text 72.3 uses ("their R reaches our Q in 1").
   Else verdict `reachable`.
9. OUTPUT: `regress.skeleton_goals(b, us, k=REACH_K) -> list[Arrangement]`, each a dataclass: target (square or 'king'), goal kind, placement (unit sq, square) or None, jobs, assignment

### 72.10 THE LOCAL INNER AGENDA: carry the frame and the goal forward; after their move ask three questions, not twenty-five (Kaveh 2026-10-23 evening, GO)

THE OBSERVATION (W0VFO at 10 s, OBS: questions asked 3,846, inner agendas 152 -- ~25 questions per inner agenda where Kaveh's reasoning needs one: "Qb7 threatens mate; who can be brought
to the defence in one move? the queen cannot; a rook can, and is lost; can they delay? they cannot"). The REPLIES are already local: a reply that touches none of the claim's read set
leaves the claim binding and is closed by the frame lemma (W0VFO's Qb7: "2 parries: Rf7, Rc7"). The INNER AGENDA opened after a parry is not: it rebuilds every root question of the new board
(win each piece, save each piece, promote, forks) and runs their whole agenda with the pass. THE PROOF THAT THE REST OF THE BOARD CAN BE NEGLECTED exists: every word carries a read set;
`Ideas.FrameLemma` (proved) says a move touching none of a word's reads leaves its value; the contrapositive: anything NEW after a move (a parry, a fresh threat of theirs, a delay) has a
word whose reads meet the move's DIFF (its from and to squares, the lines it opened and closed -- `Ideas.Battery` for the discovered ones). What is not a function of squares (the fifty-move
count, repetition, insufficient material) is a TERMINAL read by the Game, not a claim: nothing is lost by locality.

THIS IS A SPECIFICATION FOR AN AGENT (Opus). Build exactly this.
1. THE DIFF of their reply r on board b: `diff(b, r)` = {from, to} ∪ the squares on every line through `from` now opened (the ray beyond `from` in each direction up to the first piece, for
   sliders of ours and theirs that now see through) ∪ the squares on every line from `to` the moved piece now bears on ∪ (captures) the captured square ∪ (castling / en passant / promotion)
   the extra squares they touch. Reuse `AC.Pos.diff` / `P0.diff(P2)` (agenda.py: `frozenset(P0.diff(P2))`) if it is this; else write it in regress.py with a test against a brute-force
   "every word whose value changed" check on 50 random positions (the Lean condition: the diff is a superset of every changed word's reads).
2. THE CARRIED FRAME: the chased claim's read set (the question's `reads`, the route's facts' reads: agenda `_claim_reads`, 52.21 (2)) and its goal are passed into the inner agenda
   (`Agenda(..., frame=reads, goal=q)`); today's `inherit`/`diff` machinery (52.12 (3), 52.13 (1), `_inherit_for`) is the place -- extend, do not duplicate.
3. THE THREE QUESTIONS the local inner agenda asks after a parry, in this order, and NOTHING ELSE while the chased claim is alive:
   Q1 THE CLAIM ON THE DIFF: re-verify the chased claim with its reads ∩ diff re-read (the binder re-asked on the touched squares; if the claim binds again the reply was no parry -- closed);
      if it no longer binds, its DEFECTS on the new board (the existing defect words, read on the diff's squares only) and the fixes of those defects are the routes (the chase as today, but
      only for this goal).

      each as a save root of ours with the stake of what it wins -- `_threat_roots` restricted to claims whose reads meet the diff (their agenda with the pass is run on the diff's squares
      only: its roots are the units bearing on or standing in the diff).

      of ours the claim no longer binds; otherwise it is priced (what the exchange takes) and closed.

   new. Flag `LOCAL_INNER = True` in agenda.py.

## 73. THE LEMMA STORE: derived words, not hand-coded ones (Kaveh 2026-10-25 GO "Do the lemma store"; spec for Opus agents, two parts in sequence)

Kaveh, 2026-10-25, on the Rust boundary's ports of the pass claim, the race claim and the mate duty: "we've been hand-coding a lot of things, and by taking them from Python to
Rust we will never find that we've been hand-coding them ... The concept of a tempo and the concept of material are the only base concepts. Attacks, movements, tempo, time and
material are the base concepts. Everything else should be derived ... by the machinery and not by us ... I would expect these things to be in a lemma store, not a fact store."

THE THREE STORES, kept apart: the FACT STORE (plan 52.19-52.21) holds per-position claims keyed by what they read, served on transpositions; the POLICY (plans 60, 69) holds
ORDER, which question and which route first; LEAN holds proofs. None holds a WORD. The LEMMA STORE holds the derived words: what the agenda may ask beyond the base, where each
came from, what it rests on, and whether it is proved.

THE BASE (supplied, never derived; plan 71.3's `BaseWords`): MOVEMENT and ATTACK (a unit's moves and the squares it bears on; legality), TEMPO (whose move; a count of moves), MATERIAL
(a unit's worth; the exchange count on a square, the exchange law `Ideas.ExchangeLaw`). The rules of the game (check, mate, stalemate, the draws) are the game's, not words.

### 73.1 What an entry is
A LEMMA ENTRY is a derived word with: `name` (the string the trace already prints in `Claim.lemma` / the kill and GAP reasons: "delayed_root_max_alive_d1", "chase: step_after+step_least",
"mate_in_two", "repetition", "syzygy", "stuck_reach", "tempo arithmetic ...", ...); `kind` -- CLOSING (closes a line at a leaf: the exchange reading, "nothing of theirs"), DEFECT/FIX (why a
goal fails and what mends it: flight, stopper, blocker, interposition, deflection, the priced stopper), FORCING (why a move forces: check, capture, threat of mate, the delayed threat, the
passer threat), TECHNIQUE (a goal with a MEASURE and a terminal theorem: the K+Q mate's region, plan 62.3's `mating.rs`), STOP (a chain stop: the chase clock, tempo arithmetic, the second
check in a row), TABLE (the five-men table: an oracle, kind of its own); `reads` -- the base words it is built from (movement, attack, tempo, material: at least one; a word reading none is a
finding); `terms` -- the vocabulary s-expressions it compiles, when it is a term (the compiled terms are ALREADY compositions over the base: the generic part we have); `status` -- PROVED
(the Lean theorem names it mirrors, each present in docs/LEAN_INDEX.md: AGENTS rule 11), CONJECTURE (evidence, no proof), REFUTED (a position where it is wrong), HEURISTIC (a stop or a
tie-break with no proof obligation: labelled so, never called proved); `origin` -- BASE, HAND (we wrote it: the plan number and the journal date), MINED (the generator produced it: the run
and the corpus); `measure` (TECHNIQUE only: the quantity the per-move question drops; the floor at which the terminal theorem binds); `evidence` -- use counts from runs (how often asked,
how often it closed or claimed, printed as OBS), the positions that refuted or confirmed it; `implementation` -- where it runs (regress.py / words.rs / race.py / mating.rs / agenda.py: the
function names) so the port is visible, not hidden.

### 73.2 The store (part 1, agent A)
A tracked directory `catspace/incubator/analyst/discovery/lemmas/` (small JSON, one file per entry, git-tracked -- NOT data/derived), a loader `lemma_store.py` (load, get by name,
report, validate), and a CLI `python -m catspace.incubator.analyst.discovery.lemma_store report|validate|uses <trace or qlog>`. VALIDATE fails when: a PROVED entry cites a theorem not in
LEAN_INDEX; an entry has no `reads`; two entries share a name; a `name` printed by the engine (in a trace's claims, kills, GAPs, judge lines) is not in the store -- the agenda's lemma
strings are collected from the trace guard's snapshots (traces + the fact store's lemma fields) and from the ten + wide case sets, so an uncatalogued word is a test failure
(`tests/test_plan73.py`). The store does not change a single decision: the guard (traces, read sets, leaf lists, ten + wide, tier 0 and 2) is identical before and after.

### 73.3 The honest inventory (part 1, agent A)
Every produced word the engine prints today becomes an entry with origin HAND: from regress.py / words.rs (defects, fixes, forcing reasons, the priced stopper, reach/stuck, the passer
duty, the race words), graph.py's terms (the vocabulary s-expressions: list them with their base reads), race.py, mating.rs (the K+Q TECHNIQUE: measure = the region's off-edge squares,
terminal `Ideas.QueenMate.kq_mate_on_edge`), table.py (TABLE), the chase's lemma strings ("chase: step_after+step_least", "repetition", "unfinished line", "none" = the smallest loss,
"stuck_reach", "their open question"), the STOPs (the chase clock, tempo arithmetic, the second check in a row, the fuse, the judge's cut: all HEURISTIC), and docs/SWITCHES.md's
plan-numbered mechanisms where they name a word. Each PROVED entry cites its Lean theorems by name (from the docstrings, verbatim; where a docstring cites none, status is CONJECTURE and
that is a FINDING in the report, never a silent upgrade). The report prints OBS: entries total, by kind, by status, by origin; the words whose Lean citation is missing; the words that
read no base word. A per-run OBS line in the agenda's tally: `OBS lemma uses <id>: name count, ...` for the lemmas that closed, claimed or stopped in that run (the use counts feed `evidence`
later; nothing is written back during a run).

### 73.4 The adapter (part 1, agent A)
The engine prints lemma names from many sites. The adapter is ONE place: `lemma_store.name(s)` returns `s` after checking it is a known entry (or a known PATTERN: the chase composes
"chase: step_after+step_least over X, Y" from entry names; "carried from tier ...", "[tier pool 1]" are prefixes, not words); unknown -> a `GAP` note "uncatalogued word <s>" in the trace
(never an exception in a run: the gap is counted, `ctx.uncatalogued`, and the validator fails on it). The agenda's claim/kill/GAP sites call it where they set `lemma`. Behaviour identical;
the trace gains no line when every word is catalogued. Words.py's `Words` protocol gets `lemmas()` -> the store (the domain tells the machinery which produced words it has and their status).

### 73.5 The generator (part 2, agent B, after part 1 is merged): the K+R v K lemma, mined not written
THE RECIPE (the K+R v K discussion, 2026-10-23): (1) THE CLASS: a frame class where the engine often has NO CLAIM -- the material signature (K+R v K first; the generator takes the
signature as its argument and must work unchanged on K+Q v K, see acceptance); (2) THE CORPUS: won games in the class -- play-outs from random legal starts, the winning side moved by the
Syzygy table (DTZ-best), the defender by the table's slowest line, 50 to 200 games, the fifty-move rule and repetition observed (`scripts/play_krk.py`-style driver, generalised to the
signature; the table is the ORACLE here and only here: it writes the corpus, it never answers in the agenda); (3) THE MEASURES: a small library of quantities DERIVED FROM THE BASE, each a
function of (board, side): the REGION of their king (the squares it can reach by king moves without stepping onto a square we attack, our units held still: movement + attack; its size, its
off-edge part, its bounding box area), the distance of their king to the nearest edge / corner (movement), the king distance (movement), our material and theirs (material), the tempo
count (tempo), and the PRODUCTS and SUMS of two of them (one level of composition; no hand-picked K+R formula); a measure is a CANDIDATE TECHNIQUE when over the corpus it is non-increasing
on every winning move (strictly decreasing on at least one move in every game) and its FLOOR (the minimum before the mate) is where the existing mate words bind (`mate_in_one` /
`mate_in_two` / the planner's three-move net), printed as OBS per measure: games, moves, violations, floor; the generator chooses the measure with no violation and the smallest floor
spread, and if several tie, the one with the fewest base reads (the simplest); (4) THE ENTRY: kind TECHNIQUE, origin MINED, status CONJECTURE, `measure` = the chosen quantity's term
(a composition over the base, printed), `terminal` = the mate word at the floor, the Lean OBLIGATION written as a statement in the entry (the twin of `kq_mate_on_edge`: "in the class, mate
only at the floor"); it becomes PROVED only when the theorem is in LEAN_INDEX (agent B may prove it if it is within reach; else it stays a CONJECTURE and says so); (5) THE QUESTION: the
agenda asks a TECHNIQUE entry as a GOAL: in a position of the class with no claim, the root question "drop the measure" with routes = the legal moves after which the measure is lower
against EVERY reply (the minimax of the measure at depth one, the existing "can I force a drop in our measure" reading), each route refused if it stalemates, hangs the piece (the exchange
law) or allows a claimable draw (the game's rules); ties by the smaller floor distance; no route -> the technique is silent (GAP "no measure-dropping move", never a kill) and the agenda
goes on as today. The entry's `evidence` records the corpus and the acceptance runs.
ACCEPTANCE (printed, directional): (a) `play_krk.py` with the table claim OFF and the mined entry ON: result, questions per move, moves to mate, three random starts -- against the
2026-10-23 baseline (draw by repetition, 35 questions per move); (b) GENERICITY: the same generator on K+Q v K must produce a measure equivalent to the hand-made one in mating.rs (the
region's off-edge squares, or one that mates the corpus equally) WITHOUT reading mating.rs; print both measures' OBS; (c) the guard's ten + wide cases: identical (no case is in the class);
(d) K+R v K with the table claim ON is unchanged (the table outranks a conjecture: `_claim_key`). The K+Q entry from mating.rs is re-labelled HAND/PROVED in the store and the mined K+Q
entry sits beside it as MINED/CONJECTURE: the two are the store's first comparison.
NOT IN 73: deriving the pass claim, the race claim and the mate duty from the base (the inventory makes them visible as HAND; their derivation is the generator's next class, over the
puzzle corpus rather than endings, and is written after 73.5 reports what the generator can and cannot find).

COST: part 1 none (identical); part 2's corpus is written once (the table), the measures are evaluated offline; the technique question costs one measure evaluation per legal move per
reply at the root of a position in the class and nothing elsewhere.

### 73.5b THE GENERATOR, AMENDED (2026-10-25; the first run of 73.5 found no technique in K+R v K or K+Q v K -- the SPEC asked the wrong question)
THE ERROR (the spec's, not the agent's): 73.5 (3) chose a measure that is non-increasing ON THE TABLE'S MOVES. The table's fastest play is not a technique: it takes shortcuts every
measure counts as backwards (OBS: game 0, 8/8/4K3/6k1/3R4/8/8/8 w, after Re4 and the table's reply the region's area 16 -> 32; the line still mates). The plan's own Lean obligation
(73.5 (4)) asks something else: "above the floor a measure-dropping move exists against every reply". The corpus play need not follow the measure; the measure must ADMIT a drop.
OBS (73.5's labelled diagnostic, directional): the lexicographic pair (region size, then kings' distance) has no dropping move against every reply at 168 of 1116 KRvK positions one
move deep and at 5 two moves deep; KQvK 23 of 683 one move deep, 4 two moves deep. The hand-made K+Q technique (mating.rs) has exactly the three missing parts: a lexicographic measure
of three ranks, a tempo move within two or three moves, a floor that is a three-move net.
THE AMENDED CRITERION. A measure M is a TECHNIQUE for a class when, on a SAMPLE of the class's won positions (the corpus positions AND uniformly sampled won positions of the class, the
table judging "won"; the winning side to move), every position is either AT THE FLOOR -- the engine's existing mate search finds a mate within n moves (n = 2, the mate words; then
n = 3, a full three-move mate search, as mating.rs's net) -- or admits a DROP: a strategy of ours of at most d moves (an AND-OR search: some move of ours, every legal reply, ...) after which M
is strictly lower, never passing through a stalemate, a unit the exchange law loses, or a claimable draw (the game's rules). M bounded below and strictly dropping makes the technique
terminate; the floor makes it mate.
THE COMPOSITIONS (generic combinators over the base atoms of 73.5 (3), never a formula named after an ending): the atoms; their sums and products (as before); and the LEXICOGRAPHIC
TUPLE of atoms (compare the first; on a tie the second; ...). TEMPO enters as d (our moves allowed before the drop: a waiting move is a move of ours that drops nothing yet).
THE SEARCH, simplest first, principled: d = 1, then 2, then 3; for each d, one rank, then two, then three; the first (d, ranks) where some measure has ZERO failures on the sample is the
answer; among those, the fewest base reads. The named fuse is the hand-made K+Q technique's own shape (three ranks, d three, n three): beyond it the generator stops and reports the best
measure and its failing positions -- a result, not a relaxation. Cheapest first: every candidate at d = 1 on every sample position; only its failures at d = 2; only those at d = 3; memo
by (position key, d, measure); print the cost.

### 73.6 THE PROVER: the engine states the obligation and an off-the-shelf prover finds the proof (Kaveh 2026-10-27 GO: "instruct the engine to try to find the proof using alpha proof
or whatever off the shelf tool instead of exhaustive search"; "I don't want you to write this")
The 73.5b technique's obligation was CHECKED on all 175168 positions of the class: an enumeration, not a proof (Kaveh: "doing an exhaustive check on all king+rook positions is dumb. The
proof is simple."). The reference proof is his, in the journal of 2026-10-27, and it is NOT given to the prover in the blind attempt. Nobody writes the proof: the engine writes the
STATEMENT, the tools search for the proof, Lean checks it.
(1) THE STATEMENT, emitted by the engine. `technique_lean.py` turns a TECHNIQUE entry of the store into a Lean file `lean/ideas/Ideas/Mined/<slug>.lean` over the chess-lean rule kernel
the library already uses (Game.step / the board model of QueenMateBoard, Ideas.Forced): the class predicate (the material signature, the winning side to move), the moves `ours` (legal,
with the never-rules: no stalemate, no unit the exchange law loses, no claimable draw) and `theirs` (legal), the measure as DEFINITIONS generated from its term (each vocabulary atom
compiled to a Lean definition over positions; the lexicographic tuple to its mixed-radix number, as the entry's obligation already says), and the theorem `hprog` of
Ideas.Forced.forced_by_measure at k = the entry's depth, with `sorry`; the corollary (the forced mate from every position of the class) is proved from `hprog` by forced_by_measure in the
emitted file, mechanically. The file must BUILD with the one `sorry` (the statement type-checks) before any prover runs; a statement the kernel cannot express is a FINDING.
(2) THE ATOMS, generic: add per-axis distances (a unit's rank / file distance to an edge; the rank / file distance between two units) and the side to move's parity to the miner's library
(73.5 (3)), so "distance from opposition on each rank" is expressible from movement and tempo; re-mine KRvK (and KQvK); emit the statement for the chosen measure and for every zero-failure
measure of the chosen level (the prover may find one easier than another). The whole-class check stays EVIDENCE, never the proof.
(3) THE PROVER HARNESS `prover.py`, cheapest first, each attempt checked by Lean: (a) Lean's own automation on each `sorry` (aesop, simp, omega; Duper / lean-auto if a version matches Lean
4.32 and Mathlib v4.32); (b) LeanCopilot's search_proof if it builds on 4.32; (c) an OPEN-WEIGHT PROVER run locally through ollama (Goedel-Prover-V2-8B, DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B or NanoProof:
whichever is available as weights that fit 36 GB; name it and its version) in an AGENTIC LOOP: whole-proof attempts with the compiler's errors fed back, and SUBGOAL DECOMPOSITION -- the
model proposes `have` lemmas, each becomes its own `sorry` attacked recursively (the DeepSeek-Prover-V2 / Discover-and-Prove pattern); (d) Harmonic's Aristotle API ONLY when a key is
configured (`ARISTOTLE_API_KEY`; absent -> skipped with a line saying so; never send files without it). A named fuse per obligation (wall-clock, stated), not a count tuned to a result.
BANNED in an accepted proof (Kaveh's rule: by reasoning, never brute force): `native_decide` (`#print axioms` must show no `Lean.ofReduceBool`), `decide` / `Fintype` enumeration over
positions or squares-of-the-class, `sorry`, new axioms. A proof that passes `lake build` and these checks is accepted.
(4) THE STORE: an accepted proof makes the entry PROVED (lean = the theorem names; LEAN_INDEX rebuilt); every SUB-LEMMA the prover proved on the way becomes its own entry (origin MINED,
kind by role -- a lemma like "the rook is never lost to a lone king" is a word in itself, Kaveh: "This should be a lemma in itself"), reusable by the agenda and by the next proof. Unproved
sub-goals become CONJECTURE entries with the prover's last state. Everything the prover tried is logged (artifacts/experiments/prover/), the tally printed as OBS.

## 74. THE REASONING GRAPH: one worklist over a justification graph, generic (Kaveh 2026-10-27 GO: "Do it because it seems generic. As long as it's generic, I'm happy to do these
advances so that we can automatically ask questions and find the answers."; spec for an Opus agent, queued behind 73.6 -- both touch agenda.py, one agent at a time)

Kaveh's picture: "a chain or a line of reasoning ... I do this, then he wants to do this or that ... lines of reasoning converge and the reasoning progresses ... a graph of reasoning ... if
I'm analyzing one line and a question pops in my head, I queue it for later." The shape has names: a GIVEN-CLAUSE worklist (passive / active sets, the best passive item processed next,
its consequences re-queued: Otter, E), a JUSTIFICATION-BASED TRUTH MAINTENANCE SYSTEM (every belief with its justifications; a retracted premise retracts its dependents: Doyle, de Kleer),
Soar's IMPASSE -> SUBGOAL -> CHUNK, and AND-OR search over replies (Allis). What exists: the agenda heap (root only), GAPs with resume points drained by the ponder, the fact store keyed by
read sets with the listener (the TMS), the chase (the impasse step), the survey's clues (trace + policy features only), the printed justification graph of a decision. What is missing: ONE
worklist across depths (inner agendas are recursive calls: a question found three plies deep cannot be handed to the root's queue), PROVENANCE on questions ("arose from that line"), and
clues as nodes. Nothing in 74 is chess: a test asserts the new modules name no unit, no piece, no square word (as 73.5b's does).

### 74.1 The graph
Nodes: QUESTION (goal, stake, its FRAME = the read set it binds on, depth, provenance), LINE (a route and the reply path to a position: the moves as ucis, the position key), ANSWER (a claim,
a kill, a GAP, with the justification edges the trace already prints as `#id claim ... reads {...}`), OBSERVATION (74.4). Edges: AROSE_FROM (question <- line or observation), SERVES
(answer -> question), READS (answer -> the position's read set: the fact store's key, so two lines that reach positions agreeing on the read set meet at one answer: convergence),
REFINES (a chase question -> the question it chases). One store: the fact store extended with questions and edges (its keys and listener unchanged), or the Rust kernel's Datalog
(`ascent`, plan 40's agenda.rs) if it fits without a rewrite -- the agent decides from the code and says why; Python first is acceptable.

### 74.2 One worklist
A single PASSIVE set of questions for the whole run, every depth; an item carries (stake, depth, provenance, forcedness of its replies, the policy's score). SELECTION = the judge's rule
(72.9: can this question change the decision? are its replies forced? then read it whatever the rate) and the policy's order, as today -- one rule for root and inner alike. The
budgets are today's (count / time); 74 adds no number. An item whose key (position read set + goal) has an ANSWER in the store is SERVED, not asked (convergence); an item whose frame is
hit by a later move is re-asked by the listener, as claims are today.

### 74.3 The chase as expansion
A route is expanded depth-first WITHIN ITS FRAME exactly as 72.10 does (the three local questions inline: the goal on the diff, their threats through the diff, the price of their move).
Any question outside the frame is ENQUEUED with provenance (arose from this line at this position), never asked inline. 72.10's "the full agenda when the goal is dead there" becomes:
enqueue that position's root questions (depth d+1, provenance the line), mark the route PENDING on them (the cheap pass's pending protocol), continue; the route closes when its pending
questions are answered or cut (a cut is a GAP with the resume point, as today). The inner agenda as a recursive call disappears in the end state; in the build it is replaced stage by stage.

### 74.4 Clues
An OBSERVATION node = a term evaluated at a position with its reads (the survey lines of 72.5 are the first; a bounded-reach fact "no attack along this line for at least t tempi while these
blockers stand" is another, reads = the blockers; a mobility count another). Observations sit low in the worklist; one is PROMOTED to a question when a goal's frame touches its reads or
the policy scores it above an open question. Words to mine, not code: 74 adds the node type and the promotion rule, no new chess word.

### 74.5 Provenance in the trace
Every question prints why it was asked ("asked: arose from Qb7 Rf7 at depth 1" / "served: the answer of <line> read the same squares"); the decision's justification graph (already printed)
gains the question edges. The explanation a user reads is the chain Kaveh described.

### 74.6 Acceptance (printed, directional)
The restructure may reorder trace LINES; it may not change DECISIONS. On the ten + the 99 wide cases at the count budget (PYTHONHASHSEED=0): every DECISION line identical; the set of claims
(what, value, proved) identical per case; the read sets identical; the leaf verdict lists identical; the trace text diff listed and read (order only). Questions asked per case NOT higher
(the point: inline full agendas become queued, deduplicated items) -- print before/after per case and the total. W0VFO at 10 s: decision and proof unchanged, inner questions printed.
The loop-2 batch (rand14_10 .. rand17_10 at 15 s, graded by proof in a separate process): not worse than 31 RIGHT / 7 WRONG (one batch each, directional). The gate: every file green.

### 74.7 Stages, one commit each, each acceptance-checked before the next
(a) the graph store with provenance and the trace lines of 74.5 -- behaviour identical (traces identical modulo the new lines, which the guard masks by a prefix); (b) the single worklist
for ROOT questions only (the heap replaced; selection as today) -- decisions identical, traces identical; (c) inner questions enqueued with the pending protocol, depth 1 first, then all
depths -- decisions identical, questions not higher; (d) observations as nodes with the promotion rule -- decisions identical on the guard (no promotion fires there unless shown and read).
NOT IN 74: distribution (the worklist is the seam: AND-OR nodes are independent work; later), new chess words, the Rust port of the loop (72.7's remaining steps), any change to the judge's
rule or the policy.

## 75. THE GENERIC GOAL AND THE SUPPLIED VOCABULARY (Kaveh 2026-10-27 GO "go ahead and do it")

Kaveh: "the goal is actually very generic: first of all, don't lose, and then win ... some chess vocab has to be provided by us because we want the engine to be able to talk in the same
language as we do. We don't want it to learn everything. But from those basic things -- attacking, moving and sliding pieces, winning and drawing -- everything else should be derived from
the basic rules."
THE PRINCIPLE, in three lines: (1) THE GOAL is the outcome: don't lose, then win (the status line of plan 59 is already this ladder: losing / level / winning; status-driven widening = don't
lose, then win). Mate, material, promotion are not goals: mate is the rule's terminal, material is a DERIVED valuation, promotion is a rule. (2) WE SUPPLY NAMES, not knowledge: a NAMES
table binding our words (attack, move, slide, capture, check, mate, stalemate, draw, win, lose, the unit kinds, rank/file, tempo) to definitions of the RULE KERNEL, so the engine speaks our
language; a name is never bound to a derived fact. (3) EVERYTHING ELSE IS DERIVED: words, valuations, techniques, stops -- mined into the store, stated in Lean, proved by the prover, read by
the agenda from the store. A test guards it: the agenda's core names nothing beyond the NAMES table and the store.

### 75.1 The audit (read-only agent; runs beside the prover: it runs no gate and edits no engine file)
Every branch, constant and comparison of agenda.py (and the ponder, the tiers driver, the judge) classified as one of: LOGIC (goal regression, AND-OR, frames, the worklist, the budgets'
mechanics), RULE (a fact of the game's rules: check, mate, legal moves, the draws -- allowed, read through the kernel), NAME (a supplied name from the table), CHESS FACT (derived knowledge
written as code: the goal kinds mate/win/save/promote and their stakes, piece worth, the status line's thresholds, "a check is forcing", the stops' shapes, the smallest-loss tie-break's shape
key, the fuse's shape, the judge's forcedness words, the leaf's estimators), HEURISTIC (a tuned number or rule with no proof obligation). Output docs/AGENDA_AUDIT.md: one row per item (file:line,
the text, the class, and for a CHESS FACT the store entry it should become -- an existing one, or a new one named), the counts as OBS lines, and the list of CHESS FACTS in the order they
should move (by how many decisions depend on them, read from the traces of the ten + wide guard snapshots). No engine change in 75.1.

### 74.2b THE SELECTION RULE'S FIRST CLAUSE (Kaveh 2026-10-27): the cheapest move that keeps the status, then a better one
Kaveh: "spend your resources when searching for a move to find the cheapest move that'll maintain your state. If you're winning, keep winning; if you're drawing, keep drawing. And then you
look for a better move from there." This is plan 59's ladder (status-driven widening) made the WORKLIST's selection rule, root and chase alike, in two clauses in this order: (1) while no move
is PROVED to keep the status, select the open question whose answer would keep it at the lowest expected cost -- cost = the judge's own price (nodes x the measured rate, 72.9), the policy
ordering only among questions of equal price class; (2) once a keeping move is proved, select by the judge's existing question "can this change the decision, are its replies forced". The
pool today orders by stake and the policy first (a stake-100 mate question before a cheap save that already keeps the status: W0VFO's and 2CEDb's seconds); after 74 it orders by clause (1)
first. No new number. Acceptance adds: on the ten + wide, the time (or count) to the FIRST proved keeping move, printed before/after, not higher.


## 76. THE RULE SPEC AND THE ONTOLOGY: chess becomes an input (Kaveh 2026-10-28 GO "Yes, and go")

Kaveh: "the machinery -- the learning and storing and remembering and applying machinery -- has nothing to do with chess. Chess is a rule set which comes and becomes the base layer of
every other learned reasoning on top of it." And on risk: "if there is a disagreement somewhere, that's a surprise. We look at that disagreement and say what do we need to add or subtract
... and keep asking questions logically. That is the essence of the machinery." The complication is accepted for the generality.

THE DESIGN. One physical store, three logical shelves: RULE (the game's rules: given, never derived; in Lean they are DEFINITIONS, not axioms), LEMMA (derived words, plan 73), FACT (per
position, plan 52.19). Below the rules, THE ONTOLOGY: object kinds (supplied: square, unit, side, move, board, clock; derived: line, ray, blocked, region, reach, ...) and relation kinds
(at, moves_to, attacks, blocks, on_line, defends, reach_k, ...), each ONE NAME with THREE BINDINGS -- the Rust relation (the Datalog in rules.rs), the Lean definition, the store entry -- and a
test that the three agree (as names.py's 22 names do today). No fifth vocabulary: the names table grows into the ontology shelf; the term language's atoms ARE the relations.

THE RULE LANGUAGE: GDL (Stanford's Game Description Language: Datalog clauses -- roles, init, legal, next, terminal, goal; GDL-II adds `sees` and `random` for hidden information and chance,
so fog-of-war chess is expressible later). Chosen because it IS Datalog and the Rust core runs Datalog; Ludii's chess description and its concept list are the cross-reference, not the
format. SPEC + IMPLEMENTATION: the GDL file is the source of truth and is slow; the fast kernel (shakmaty / python-chess) is an IMPLEMENTATION certified against it by cross-play; the Lean
definitions are GENERATED from the GDL (Datalog -> inductive definitions), never hand-written per piece again.

THE SURPRISE LOOP (the borrowings of 2026-10-28, each a small mechanism): (1) COUNTEREXAMPLES ARE PERMANENT: every cross-play disagreement, every refuted measure, every puzzle miss is
SHRUNK to its smallest position and written to a case set the guard and the miner read forever (the surprise store: a shelf of the one store); (2) CHUNK USE COUNTS: `evidence.uses` written
from the run tally; unused entries are pruned by a stated rule, never by a number; (3) AGE / WEIGHT: the worklist reads the OLDEST open item once per pass so cheapest-first never starves a
question (one principled rule); later, in the mining stages: (4) LEARNING FROM FAILURES: a measure violated at position P prunes every measure implied by it on P (the term language computes
implication); (5) INTERESTINGNESS FROM USE: a derived object's worth is how often accepted measures and proofs cite it (evidence.uses as the miner's prior) -- never a hand-written score
(AM / Eurisko's death).

### 76.4a DEFECTS AND FIXES FROM THE SPEC (Kaveh 2026-10-28, "how are the defects found and raised?": by hand, a fixed list per goal kind -- the largest chess fact still in code)
Today a goal is a pattern tested by a word; when the word fails the DEFECTS are a hand-written list per goal kind (mate: a flight square, the checker takeable, an interposition, the landing
attacked; material: defended, not attacked, can run; promotion: stopper, blocker, the square or the path attacked; fork: the landing unsafe, one target defends the other), and a second
hand-written table maps each defect to its FIX family (cover or block the flight, deflect or remove the taker, ...). The lists are a human reading of each definition's conjuncts.
Since 76.1-76.2 the definitions are the SPEC: mate, capture, promotion, check are relations of rules/chess.gdl with clause bodies, generated into Lean and proved equal to the kernel. GOAL
REGRESSION over a clause body is generic: the goal is a head; its DEFECTS are the body atoms false in this position (with the squares that make them false: the read set); a FIX is a move
after which such an atom becomes true, computed by the spec's next-state relation (certified: NextEquiv), filtered by legality (LegalEquiv). Nothing in that knows what a flight square is.
BUILD: `regression.py` (generic: works on any relation of the spec through the ontology shelf and the GDL interpreter; names no chess object) producing defects and fixes for the GOAL
entries; the hand tables (regress.py / words.rs: the D1a-D1h families of the audit) become TEST ORACLES; on the guard (ten + wide, tiers 0 and 2) the derived defects equal the hand defects
as sets per question (print disagreements and read each: a derived defect the table lacks is a FINDING -- the table was incomplete -- never a reason to filter); decisions identical; the
recount: the D1 families leave agenda.py / regress.py; then one goal we never wrote a table for ("win this exchange"; a mined technique's floor) regressed by the same code, shown in a
trace. Speed: the regression is cached per (position key, goal); the Rust port of the regression is 72.7's remaining step, not 76.4a; print the cost (ms per question) before and after.
Then 76.4 as written: mining objects (line, blocked, region as test cases), material as the first mined valuation, the second game.

### 77.3 THE LOOP PROPOSES ITS OWN WORDS (the miss -> word step, the heart of the first system)
(a) THE MISS AS INPUT: a loop miss (the surprise shelf: the position, the engine's answer, the right answer from the table / Stockfish in its own process, the trace with its GAPs and the
words it asked) is read by a PROPOSER: from the right answer's line (the moves that refute the engine's claim or prove the answer), the proposer asks the regression WHY the engine's claim
failed there (which body atoms were false) and WHAT the answer's line reads (its read set), and searches the term language (priced by size, pruned by implication) for a WORD -- a predicate
over the base relations -- that is TRUE on the answer's line and FALSE where the engine's claim stood (the frame of the miss), scored by use on the surprise shelf's other cases (does it
separate right from wrong there too?); the best candidates are filed as CONJECTURE entries with the miss as evidence and the Lean obligation stated (the emitter of 73.6); (b) THE WORD ASKED:
a filed word enters the agenda through the store as a CLOSING / FORCING word (the kind the proposer labels from where it bites: at the leaf, at the forcing read, at their pass), so the next
run of the miss asks it; the guard: decisions elsewhere identical, the miss's decision read (fixed / unchanged / changed otherwise, with Stockfish's reading); (c) THE LOOP RUN: iteration 3
(rand18_10 .. rand21_10 at 15 s): the misses traced by the proposer, not by hand; the words it proposes listed with their frames and their effect; the ones that fix a miss without breaking
the guard are kept as CONJECTURE (Kaveh adopts; nothing adopted by the machinery); the ones that fix nothing are the report (what the term language could not express: the next atom to
derive). Prior test of the proposer: the SEVEN loop-2 misses already on the surprise shelf, with their known causes (the leaf's their-side mate-in-two for r3oph; the recapture tempo stop;
the judge's cut) -- does the proposer find the word we found by hand? Print per miss.

### 77.0 THE INCREMENTAL-MAINTENANCE SPIKE (Kaveh 2026-11-03 "ok"; runs BEFORE 77.1: its numbers decide what the port builds)
Kaveh's core idea, restated 2026-11-03: the engine is a store of claims about the position (facts, predictions, proofs) kept consistent as the observables change -- "anytime the
observables change, all the relevant claims should change without incurring too much computation; that becomes an optimization problem". The field's name for that is INCREMENTAL VIEW
MAINTENANCE; the mature implementation is DBSP (the Rust engine under Feldera: signed change sets, incremental joins, recursion through nested circuits; circuits built at RUN TIME, so the
GDL file can stay the single source -- what ruled `ascent` out in 76.4b). Two kinds of change: the SLOW stream (the real game move by move; the claim store's retractions) and the FAST
hypothetical stream (the search: thousands of positions per second, make / unmake, relations over 64 squares). Expectation, NOT a measurement: DBSP fits the slow stream; its per-step
machinery may lose to bitboards on the fast one. If so, the fallback is NOT a fork of DBSP (its overhead is structural; a fork of a weekly-released crate is a standing cost) but a small
SUB-PROJECT crate of our own with DBSP's semantics -- signed deltas (undo = the negated delta), delta rules compiled from rules/chess.gdl at load time, relations as bitboards over a fixed
location domain, bounded recursion recomputed through the touched squares, the full evaluator as its oracle; game-generic by construction. And first of all: is deriving relations even a
large share of the search's time? (The profiles say the time is in the NUMBER of questions; the Rust regression is 0.054 ms per question.)
MEASURE: (1) THE DERIVATION SHARE -- cProfile / Rust timing of W0VFO at 10 s, the discovery position at 30 s, the ten at the count budget and five loop-2 puzzles at 15 s: the share of wall
in deriving relations (gdl.rs, the regression, the words) vs questions / inner agendas / the judge / Python overhead. (2) THE CRATE -- a separate spike crate (rust/spike_dbsp/, its own
Cargo.toml; analyst_core's build and the editable install untouched) building a DBSP circuit AT RUN TIME from rules/chess.gdl for cell, attack, check and the mate regression's relations;
outputs EQUAL to gdl.rs on the ten + wide + surprise positions and along a random game; timings: full recompute (gdl.rs) vs DBSP initial load; one move's incremental update; a make + unmake
pair; a claim-store retraction (claims as a relation claim(id, square) against the changed squares) vs the current fact store's listener; the crate's license read from its Cargo.toml.
(3) THE DECISION REPORT -- per layer: the crate for the slow layer yes / no; the sub-project for the fast layer needed yes / no given (1); what 77.1 should build.
NOT IN 77.0: any change to the engine's decision path; adopting anything (Kaveh decides on the report).

77.0 RESULT (2026-11-03, done in the main session -- Kaveh: "do it yourself"; the agent stopped): THE DERIVATION SHARE ANSWERS IT, the DBSP crate experiment deferred.

  five loop-2 puzzles 15 s: python-chess 41.0 %, Rust words 15.1 %, glue 14.0 %, builtins 10.6 %, agenda 9.1 %, Rust regression 4.0 %, store 2.3 %

### 77.1 (d) RULES INGESTION KEPT MINIMAL, ITS VERIFICATION IN THE MACHINERY (Kaveh 2026-11-04: "i don't want to hand-code anything chess-related ... extracting rules from GDL

only with a CERTIFICATE the engine keeps; everything that is not a rule (the exchange law, the passer lemma, the race word) is a store lemma -- its Lean proof, its declared domain, its
certificate against the regression -- and ideally mined.

inside a declared domain (masks of the kernel's unit kinds: Rust knows no lemma), and each lemma is asked only where its own domain holds. Acceptance: the definition's answers equal
before (the guard identical), no unit kind named in the glue.
(2) THE CERTIFY STAGE (`discovery/certify.py`, the package, not a script): every fast binding is an entry with the spec relation it ingests and its oracle (the GDL evaluator for a rule;
the regression on the spec for a claim: win, mate, mate in n; a lemma's declared domain against the lemma: it never fires outside it). The engine certifies at load on a fixed corpus
and keeps checking on a priced share of the positions its search visits; a certificate (positions, disagreements, date) is kept in the store; a disagreement is a fact, and the binding
is demoted (that relation read from the spec evaluator: slow, right). scripts/crossplay.py, plan76_4a.py crosscheck and the port harnesses become callers. Acceptance: the certificates
of every binding the hot path reads printed (OBS); a planted wrong binding (a test's) demoted and the decision read through the spec; the cost of the online share printed.

## 78 THE END-TO-END SYSTEM (Kaveh 2026-11-04: "i would rather have an end-to-end working system first, then improve upon the layers (and maybe multiple cooperating approaches for
each layer). Each layer should be modular and as much as possible chess-free. Let's scope it to handle all chess variants where perfect information exists for now. We want room to be
able to extend to not-perfect-information after getting chess done"; "the slow parts should be in rust, loops should be in rust"; "Good. Go")

THE AIM: a system that plays full games of every perfect-information chess variant with EVERY LAYER PRESENT (thin where it must be), then the layers improve one by one, each layer a slot
with competing approaches. What exists today (plans 52-77) is the TACTICS layer for chess, in Python over python-chess with its hot words in Rust; it becomes the chess REFERENCE
approach (`legacy-agenda`), not the foundation.
THE LAYERS (Rust crates in the workspace rust/engine/; the loops and the slow parts in Rust; Python only outside the loop -- the harness, the store editing, training, the trace's
formatting; one pyo3 entry, called once per move):
  game       the `Game` trait -- roles, the side to move, legal moves, apply, terminal -> the outcome per role, a state key, move names, and `observe(state, role)` (the identity for perfect
             information: the extension point of GDL-II's `sees`). Implementations: `GdlGame` (any GDL text: the spec evaluator, slow; gdl.rs moved into its own crate, which analyst_core
             then uses) and `KernelGame` (shakmaty's VariantPosition: chess, Chess960, crazyhouse, atomic, antichess, king of the hill, three-check, racing kings, horde).
  certify    the kernel against its GDL text per game, in Rust (the loop); a variant without a GDL file plays on its kernel with its certificate MISSING, and the report says so.
  tactics    trait: answer(state, goal, budget) -> claim / kill / GAP, with its trace. Approach `forcing`: the one definition (77.1) over the Game trait -- the every-reply clause on the
             terminal outcome and on the store's measure; `legacy-agenda`: today's engine (chess only).
  planning   trait: subgoals(state) -> ranked conditions with evidence. First approach `keep`: the cheapest move that keeps our state by the measure (the search law, 2026-10-27).
  decision   the anytime loop within the clock: a proved claim, else the planner's move, else the fallback; every choice traced.
  memory     the store read by Rust (serde): goals, valuations, names per game.
THE TEST that guards it: the layer crates name no chess object (the generic test, extended to Rust); only `KernelGame` and the GDL texts are chess. Variants are the test of it: their
goals differ (the centre, a third check, losing every unit, an explosion), their rules differ (drops, compulsory captures), antichess has no royal unit.
STAGES:
  78.1 the workspace; the `game` crate (the trait, GdlGame, KernelGame over every variant); certify in Rust (chess.gdl against the chess kernel first; variants' GDL texts as written --
       king of the hill and three-check first: goal changes only); OBS per game: positions, disagreements, or the certificate MISSING.
  78.2 the thin approaches in Rust (tactics `forcing`, planning `keep`, the decision loop); the pyo3 entry; a UCI engine (UCI_Variant) and the play server's variant games.
  78.3 THE MEASURE: full games per variant against a fixed opponent (Fairy-Stockfish if installed; until then a random mover, and for chess the legacy engine) -- results per variant,
       where each layer fell back, the cost per move.
THEN the layers improve: the trajectory planner from game data (lichess has variant games), 77.3's proposer, the legacy engine's chess facts moved to the store and its loop ported.

#### 78.12 THE SHARED INTERFACE AND THE BATCH SOLVER (2026-11-05; reconciling rust/engine with "Interpretable Game-Learning Engine Architecture", Kaveh's document of 2026-11-05)
THE AIM: the layers keep doing exactly what they do (no change of play), but through the interface the architecture document names, so a trained router, a mixture of experts
or a new operator plugs in without touching the others, and so a whole puzzle set is one call. Constraints kept: nothing game-specific in the interface (the generic test of
78.1 covers the new crates); every cost MEASURED (nodes and seconds returned by the call, never estimated); the Rust loop unchanged, Python only outside it.
  cs_operator (new crate)  `Operator::run(game, state, goal, budget) -> Outcome`; `Controller::choose(context) -> Action` (run an operator toward a goal with a budget, or play);
             `drive` (the loop, a step fuse). `Goal` = Win / Ledger / Keep / Prefer / Survey, each with its MODE (forced, cooperative, modeled) where it has one -- an operator that
             does not read a mode answers `Unsupported`, never a guess (mixing modes produces false lemmas). `Outcome` = status (Proved, NoLine, Gap, Read, Unsupported), the move,
             value, depth, equally good candidates, the evidence lines, the measured cost, the new facts. `Budget` (moved from cs_tactics, re-exported) gains a depth cap and the
             deadline of the whole decision.
  operators  tactics: `forcing` (Forced only), `ledger` (the judge a field; reads its ties on request), `census` (its tactics as `tactic` facts); planning: `keep`, `density`.
             Each wraps the function the engine has always called, unchanged.
  controller cs_decision `Fixed` = the order of 78.5-78.8 (proof, ledger, density over the ledger's ties); `decide_with` is now a call of `decide_params` and keeps its signature.
  batch      cs_decision::batch + `cs_engine.solve_batch(positions, ...)`: one call, a rayon pool, the Python lock released, one summary per position in order, a panic or a bad
             position is its own error row; every decision's steps appended to a JSON Lines log tagged with the SNAPSHOT id the caller names.
WHAT CHANGED THAT IS NOT A WRAPPER: the density prior reports the nodes its census readings spend (the old decision's node count left them out; `Choice.nodes` now counts them).
NOT DONE (the document's remaining distance): a store SNAPSHOT (the id is the caller's label; the store is still read at init), a columnar log (the JSON Lines schema is flat; a
Parquet conversion belongs to the harness), the training-only flag on the teacher, a router or gate and its training, subgoal proposals with modes beyond Forced, MCTS as an operator.
TESTS: rust/engine/decision/tests/equivalence.rs (the 78.11 decision kept as the oracle: same move, same proved flag, same trace on depth-capped runs, prior off / on / valuation
judge), interface.rs (modes refused, the missing operator, the step fuse, batch order and panic), tests/test_plan78_12.py (the Python entry, the log, threads, the lock), and the
generic test of 78.1 over the new sources. The three cs_game certificates were stale only through Cargo.lock (new crates); re-run by co-play, 0 disagreements.

#### 78.13 COSTS IN PARTS, THE TEACHER'S FLAG, THE FACT LAYER (2026-11-06; Kaveh: "costs should be recorded with granularity", "go on all 3 ... stay generic as much as possible, but stay correct, and complete, and modular")
COSTS IN PARTS: `Outcome.parts` -- what each deepening step of the proof and of the ledger search, each defect level of the census, each candidate the density prior read, each phase of the
lemma operator spent, as measured (nodes and seconds); the parts add up to the call's total (tested for the proof, the ledger and the census). The batch log carries them, with each step's
principal line and ledger events.
THE TEACHER'S FLAG: `cs_learn::watch::Teacher` has `training_only` (true unless an implementor says otherwise; `watch` refuses one that does), and no crate of the decision path (operator,
tactics, planning, memory, decision) depends on the learning crate or names a teacher -- tests/test_plan78_14.py reads the manifests and the sources. What a teacher touched is recorded on the
lemma (`meta.teacher`) and on the snapshot (`teacher_used`): every result can be reported with and without it.
THE FACT LAYER (the architecture document's "ground facts and derived predicates"): `Game::base_facts` (the state as ground facts), a `Vocabulary` per game (the derived relations that belong to
the layer, the relations a move's effect is read in, how a state holds its units), `FactView` (a description evaluated over base facts: base plus derived), and `GdlGame` now declares units from
its vocabulary, so the ledger, census and lemma layers run on any GDL game. The chess kernels' conversion to the description's fluents is certified by co-play like the rest (chess, king of the
hill, three-check; certify::coplay compares the facts at every state).
FOUND by that certificate: the first conversion of three-check counted a check when it is given; the description counts it one state later ("counted into the next state"). Fixed in the
conversion, not in the description.
OBS facts co-play (rust/engine/game/tests/facts.rs, 6 seeded games each): chess 2115 states, 2109 with facts compared, 0 disagreements; king of the hill 1207 / 1201 / 0; three-check 497 / 491 / 0; the
  control (the three-check kernel against plain chess's description) disagrees. The three kernel certificates re-run: chess 6431, king of the hill 4014, three-check 1833 positions, 0 disagreements.
ANOTHER GAME: a six-line description of a game that is not chess (a row of pieces that step or take) declares its units and its vocabulary and runs through the same facts, cards and lemma operator
(rust/engine/decision/tests/lemmas.rs): the layers name no game.

#### 78.14 THE MEMORY LAYER: SNAPSHOTS, THE LEMMA LANGUAGE, ONE MATCHER, THE LEMMA OPERATOR (2026-11-06)
cs_memory (new crate; game-free). A SNAPSHOT is an immutable store state for one game -- its vocabulary, its judge (copied from the legacy store's valuation entry in use), its lemmas, its parent --
named by the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its bytes; the engine refuses a file that does not hash to its name, a batch logs the id of the snapshot it read, and the Python publisher
(discovery/game_store.py) writes a new one only when the content changes (the chain: HEAD, parent). The LEMMA LANGUAGE is restricted Datalog over the game's fact vocabulary: a body of positive
literals (and negated ones with their variables bound), a response (the facts a move removes and adds), in the mover's perspective (`us`, `them`) so one lemma serves both colours. ONE MATCHER binds
a body to facts (most constrained literal first, a binding limit, a step fuse); the operator and the verification both use it, so a lemma means the same in both. The LEMMA OPERATOR answers the new
goal `Respond`: it proposes the moves a snapshot's lemmas name, and the fixed controller hands them to the ledger search as `prefer`, read first. A PRIOR, never a verdict: the value the search finds
does not depend on the order (tested: 18 comparisons identical), and a wrong lemma costs reading time and nothing else (AGENTS.md rule 7).
THE CLAIM A LEMMA MAKES, AND HOW IT IS CHECKED: "if the body holds, an optimal move of the response's kind exists". Checked on CARDS: a position's facts and, for every legal move, its effect and its exact value
at a stated depth (the plain minimax of the judge -- no null-move pruning or reductions, which are not exact -- or the card says its reading was cut), with the units each side loses along its best line.
The evaluation reports fires, holds, refutations, the independent games they came from, the precision, the precision a random choice of as many moves would reach (`expected`), the excess over it, and the
share of the legal moves the response matches (`selectivity`): the gates against a lemma that is true but trivial. Status SAMPLED -- exact on a sample, not proved (Lean stays the source of truth).
The learned lemmas live in rules/learned/<game>/ (a person reads them; rules/learned/README.md); the legacy lemma store (chess words, Lean-cited) is untouched and still the valuation's home.
OBS (rust/engine/decision/tests/lemmas.rs): the hand-written "take the attacker" lemma proposes exactly the capture, from either side; on 4 cards it fires 3, holds 2, refuted 1.

#### 78.15 THE WAKE AND THE SLEEP: THE SURPRISE LOOP ON THE NEW ENGINE (2026-11-06)
wake.py: self-play in lockstep, every ply the running games decided in ONE batch call, every decision a labelled row of the trace log (its steps, goals, evidence, cost in parts, the snapshot read), games
ended by the outcome, the threefold repetition or the ply cap. sleep.py (the document's surprise loop; Python orchestrates, the engine reads): (1) DETECT a surprise -- the second side sees a loss of the
first side's units along its best line that the first side's best line did not foresee (read from the ledger events in the log; a proved win counts); (2) REPLAY the position as a card and CONFIRM the
loss at an exact depth that can reach it (the plies the second side read, plus one -- the funnel counts the replayable ones: a loss one ply past what a replay can reach is a horizon effect it cannot
reproduce), and take the SAVING moves (they lose fewer units and are optimal); (3) EXPLAIN: the saving move's effect, with the facts around it and around where the loss happens, is a ground seed;
(4) ABSTRACT (abstraction.py): the climb of single LIFTS (a constant to a variable everywhere) and DROPS (a body literal), every step read by the engine on the development games' cards and taken only if
the lemma stays admissible (precision, excess over chance, selectivity, no cut reading) and fires on at least as many cards -- lifts before drops, so the body keeps the literals that exclude the cases the
claim is false on; (5) VERIFY on the held-out games' cards (games the seed and the climb never saw): the same gates and enough firings in enough independent games; only then is a lemma stored; (6) PUBLISH.
The funnel and every rejection are reported. The climb was found correct on a planted motif in real positions (a pawn attacked by a pawn it can take, with decoys): every file, rank and kind became a
variable, the attack literal stayed (it is what excludes a rook that can take a defended pawn), and the lemma held at precision 1.0 on 10 held-out positions in 10 games. Over-generalization is caught
by exact counterexamples (a pawn on the fifth rank beside the black king: taking is not best, a quiet pawn move is).
RESULTS (2026-11-06; scripts/printed OBS lines, JOURNAL): the machinery is complete and correct on a planted motif; on real self-play NO lemma has yet survived the held-out gates. The funnel, self-play at 0.01 s a move
(about depth 4), replay depth 5, dev / held-out split of the GAMES:
  24 games:  decisions 1105, surprises 240, replayable 179, confirmed 94, with saving moves 26, seeds 55, climbed 41, supported on dev 8, verified on held-out 0.
  96 games:  decisions 4210, surprises 895, replayable 669, confirmed 256, with saving moves 77, seeds 150 (60 read), climbed 33, supported on dev 8, verified on held-out 0 (1306 s).
Every one of the 8 that reached the held-out stage had precision 1.0 on 3 to 11 development firings and failed there (precision 0.0 to 0.75; the excess over chance below 0.2 for six of the eight): small-sample
overfitting, caught by the games the climb never saw. That is the gate working, not a bug, and it says where the work is: (a) more data per lemma (the dev gate at 3 firings is too soft: a lower
confidence bound on the precision, not the point estimate, should gate a seed); (b) a richer language (the body has no negation yet in what it mines: "undefended" needs it); (c) better surprises --
a self-play engine at depth 4 loses material to horizon effects, which may often have no local pattern (not tested); human games or a stronger opponent may give tactics worth learning. The cost is
in the exact cards (depth 5 over every legal move) and the climbs; how the 1306 s of the 96-game sleep divide between them is not yet measured.
CREDIT BY REMOVAL is written (sleep.credit: each lemma left out in turn, the same positions decided again; on the positions it fired on, how often the decision changed and the depth and nodes with and without,
with the standard error) but has not yet been run on a lemma found in play -- there is none; on the hand-written capture lemma over 6 firing positions the depth is the same with and without it (those pawn
endings are read to their end either way).
NOT DONE: mining negated literals; a
statistical gate on the development precision; the Python wake / sleep for GDL games other than the kernels' (the Rust stack runs on any `Game`: tested on a second game; the Python glue builds
games by variant name); Monte Carlo tree search as an operator; a trained router.

judge), so "optimal" in the claim was by a judge the sleep never named; (2) the development gate was a point estimate (3 clean firings), and the climb selects among many
candidates on the same development cards -- the eight lemmas that failed held-out had passed it on 3-11 firings; (3) the seed cap took the first 60 seeds by game order;
(4) a seed found inadmissible was reported without its figures, and the time of a sleep was not split by phase.
