#### 78.17 THE TWO TOOL KITS: THE KIT IN THE TYPE, THE ESTIMATE, THE SELF-DIAGNOSIS, THE SLEEP THAT CHOOSES ITS TOOLS (2026-11-08; Kaveh: "the engine has multiple tools available to it,
and it should use those tools intelligently in order to be able to assess the position at hand, when training. At inference time (analysis or playing), it only has access to lemmas and MCTS,
not past game data"; built by three Sonnet agents under the rules: generic, modular, unit-test the pieces, record the structure, prefer lightweight off-the-shelf parts)
THE PRINCIPLE: two kits. INFERENCE reads the snapshot (lemmas, the distilled valuation) and searches over the rules (the proof, the ledger, Monte Carlo tree search). TRAINING (the sleep) may also ask
a teacher, past game data and deeper search -- chosen by what the engine's own log says it lacks, at a measured cost -- and stores the explanation (a lemma), never the oracle.
BUILT: (1) `cs_operator::Kit { Inference, Training }` is a property of every Operator (`kit()`, default Inference); `drive` = `drive_in(Kit::Inference, ..)`: an inference drive does not run a training
operator -- the step records Unsupported and says why; a training drive runs both. `Step.kit` says who answered. (2) cs_learn (the training kit): `Advisor` (an outside source's ordering of the legal
moves with scores of unknown scale), `TeacherOp` (Kit::Training, answers the new `Goal::Advise`), `ScriptedAdvisor` for tests; no decision-path crate depends on cs_learn (the 78.13 test still reads the
manifests). (3) `cs_planning::mcts`: UCT over the Game trait, multi-role, a pluggable `Rollout` (Uniform by default, the game crate's seeded RNG), budget-bounded with parts per 64 playouts, answering
the new `Goal::Estimate` -- an estimate, never a proof; `cs_engine.estimate` exposes it. (4) `cs_decision::Params.ties`: the ledger's ties read WITHOUT the prior (the ledger keeps `ledger_share` of
the clock), so the tie rate is measurable; `solve_batch(ties=)`, `wake --ties`. (5) discovery/diagnose.py: the engine's self-diagnosis over its own log -- the tie rate, surprises by kind, Gap share,
cost by operator and part, the depth distribution. (6) sleep.py: RANK SOURCES of one shape (`rank(variant, moves) -> [(move, score)]`): `UciTeacher.rank` (python-chess MultiPV; training-only) and
`EstimateSource` (the engine's own MCTS; inference kit, so nothing it touches is flagged as taught); the SECOND KIND OF SURPRISE (`disagreement`: rank-based, scale-free -- the source's top move
is below our best, or none of our optimal moves is in its top k), confirmed only when OUR exact replay two plies deeper finds the source's move optimal, then seeded like any other; tie-BREAKING
among the judge-tied saving moves by the source (`break_ties`); and `plan_tools`: the sleep reads the diagnosis and turns the source on when the judge ties often or the wake never read ties.
Held-out verification is untouched by any source: exact, by our judge, on cards no source saw. Provenance: `meta.teacher` only for a training-only source, `meta.source` always.
OBS the engine's own diagnosis (tests/test_plan78_18.py, 4 games at 0.02 s with --ties): tie rate 0.5, mean 4.6 moves as good as the best where ties were read. The 78.16 log (m48) never read ties: the chooser
  calls the coarseness unknown and turns the source on.
OBS the estimate (cs_engine.estimate): the scholar's-mate position, 0.3 s: h5f7 most visited, value 9279 of 10000 for the mover, 20803 playouts (2605 cut), 589056 nodes.
OBS THE CONTROLLED COMPARISON, the same 48-game log, judge material (mined), cards at depth 5 (the 78.16 baseline: 1 lemma verified; climbs 391 s / cards 113 s measured here):
  teacher (Stockfish, 50 ms MultiPV): 200 positions ranked, 25 disagreements, 5 confirmed by the deeper exact replay (20 not), seeds 36, climbed 30, supported 3, verified 1 -- the SAME lemma as the baseline
    (cell-response-0265aee4, now flagged teacher because the teacher ordered its tie); the five teacher seeds all fell for support. 565 s.
  estimate (MCTS 0.2 s): 200 ranked, 110 disagreements, 4 confirmed (106 not: a sampled estimate at 0.2 s disagrees with the exact depth-5 reading more often than not), seeds 35, climbed 31, supported 1,
    verified 0 -- the baseline's seed was DISPLACED: in break mode the estimate ordered three other tied saving moves ahead of b4b5 and the cap of three cut it. 760 s.
FOUND AND FIXED: a source that breaks ties can order the engine's own first choice out of the seeds; break mode now keeps it among them (sleep.py).
WHERE THE TIME GOES (now measured): the climbs (391-483 s) dominate the cards (110-113 s); verification is negligible.
READING: on this data neither source added a verified lemma; the teacher's disagreements are few and mostly unconfirmable at depth 7 (horizon or positional), the estimate's are mostly noise. The honest value
of 78.17 is the loop closing -- the engine measures its own coarseness, chooses a source, and every source's touch is recorded and reversible -- not a gain in lemmas yet.
NOT DONE: a rank source stronger than 0.2 s of uniform playouts (a Rollout from the ledger or a lemma prior); the training-time controller in Rust over `Operator`s of both kits (the Python `plan_tools`
is its first, one-rule form); the climb's cost; negated literals; the second game's Python glue.

#### 78.18 THE STRONGER RANK SOURCE: INFORMED PLAYOUTS AND A LEAF VALUATION AS PLUGGABLE PIECES (2026-11-08; Kaveh: "continue building the stronger rank source")
WHY: 78.17 measured that 0.2 s of UNIFORM playouts scored at the game's end is a noisy judge (110 disagreements, 4 confirmed). Random play in a game with units is nearly noise: a playout gives
away what it holds, and a playout cut at its cap scores a draw whatever stands on the board. Two cheap, generic remedies, each a small trait so other policies can plug in beside them.
BUILT (one Sonnet agent, Rust; integration here): (1) `Judge::worth(kind)` -- the plain worth of a unit kind (Count: 1; Worth: its table). (2) `cs_planning::rollout`: `Leaf` (the value per role of a
NON-terminal state where a playout is cut): `Draw` (as before) and `Balance<J>` (each role's worth balance squashed by a logistic with a `scale` in worth units; 0 is exactly 50); `Greedy<J>` (epsilon-
greedy over a move's immediate gain: captured worth plus a change of kind; uniform when nothing gains); `Prior` (weights over the legal moves) with `Weighted<P>` sampling proportional to weight plus a
floor, and `GainPrior<J>` (weight exp(gain / temperature)); `search` takes a `leaf`; `MctsOp::with_policy(.., rollout, leaf)`; the evidence line names both. (3) `cs_decision::LemmaPrior`: a snapshot's
bound lemmas as a `Prior` (boost for the moves a bound lemma's response matches), matched exactly as LemmaOp does. (4) `cs_engine.estimate(.., rollout=uniform|greedy|gain|lemma, leaf=draw|balance,
eps, scale, temperature, store, prior, floor, spec, boost)`: the store's judge record builds the balance leaf's Worth. (5) sleep.py: `source_of("mcts:<rollout>/<leaf>")` names a policy; EstimateSource
forwards the options and names itself `mcts:<rollout>/<leaf>`; `--source mcts:greedy/balance`. (6) discovery/rank_bench.py: a rank source's AGREEMENT with a reference (a teacher: a measurement, training
only) on positions sampled from a wake log spread over its games -- top-1, top-3, the reference's best move's rank in the source's order -- and a MATCH of two rank sources (the first move of each
ranking; the game's own outcome, the record's draw, the ply cap). Tests: planning/tests/rollout.rs (12), decision/tests/lemma_prior.rs (2), tests/test_plan78_19.py (5, integration).
OBS the scholar's-mate position, 0.3 s: uniform/draw h5f7 value 9338, 22970 playouts; greedy/balance (material (mined), scale 3) h5f7 9909, 207987 playouts (952 cut: greedy play ends games fast);
  gain/balance h5f7 9047, 14403 playouts.
OBS RANK AGREEMENT with Stockfish (300 ms) on 60 positions of the 48-game log (one of each game in turn), each source 0.2 s a position (rank_bench_chess_m48_agree.out):
  uniform (78.17's source):  top1 0.033, top3 0.133, mean rank of the reference's best 14.1 (median 13)
  uniform + balance leaf:    top1 0.067, top3 0.183, mean rank 14.4 (median 15)         -- the leaf alone does little
  greedy + draw:             top1 0.100, top3 0.217, mean rank 13.3 (median 12)         -- the greedy rollout alone helps
  greedy + balance:          top1 0.100, top3 0.167, mean rank 11.8 (median 9)
  gain + balance:            top1 0.100, top3 0.267, mean rank 11.6 (median 9)          -- the best of the six: the reference's move moves up from 14th to 9th in the median
  lemma + balance:           top1 0.033, top3 0.150, mean rank 14.1 (median 12), 0.355 s a position -- no better than uniform: see the cost below
  For context the ledger search's own choice (cs_engine.best_move, 0.2 s) agrees top-1 on 0.217 of the same positions (material (mined) and count alike): the estimate is still the weaker judge.
OBS THE LEMMA PRIOR'S COST: the prior derives the position's facts (the variant's description evaluated as a fact view) at EVERY playout ply: 196 nodes and 1 playout in 0.3 s, 512 nodes and 2 playouts
  in 1.0 s, against 527511 nodes and 11141 playouts for uniform in 0.3 s -- about a thousand times a uniform ply. At that price a lemma prior belongs at the TREE's nodes (once per expansion, a PUCT prior)
  or behind a cache by state key, not in the playouts; as a rank source it is wired, named and measured, and not yet useful. On the lemma's own seed position (m48_c0:10:38) it ranked b4a5 first and the
  lemma's b4b5 third (uniform: 7th) -- from two playouts, which is no evidence.
OBS THE MATCH, greedy + balance against uniform (no store: every unit counts one, scale 3), 0.2 s a move, 20 games with 4 random opening plies, colours alternating (rank_bench_chess_match_gb_u.out):
  score 0.850 (se 0.072), W16 D2 L2, 90 plies a game, 1 unfinished at the 160-ply cap -- as a PLAYER the informed estimate is far stronger than the uniform one at the same clock, though as a judge of
  Stockfish's choice the gain is modest: it plays sound captures and keeps its material, which is most of what beats random playouts; agreeing with a strong engine's move is another matter.
READING: informed playouts give a real but modest gain in agreement (median rank 13 -> 9 at 0.2 s) for the same clock; the estimate remains weaker than the exact ledger search at that clock (top-1 0.10 vs
0.22), which is the point of keeping it a SECOND source. The cheap pieces (gain, greedy, balance) are the ones to use; the lemma prior needs a faster fact view first.
NOT DONE: the lemma prior at the tree's nodes (PUCT) with a fact cache; the match of the policies at equal clock over more games; the stronger source inside sleep on the 48-game log (the 78.17 comparison
re-run with `--source mcts:gain/balance`); a learned prior as a `Prior`.

#### 78.19 PLAN: THE FAST FACT LAYER -- DEMAND, CERTIFIED READERS, THE EVENT STREAM (salvaged from plans 39-77), AND THE HUMAN GAMES AS A TRAINING SOURCE (2026-11-08; Kaveh: "these are the
efficiencies you need to build in ... salvage what we had from before ... design it properly and then adapt what we've built to it ... the pitfalls we found before are directly applicable")
A PLAN, NOT BUILT. Written from two read-only surveys of the docs (plans 39-77, the journal) and the code (rust/analyst_core, discovery/*.py, rust/engine).
THE COST, MEASURED (this session): `cs_engine.facts` on a chess position 3.21 ms for 134 facts (103 of them `attack`); the kernel's own replay-and-legal-moves 0.005 ms. The description has 114 rules
over 49 relations; the vocabulary derives ONE (`attack`, over `cell` deltas). `FactView::facts` runs `Program::run`, which (i) clones every static relation into a fresh Db, (ii) evaluates EVERY
stratum that reads input -- candidates, the legality machinery (`vacates`/`fills`/`after`/`king_ray`/`exposed`, per candidate per cell), `legal`, mate/draw/terminal/goal, `next.*` -- to read
`attack`, (iii) parses every base fact from a string and renders every row back to one, then sorts. The lemma prior then also diffs string fact sets per legal move. Hence 196 nodes in 0.3 s (78.18).
WHAT WAS BUILT BEFORE AND WHAT IT TAUGHT (the survey; J = JOURNAL.md, AP = this file):
  built: footprint memos (J 21423), the incremental ledger in the goal search (200 s -> 78 s, J 21950), the FactStore with justifications and stale flags (52.19, discovery/facts.py), read sets and
  listeners (39.5-39.6), the event loop (40, analyst_core/agenda.rs), the diff that decides what is re-asked (52.12-13, Pos.push/diff; 72.10 `move_diff`, Lean Ideas.Frame.chess_neglect), the
  incremental static exchange `exchange_affected` / `threats_arr_inc` with an equality audit of 175,502 moves (J 28818; Lean PathLemma / FrameLemma / ExchangeLocal), the demand-driven tabled prover with
  CERTIFIED relations read from bitboards (76.4b, analyst_core/regression.rs + gdl_chess.rs; Lean attackBy_iff / legal_iff), gdl.py's `wanted` (compute only what is needed; the Rust `run` lost it),
  and the incremental-maintenance spike 77.0 (DBSP: signed change sets, delta rules compiled at load, two streams SLOW and FAST) -- planned, deferred, never created.
  paid: EXACT incremental maintenance of cheap LOCAL relations (the exchange index; "the static index is where incremental reuse pays, and it is exact", J 28910); demand (the prover's cone); certified
  native readers (mate 0.692 -> 0.054 ms, AP 4176); interning and fixed arrays (65.7 -> 38.5 s, J 28821-28828).
  did not pay: reusing DEEP results across moves ("structurally vacuous on a chessboard", J 28910; zone reuse 0.0 a move); approximate footprints (stale on 4.0 % then 1.0 % of statuses, six missed
  tactics -- recompute by default, J 28196); global memos flooded by scratch positions (J 21921); schema claims served across positions ("not portable, full stop", J 31975); ported machinery that
  measured nothing (B3 cache, J 31965; scheduler/route reader, J 32018); Ascent inside the hot loop (J 27993) and Ascent at all for a description loaded at run time (AP 4169).
  the rules we broke and must not again (docs/BUGS.md class 1, key soundness): a key that does not record something the computation read -- the empty dependency (13 of 540 decisions changed, J 28950),
  the stale halfmove clock in a cached FEN (J 31966), `Pos.diff` comparing attacker COUNTS so a swap was missed (AP 3632), the word cache that must replay its read set on a hit (RUST_BOUNDARY.md 185).
  the process rule: every incremental path ships with its ORACLE (the full evaluation), an OFF switch, an equality audit that prints its counts, and a negative control (dropping the semi-naive rounds once
  gave 57,238 disagreements, J 35334 -- the harness is what found it).
THE DESIGN. The fact layer becomes a STREAM: a line of play (the game's slow stream; the search's fast stream of make/unmake) emits SIGNED DELTAS of base facts; derived facts are MAINTAINED, not
recomputed; lemma matching is TRIGGERED by the deltas it reads. Generic: everything is derived from the description's rules and the Game trait; a game's fast binding may answer a relation natively
only under a certificate. Each stage is exact against the stage before it, measured, and switchable off. The target: facts of a child state at the cost of the kernel's move (microseconds), so a
lemma prior at every tree node is affordable and LemmaOp's "facts" part vanishes from the decision's clock.
  STAGE A -- DEMAND AND NO STRINGS (cs_gdl, FactView; exact by construction; the gdl.py `needed` and the 76.4b interning salvaged):
    A1 `Program::run_for(wanted: &[Rel])`: only the strata in the wanted relations' dependency cone (chess: attack <- attack_by <- slide / empty / occupied + statics: a handful of the 114 rules).
    A2 statics shared (a Db layered over the program's static relations, never cloned per run).
    A3 interned rows end to end: `Game::base_rows` or a string -> term memo in the view; cs_memory's FactIndex / bindings / delta / perspective over `T` rows (perspective = a role swap on ids); strings
       only at the JSON boundary (cards, lemma files). A4 the evaluator's quadratic corners (index cleared on every add, Vec::contains dedup, cloned lookups).
    oracle: `run` == `run_for` on every position and every child of the m48 log; the view's facts before == after on the same (an audit binary that prints counts). Expected: a large cut; unknown until measured.
  STAGE B -- CERTIFIED NATIVE READERS (the 76.4b `Certified` kind salvaged into the Game trait): `Game::derived(s, relation) -> Option<Vec<Row>>`: a fast binding may answer a vocabulary relation
    itself (chess kernel: `attack` from its attack maps); FactView reads it ONLY while the relation holds a CERTIFICATE from co-play (certify.rs extended: on every position of the co-play games the native
    rows equal the description's; a disagreement demotes the relation to the evaluator -- the existing demotion rule, AP 4345). Game-free: the hook is generic, the certificate is the check.
  STAGE C -- THE EVENT STREAM (the FAST stream of 77.0; `exchange_affected`, `move_diff`, the FactStore's stale flags and frame restore salvaged, made generic):
    C1 `Game::delta(s, m) -> (removed, added)` base facts (default: the diff of `base_facts`; a kernel overrides it from the move alone -- 72.10's `move_diff` is the chess instance). Signed: undo is the negation.
    C2 `FactMemory` carried along a search path: the node's facts as interned rows with SUPPORT COUNTS per derived row; a delta is pushed through DELTA RULES compiled from the description at load (for each
       rule and each body literal: join that literal's delta against the rest -- semi-naive over signed deltas; deletions by counting in non-recursive strata, DRed-style re-derivation for the recursive ones,
       bounded to the rows reachable from the touched terms). Locality falls out of the rules (a `slide` row that reads no touched cell is untouched: the Lean frame lemmas' content, derived not hand-coded).
       `pop` restores by the negated delta (the FactStore's `restore`). No global memo: the memory lives on the path (the flooding lesson). Keys include the mover and the clocks (class 1).
    C3 the TRIGGER: lemmas indexed by the relations and constants of their bodies; a delta re-matches only the lemmas it meets, a bound lemma keeps its binding until a fact it read is removed (the
       Listener / Rete-lite reading of 39.6, kept to one index). The same event stream feeds LemmaOp in a decision and the lemma prior in the tree.
    oracle: at every node in audit mode the memory's facts == the full evaluation's (`INC_OFF`, counts printed); a negative control (a corrupted delta must break the equality).
  STAGE D -- WHERE THE FACTS ARE USED: the lemma prior moves from the playouts to the TREE (PUCT: the prior's weight per child enters the selection term; computed once per expansion from the node's
    FactMemory); playouts stay cheap (gain / greedy + balance, 78.18). LemmaOp in a decision reads the same memory. Measured by rank_bench (agreement, match) and by the 78.17 sleep comparison re-run.
  STAGE E -- THE HUMAN GAMES AS A TRAINING SOURCE (Kaveh, this session: "in the beginning, if it doesn't know what to do, it should query the human games ... during training ... that should allow it
    to learn some lemmas"): `HumanSource` of the rank-source shape (`rank(variant, moves) -> [(move, score)]`, score = how often humans played it, with the outcomes behind it), TRAINING ONLY
    (`training_only = True`, source "human"; Kit::Training), read from an index over data/records (19,354,162 lichess games kept, 200,000 a shard; the valuation of 78.4 is already mined from them):
    position key -> {move: count, outcomes}, built once a shard (generic: any game with records and a state key), queried at the position after `moves`. Its uses in sleep: `plan_tools` turns it on
    FIRST when the diagnosis says the judge is coarse ("does not know what to do": the tie rate), before the teacher; `break_ties` by human frequency; `disagreement` surprises where humans strongly
    prefer a move our judge does not rank, confirmed by our exact deeper replay and then seeded like any other -- the lemma is the explanation of why the humans' move is better, and it is what enters the
    store; the raw frequencies never do (the inference kit sees lemmas and distilled records only). Outcome frequencies are the "probabilities without understanding" of 78.17, kept as training evidence.
    Independent of A-D (Python, beside UciTeacher and EstimateSource): can be built first.
WHAT TO SALVAGE, WHERE: gdl.py `Program.needed/run(wanted)` (discovery/gdl.py:515-535) -> A1; analyst_core/regression.rs `Spec::new(.., certified)` / `Kind::Certified` and gdl_chess.rs `certified()`
  -> B; regress.py `move_diff` + Lean Ideas.Frame.chess_neglect and rules.rs `touched_by` / `exchange_affected` + Lean PathLemma/FrameLemma -> C1's chess override and C2's exactness argument;
  discovery/facts.py FactStore (`invalidate`, `restore`, the inverted read index) -> C2/C3's shape; analyst_core/agenda.rs `Event -> Condition -> question` -> C3's trigger; rules.rs `threats_inc_audit`
  and tests/test_plan72_10.py -> the audit harness's form; docs/BUGS.md class 1 -> the key rule. NOT salvaged: the Ascent program (compile-time, chess-only, dead), ReasoningLedger's quadratic retract,
  schema-claim portability, approximate footprints.
ORDER AND MEASURE: E and A in parallel (E is Python and independent; A is the certain win); then B (chess only needs the hook + certificate); C only if A+B leave derivation dominant at the tree's nodes
  (77.0's own rule: "only if Rust derivation then dominates is per-node recomputation the cost and the sub-project the answer"); D as soon as A makes a per-node prior affordable. Every stage prints
  OBS facts/ms and the audit's equal/unequal counts on the m48 positions before the next starts.

#### 78.20 THE TYPED FACT GRAPH AND A GRAPH-NET PRIOR -- the cheap test (2026-11-09; Kaveh: pieces, facts, proven facts, conjectures and probabilities as typed nodes with supports / refutes /
derived-from edges, "and then a graph neural network on top of all of this to become my policy whenever I need a policy ... if I add a new node with new information my policy will take it into
account, as opposed to having it as text context for an LLM"; answer: yes as the shared representation and as a PRIOR at expansions, never as a claim -- the lemmas stay the explanation)
THE GRAPH (discovery/fact_graph.py, generic -- tokens, not game names): `graph_of(facts, moves, vocabulary, bindings=None) -> HeteroData`. Node types `term` (one per constant), `fact` (one per
  row; relation token, kind ground / derived by the vocabulary, `present`), `move` (one per legal move; targets y / opt / lost when a card gives them), `claim` (lemma bindings / conjectures with
  a probability; the type exists and takes `bindings`, nothing supplies them yet). Edge types `(fact, arg_i, term)` per argument position, `(move, removes|adds, fact)` (an added row not in the
  position becomes a fact node with present 0), `(claim, binds, fact)`, and the reverses. Token vocabularies (UNK = 0) are learned from the corpus and saved with the model: a new INSTANCE of a
  known kind enters the graph and is read; a new KIND gets UNK until retrained (the honest limit of "add a node and the policy takes it into account"). `graph_hash` is a Weisfeiler-Lehman hash of
  the term/fact graph (3 rounds; permutation-invariant, sensitive to one changed fact): the abstraction key 78.19's reading (ii) asked for, the same object serving the net, the lemma matcher
  (a body is a subgraph pattern), the human index and the event stream.
THE NET (discovery/graph_prior.py, torch_geometric): `GraphNet` 3 layers x 64, HeteroConv of SAGEConv per edge type with residual + LayerNorm, an MLP head on the move nodes; loss = cross-entropy of
  the softmax over a position's moves against the uniform distribution over the OPTIMAL set (value == max by the judge at the card's depth). `train(cards_path, out_path, epochs, seed)`; CLI
  `graph_prior build-cards <game> --log --depth --stride --max-cards --judge --out` (sleep's corpus construction; even subsampling) and `train`. Trained in the TRAINING kit (cards, so the judge's
  exact depth-5 values are the labels; a teacher or the human games could label as well). `GraphSource` (source "gnn", training_only False: a prior of the inference kit -- it ranks, it claims
  nothing): facts via cs_engine.facts, each move's removed / added rows as the child-minus-parent difference over the delta relations with the child's perspective swapped back (tested equal to
  build_cards' rows on 5 positions, 100+ moves). `source_of("gnn[:<model>]")` in sleep and rank_bench; default model paths.derived("graph_prior_<game>.pt") (local). Tests: tests/test_plan78_20.py (7).
OBS gnn build-cards chess: 3714 cards from 3714 positions, depth 5, judge material (mined), 215 s (the m48 log, stride 1).
OBS gnn corpus: cards 3714, dev 2139, held 1575 (split by game), terms 37, relations 9, graph seconds 3.0.
OBS gnn baselines held (1575 cards, 1535 contested): uniform 0.4213, fewest lost 0.6810 (fewest lost reads the card's depth-5 `lost`: an oracle the inference kit cannot compute cheaply).
OBS gnn epoch 30: loss 2.9604, held top1 0.4876 (contested 0.4743), 101 s; a 100-epoch run (scratch, not the default model): held top1 0.5238 at epoch 100, loss 2.68, 335 s; held top1 swings ~0.03
  between epochs (small sets: read as directional).
OBS gnn GraphSource.rank: 40 positions, 24.8 ms a position (dominated by one cs_engine.facts call per legal move, not by the net).
OBS RANK AGREEMENT with Stockfish (300 ms) on 60 positions of the d1 log (96 games; NOT the training log), rank_bench_chess_d1_agree.out and rank_bench_chess_d1_gnn_agree.out:
  source          top1   top3   mean rank  median   s a position
  uniform         0.100  0.217  11.72      10       0.200
  gain+balance    0.067  0.233  13.02      11       0.200
  gnn (30 epochs) 0.133  0.383  10.75       8       0.022

READING: the net learned from 2139 cards of 24 games and, with no search at all, ranks the engine's optimal move and Stockfish's move better than 0.2 s of Monte Carlo search with the informed
  playouts, at a tenth of the cost -- top3 0.383 against 0.233 is the figure to read (60 positions: top1 differences of 0.03 are noise). It is far below the fewest-lost oracle on the cards, so
  the labels hold much more than it has learned; more games (the wake logs accumulate; the human games label the opening) and the claim nodes are the next inputs. The 24.8 ms is the fact
  layer again (one facts call per child): the event stream (78.19 C) or a kernel delta (`Game::changed`) cuts it to one call. DONE as the cheap test; its two uses now: (1) `--source gnn` is a
  rank source for sleep's tie-breaking and surprises like any other, (2) a per-expansion PUCT prior in the tree (78.19 D) once the per-position cost is a millisecond. Not done: claim nodes

#### 78.21 THE CONCEPT VOCABULARY AND THE GRAPH PRIOR IN RUST -- one test (2026-11-09; Kaveh: "the constants are the constants"; a dedicated chess wrapper is fine "so that vocabulary stays constant
and truly interpretable"; "the richer vocabulary will help. Take it to Rust and then test it in Rust. Let's do one test only."; and "there's a lot of this built from before, so be sure to take a look")
WHAT THE SURVEY OF PRIOR WORK CHANGED: the ontology shelf already names the sorts and the `square` product sort [file, rank]; the GDL Program already carries sorts and signatures; the S0 analyst
  (relations.py / structure.py / geometry.py / concepts.py) already defines the human concepts and serves as an oracle; rust/analyst_core/src/threat.rs `Policy` is the house way to carry a small net
  into Rust (JSON weights, hand-written forward); earlier graph nets measured that attack and move-mutation edges pay and that concept tokens did not on 5-man endgames. So: sorts and objects are read
  from the description (not learned from the corpus), concepts are RULES (data), weights travel as JSON, no ONNX runtime.
THE CONCEPTS (rules/concepts/chess.gdl, an additive delta composed onto each variant's description; the only chess-specific piece, and it is data): sort `diagonal` (26 constants named by their end
  squares) with `diagonal_of file rank diagonal`; `defended`, `hanging`, `pinned`, `fork`, `open_file`, `half_open_file`, `passed_pawn`, `isolated_pawn`, `doubled_pawn`, `absent side kind` ("there are
  no bishops on the board" as a fact row), `bishop_pair`. Not built: battery, xray, discovered attack, skewer. rules/learned/chess/graph_vocabulary.json names what a graph reader sees (state / derived
  / static relations, `objects` {square: [file, rank]}, `scales` [clock], the `concepts` delta, the variants); game_store.graph_vocabulary / graph_spec_texts read it. The lemma vocabulary
  (vocabulary.json) is unchanged: the lemma language does not see the concepts yet.
THE GRAPH v2 (rust/engine/decision/src/graph.rs, generic: it names no game object and is tested on a made-up game): `GraphSpec::new(description, graph vocabulary)`, `.graph(g, s)`. Term nodes are
  TYPED BY SORT (`square:e4`, `kind:bishop`, `diagonal:a1h8`) and ALWAYS PRESENT (every member of every sort in use, except the `scales` sorts); product sorts are fused from consecutive signature
  slots into one object node with `part<i>` edges to its components; fact nodes for state / derived / static rows (kind 0 / 1 / 2; statics built once and shared); move nodes with removes / adds
  edges; the claim type stays empty. The vocabularies are constant for a description, saved in the weights file and validated at load.
THE NET IN RUST (graph_net.rs, graph_prior.rs): `GraphNet::load / validate / forward` is the torch GraphNet's forward in plain loops over row-major f32 from a JSON weights file;
  `GraphPrior` implements the cs_planning `Prior` trait (softmax x n; uniform on error) with timing counters. cs_engine: `graph`, `graph_vocab`, `GraphModel(weights, specs, graph vocabulary)` with

#### 78.22 THE INITIALIZATION PHASE, stages 1 and 2: start positions, the material curriculum, surprise detectors as modules (2026-11-09; Kaveh: an initialization phase that explores the game
from the smallest material upward -- two kings and one more piece on their starting squares, then four, five, ... under a budget -- learning cards, claims and lemmas at each size, with variants
that are counter-positions to a lemma ("what if this weren't here"), then games with wake / sleep; "to get surprise, compare with the teacher ... one way to generate surprise; keep it modular so
that we could use [another] method for cases where we don't have an oracle. But now that we do have a cheap oracle in Stockfish, let's just consult it.")
THE FLOW AS PLANNED: (1) start positions + the curriculum, (2) detectors with the teacher always consulted, (3) the lemma bindings interface, then counter-positions and claim nodes on it,
  (4) the driver that climbs sizes under a budget and stops on yield (new verified lemmas an hour). Stages 1 and 2 are BUILT here; 3 and 4 are not.
START POSITIONS: a start is an opaque position string the kernel accepts (None = the game's own). wake.play_self(starts=[...]) / `--starts <file>`; the game rows carry `start`; read_log, the corpus
  items, the deeper cards, graph_prior's corpus and rank_bench's samples carry it; the rank-source shape is now `rank(variant, moves, cap=None, start=None)` (UciTeacher, EstimateSource,
  HumanSource, GraphSource). Old logs read as before.
THE CURRICULUM (discovery/curriculum.py, generic): the sub-positions of the game's initial position that keep `size` units. A `PositionCodec` (units, keep) is the one game-specific adapter
  (ChessCodec over FENs; castling rights only where king and rook still stand); `required(game)` is found BY TEST (a unit whose removal the kernel rejects or that ends the game); every candidate
  is checked by the kernel (accepted, not over, has moves); a seeded sample when there are more than the limit. CLI `curriculum <game> --size n`.
THE DETECTORS (discovery/detectors.py): one shape -- `name`, `training_only`, `detect(ctx) -> [surprise]` -- and a registry. `Hindsight` (the engine's own later reading against its earlier: the
  method with no oracle), `Disagreement(source)` (a rank source's ordering against the card's), `Regret(source)` NEW (the move PLAYED against the source's ranking: worse than its best by the
  source's own declared gap, UciTeacher.gap 100; order alone when a source declares none). Regret runs whenever a rank source is given (Settings.regret), whatever the tie diagnosis. A rank-based
  surprise becomes a seed only when OUR exact card two plies deeper confirms it; for Regret: the source's top move optimal there AND the played move strictly worse. Source's top optimal but the
  played move tied under our judge is OPEN and is listed (rep["regret"]["open"]): the judge cannot see what the source sees. The teacher still never enters the store.
Tests: tests/test_plan78_22.py (15). sleep CLI gains --teacher-ms and --teacher-option NAME=VALUE (SyzygyPath makes Stockfish exact on the 3-5 unit positions; our tables end at 5).

#### 78.23 THE ORACLE AS THE JUDGE OF THE CARDS, and its lines as the WHY (2026-11-10; Kaveh: "even under 5 units, it should be stockfish"; "it can say this is why it's bad because it
leads to this and this and this")
WHY: 78.22 ended with 58 regrets the oracle saw and none confirmable, because the material judge ties every quiet move. The own-solver idea is DROPPED: Stockfish (with the Syzygy tables)
  is the oracle and the judge at every size. A lemma claims "an optimal move of this kind exists"; optimal is by a judge, and the judge is PART OF THE CLAIM (recorded on the lemma).
BUILT (discovery/judges.py, generic over rank sources): `Settings.judge_by = "source"`: the cards are built as before, then every move is revalued by the source's graded score
  (`CardSet.revalued`, Rust; a move the source does not rank cuts the card). A source may declare `grade(score) -> int` (UciTeacher: a mate keeps its exact distance, anything else is
  score // gap, so moves within a gap tie) and `lines(...)` (its own principal line after each move, from the same analysis). Regret is then confirmed DIRECTLY on the revalued card (the
  played move strictly worse than the best); Disagreement is skipped (the source would disagree with itself). `consequence(...)` replays a line through the kernel: plies, outcome, where
  the units first change. Every teacher-judged lemma carries meta.judge_source (the source's parameters), meta.teacher = true and meta.why (the line after the played move, the line after
  the best move, and where each ends). The source stays in the training kit: nothing of a decision calls it. Tests: tests/test_plan78_23.py (12).

  endgame. Stockfish at 100 ms is also not repeatable run to run (57 regrets in one run, 66 in another on the same log).

#### 78.24 THE LEMMA LANGUAGE, THE LOOP ON A SANDBOX STORE, AND THE AUDIT OF APPLICATION (2026-11-10; Kaveh: "I want to see what lemmas are mined and whether they're mined correctly and
whether they're applied correctly ... one lemma is not going to win the game. But the machinery is working, and that's the key point")
THE GOAL IS THE MECHANISM, NOT STRENGTH: starts -> wake -> sleep (oracle judges) -> lemmas filed -> next snapshot -> wake with them -> audit. Built by three Sonnet subagents, integrated here.
A. NAMED VOCABULARIES AND EFFECTS ON DERIVED RELATIONS. rules/learned/<game>/vocabulary.<name>.json (optional `concepts`: rules deltas composed onto the description); game_store
  vocabulary(game, name) / spec_texts(game, name) / read_lemmas(game, vocabulary) / build and publish(vocabulary=); the default vocabulary's snapshot bytes are unchanged. A vocabulary's
  `delta` may now name DERIVED relations: cs_memory op.rs `Effects` (the derived facts before and after a move, one helper for cards, the lemma prior and the lemma op). The climb gains
  "drop a response literal" (the response keeps at least one); `Gates.override`; sleep CLI --vocabulary, --gate NAME=VALUE, --held-gate, --teacher-mate-bucket. Tests: tests/test_plan78_24.py.
  Cost, printed by the build's check on 200 cards at depth 2, 1 thread: base-only delta 0.192 s, derived delta 2.505 s.
B. RELATIONAL UNIT CONCEPTS, as rules (rules/concepts/chess_units.gdl): distance, apart (king to unit distance), closer, flight, opposition, diagonal_opposition, to_promote, king_ahead,
  in_square; rules/learned/chess/vocabulary.relational.json names them as derived and as delta. Tests: tests/test_plan78_24_concepts.py.
  OBS units vocabulary: 72 positions, 53 facts a position (small) / 157 (full board), 0.8 ms a position (small) / 0.7 (full board)
C. THE LOOP AND THE AUDIT. discovery/initialize.py `run_size(game, size, source=...)`: the loop for one size on a SANDBOX store (paths.derived("init_store"); the real rules/learned is
  never written). discovery/apply_audit.py: `render` / `mined` (a lemma read as IF body THEN a best move removes / adds, with its stats, judge and why) and `audit(game, log, source=...)`:
  for every decision where a lemma fired, the moves it proposed (recovered with the ENGINE's own matcher, checked against the engine's count), whether the engine played one, and whether
  the claim held by the source. judges.Cached(source, file): a rank source remembered on disk, so the sleep, the audit and a re-run read one verdict per position.
  Tests: tests/test_plan78_24_loop.py. Integration fixes here: the vocabulary name reaches mined / audit / spec_texts; initialize gains --gate, --held-gate, --teacher-mate-bucket,
  --teacher-cache.

#### 78.25 THE REASONING CHAIN AS A TOOL: THREATS BY STAKE, THE FRAME, PARRY OR COUNTER, AND WHAT IS IRRELEVANT (2026-11-10; Kaveh: "my king is about to get mated ... that means I can ignore
the pawn on the corner because it's irrelevant to the mate ... first of all, I should not get mated ... how do I create a greater threat than mate? I can't. But if my rook is under attack, I
could create a greater threat than my rook ... this logical reasoning chain was a lot more useful, and I want that to be a part of one of the tools available here")
THE LOOK BACK. The lemmas Kaveh remembered are October's: plans 41 to 51 (selfmine: a window, the root lemma, diagnose, repair, the perturbation drill, schemas proved once in Lean and bound
everywhere) and plans 52 to 72 (the agenda: root questions in order of stake, defects and fixes, their agenda on the passed board, the frame carried forward, a budget hit is a GAP).
Both still run today: selfmine on game sHa6yUKv binds `delayed_balance_alive_d2`; analyse on dev_20 01IFU decides Nf3+ by mate_in_two. What stopped it, from its own record: schemas for
one and two of our moves only, a chase clock, material-only leaves, and no estimate past the budget (plan 61's ESTIMATE fired on 0 leaves; plan 69.2 was not built); 428 hand-written rows
of chess facts in the agenda. A prior net says WHICH unit matters; the chain says WHY. This slice brings the chain into the engine as ONE OPERATOR among the others, on the Game trait only.
DEFINITIONS (cs_tactics::reason, no game named):
  STAKE: the ledger value of a threat's line by the judge in use; the game's own goal is above every unit.
  THREAT against the side to move: a tactic of the other side with no defect on the PASSED state (the census of 78.6); a side with no pass must answer, every move is then read.
  FRAME of a threat: the base facts its line removes or adds, the line cut at its last ledger event; facts every legal move changes are no part of it.
  NET of a move of ours: its exact ledger value one ply deeper than the threat was read (`root_values`). A move ANSWERS when its net beats passing (net > -stake).
  The question asked of each answer is whether they can STILL CARRY THE THREAT OUT: the threat's first move, if still legal, is read exactly and its line searched for the targets.
    PARRY: they cannot. COUNTER: they can, and our net if they do is above 0 (a greater threat). COVER: it is 0 (what they take is taken back or matched).
    LESSEN: it is below 0 and still better than passing. A threat on the goal has parries only: nothing outbids it.
  UNIT: the facts of ours a move removes. IRRELEVANT: a unit none of whose moves answers and none of whose facts is in the frame. A move the budget left unread is never called irrelevant.
  With no threat against us the candidates are OUR tactics: the ones that work now, then the threats one free move creates.
  The result is an ORDER (the ledger search reads these moves first, after the lemmas') and an EXPLANATION (`reason:` lines in the decision's trace). Never a verdict: the ledger's value decides.
BUILT (a Sonnet subagent, then refined at integration): rust/engine/tactics/src/reason.rs (`reason`, `reason_within`, `explain`), `ReasonOp`, `Goal::Reason`, `Params.reason` (default OFF,
REASON_SHARE 0.1 of the clock), py `reason(...)` and `reason=` on best_move and solve_batch, wake `--reason`. Tests: tests/test_plan78_25_reason.py (10).
INTEGRATION FINDINGS, each fixed and tested: (1) the first parry / counter split called Rxa8 (taking the attacker) a counter and a knight move that attacks the queen a parry; the question
"can they still carry it out" replaced it. (2) A threat's line carried the reading's quiet tail into the frame; the line now ends at its last ledger event. (3) A guard was named a counter
("outbid") at net 0; COVER is its own kind. (4) Our own census ran under its node fuse alone:
OBS decision seconds on n 423 median 0.201 p95 0.203 max 0.463 over 0.25: 4
  One deadline now holds for the whole chain (`census_within`); after it, same run:

READING. (1) The chain is a tool beside the others and says why: the threat, what it is worth, the facts it runs through, which moves stop it, which outbid it, and which units have no
part in it. (2) It is CUT OFTEN ON A SHORT CLOCK: at 0.2 s a move it is a GAP in 309 of 427 decisions, at
0.5 s in 127 of 432. The cut readings are mostly our own census (one free move, then a gain: one reading per quiet move) and the readings after each answer. A GAP is said as a GAP. (3) Its
share costs the ledger depth at both clocks (the means above). (4) NOT MEASURED: strength. No match was played with the chain on against the chain off; the order it gives the ledger and
the move the ledger then plays agree often (first candidate 297 of 414 at 0.5 s), which says the two readings are consistent, not that play improved.
OPEN: follow the chain DEEPER (their answer to our answer, the frame carried forward as in 72.10) with an ESTIMATE where the budget ends, which is what October lacked; the irrelevant
set used to NARROW a reading and not only to explain it; our own census ordered by stake so a short clock reads the best first; targets compared by kind, not by place; the chain's
facts (threat, frame, answer, irrelevant) as the vocabulary of lemmas; whether to switch the chain on by default (a match on against off decides).

#### 78.26 WIN / DRAW / LOSS FROM ANY POSITION, SHARPNESS, AND WHICH PATH TO TAKE (2026-11-10; Kaveh: "in order to be able to get past where we got stuck in October, we need to have a
probability of win, draw, loss from any given position ... query the database for positions that are like this, or run a Monte Carlo simulation from that point on. And then once we know how
sharp the position is ... if the chance of draw is low ... we should continue reasoning. And basically, if that's not true, we should probably rely on the probabilities to pick one path")
WHERE OCTOBER STOPPED (78.25's look back): the chain had no answer past its budget; a GAP was a GAP and the unproved pick was a guess. This slice gives every position an ESTIMATE
of win, draw and loss, a reading of how SHARP it is, and a rule in the controller that takes one of two paths by that reading.
DEFINITIONS (cs_planning::wdl, no game named):
  WDL: win / draw / loss MASS from one role's view (counts, possibly fractional). SCORE: (win + draw / 2) over the mass. SHARPNESS: (win + loss) over the mass, 1 less the draw probability.
  SPLIT of one outcome v in 0..1: above one half it is win 2v - 1 and draw 2 - 2v; below it is loss 1 - 2v and draw 2v. The score is kept exactly; there is no band constant.
  SOURCE 1, PLAYOUTS: the UCT search of 78.17 with a tally at the root and under each root move. A playout that reaches the game's end counts by the game's outcome; one cut after
    WDL_PLAYOUT plies counts by the units standing (the `Balance` leaf, its scale WDL_SCALE times the smallest positive worth standing, so the judge's unit does not matter).
  SOURCE 2, THE TABLE ("positions like this"): counts of results from the mover's view under keys, most specific first: `exact:<the position's key>`, then
    `units:<each role's unit kinds>:<the mover>`. A lookup takes the first key holding TABLE_MIN mass. Pooled with the playouts, a hit brings at most TABLE_CAP mass.
  SHARP: sharpness at or above SHARP. UNKNOWN: less than MIN_MASS mass. QUIET: the rest.
  THE RULE (cs_decision, `Params.wdl`, default OFF): lemma and proof as before. If the proof does not decide, the operator "wdl" estimates the position on WDL_SHARE of the clock.
    SHARP or UNKNOWN: keep reasoning. The chain of 78.25 runs, then the ledger with the rest of the clock; the ledger's move is played.
    QUIET: the ledger reads with its ties; if its value does not decide and it leaves more than one move equal, "wdl" is asked to PREFER among those moves and its pick is played.
    The exact reading stays the guard in both paths: the probabilities choose only among moves the ledger could not tell apart. One trace line says which path and why.
BUILT (a Sonnet subagent, refined at integration): rust/engine/planning/src/wdl.rs (`Wdl`, `split`, `sharp`, `Table`, `leaf_scale`, `WdlOp` answering `Goal::Estimate` and
`Goal::Prefer`), the tallies `root_wdl` and `move_wdl` in `mcts::Search` (every earlier result unchanged), `Careful` in rollout.rs, `Params.wdl` and `Params.wdl_table`, py `wdl(...)`,
`wdl_keys`, `wdl_keys_along`, `wdl=` and `wdl_table=` on best_move and solve_batch, discovery/wdl_table.py (the table built from FINISHED games of wake logs, provenance "own games"),
wake `--wdl` and `--wdl-table`. Tests: rust/engine/planning/tests/wdl.rs (8), one more in tests/rollout.rs, tests/test_plan78_26_wdl.py (16).

READING. (1) THE MECHANISM WORKS END TO END: any position gets win / draw / loss from playouts, from a table of similar positions, or both pooled; sharpness is read from it; the
controller takes the reasoning path or the probability path by it, and says so in the trace. (2) THE ESTIMATE IS THE WEAK PART, in this order: the sharp call misses most positions
the oracle calls decided; the pick among tied moves is only partly repeatable; the own-games table is thin, and unfinished games are skipped (28 of 48 here), so it holds only what this
engine could play to an end. (3) NOT MEASURED: strength. No match was played with the rule on against off.
DECISIONS LEFT TO KAVEH: (a) WHICH DATABASE. The table is filled from the engine's own results. Human games would fill it far better and the builder takes any list of finished games,
but human frequencies entering a decision crosses the rule of 78.17 (teachers and human games are training tools). (b) HOW MUCH THE PROBABILITIES DECIDE. Here they pick only among moves
the exact reading leaves equal. Picking outright in a quiet position would drop that guard.
OPEN: a better sharp call (the count of threats and forcing lines from 78.25's chain as a second sign of sharpness; a leaf that reads the exchanges out before it counts); one search
over the tied moves in place of an even split, so the playouts go where the scores are close; the estimate where the chain's budget ends (78.25's open item) and not only at the
root; the scale of the squash fitted against the oracle at sleep; the table keyed by more than the units standing; a match on against off.

#### 78.27 THE SLEEP CYCLE OF THE ESTIMATE: WHERE THE WAKE LACKED THE DATA OR THE LEMMA, THE SLEEP WORKS THERE (2026-11-10; Kaveh: "if you find that you don't have the data or the lemma,
then you go back to a sleep cycle, and in the sleep cycle, the training, you are allowed to look at the games, find new rules, improve your prior, improve the WDL probabilities from the
playouts, and then at the wake time, we use those lemmas again, or our priors. So we don't leak the engine information into the inference time, into the wake time. We only do it in the
sleep time. And then there is a human database on this, if we need to, but I want to see how the sleep cycle works with this.")

THE RULE, RESTATED. The wake decides with what the last sleep left it and nothing else: the store (lemmas, judge), the prior, the results table, its own search and playouts. Where it lacks
the data or the lemma it says so in its log. The sleep reads that log and works exactly there with the training kit: the games, deeper playouts, the lemma miner, and the outside engine as
JUDGE. No number of the outside engine is written into anything the wake reads. The human games stay unread until Kaveh asks.

DESIGN (answers 78.26's first open decision: the table is filled by the engine's own games and the sleep's own playouts).
  1 THE GAPS  a reading of a wake log played with `--wdl`, decision by decision: no table row; only a coarse row (not the exact position); the estimate unknown (too little mass); a
              quiet pick whose two best moves are closer than a margin; no lemma fired; and, in a finished game, the estimate on the wrong side of the game's own result. Counted,
              and listed as the sleep's worklist. Own data only.
  2 THE READING THE SLEEP USES  a small menu of the engine's own estimate settings (the wake's own, the same with a long clock, a far cut, playouts to the end). When a judge is given
              the sleep measures each on a sample of the wake's positions against the judge's win / draw / loss and takes the closest; without one it takes the long clock and says
              so. The judge chooses a TOOL; its numbers go nowhere.
  3 SETTLE    an unfinished game's last position is read with that setting and the game counts with that reading as its result (marked as settled, not played).
  4 DEEPEN    the gap positions (capped, spread over the games) are read with that setting and the readings filed under the position's keys: on the exact key at the table's
              full weight, on the coarser keys as one position's vote.
  5 THE TABLE the finished games, the settled games and the deep readings, each source counted in the file's stats. The next wake pools it with its playouts as 78.26 does.
  6 MEASURE   the wake's own estimate (its clock, with the old table and with the new one) against the judge on positions of the log the deep readings did not touch, and
              separately on the ones they did (said so). Then the next wake's gaps against this wake's.
  7 THE CYCLE the loop driver of 78.24 (initialize.py, a sandbox store) with the estimate on: wake, gaps, the lemma sleep, the estimate's sleep, the next wake with the new snapshot
              and the new table, for a number of cycles; the table lives in the sandbox next to the lemmas.

  READING
  1 THE CYCLE RUNS END TO END. The wake's log gives the gaps, the lemma sleep mines and admits (B: three lemmas from no lemmas), the estimate's sleep settles, deepens and writes the table,
    the next wake reads the new snapshot and the new table, and the table is carried into the following sleep. In B the lemmas fire in the later wake and the audit finds their claims
    held by the outside engine where they fired. Nothing of the outside engine is in the snapshot or the table (the test builds the table with and without a judge and compares).
  2 MORE OF THE SAME PLAYOUTS IS NOT A BETTER ESTIMATE. In all four sleeps the readings with thirty times the clock, or cut far later, or played to the end, are within noise of the
    wake's own quick reading against the judge, and twice worse. The error is in what a playout plays and how its leaf is valued, not in how many are played. So the table filled from
    deep playouts repeats the wake's own opinion with more mass; held-out accuracy does not move in A. In B it moves once (first sleep) and not the second time.
  3 THE KEYS DO NOT GENERALISE WHERE THEY SHOULD AND GENERALISE TOO MUCH WHERE THEY SHOULD NOT. In full games a fresh wake never met an exact row; only the coarse row answered.
    At three units the coarse row answers almost every position, with one opinion for every position of the same units.
  4 THE TABLE AS BUILT HURTS PLAY AT THREE UNITS. Unfinished games rise from wake a to the wakes with the table, and the controls in C separate the causes: the table without the
    lemmas has more unfinished games than the lemmas without the table. A coarse row pooled into every child of a position pulls the moves' estimates together, so the
    pick among them is thinner (the thin_pick count rises with the table). The regret of the last wake against the outside engine is higher than wake a's. A mechanism check, as the line says.
  5 THE LEMMA SLEEP'S SECOND PASS ADMITTED NOTHING NEW (rejected 60): the candidates it climbed did not survive the held-out check.

  LEFT TO KAVEH (none started)
  a the coarse row should not be pooled into the comparison of sibling moves, only into the estimate of the position (a change in cs_planning::wdl);
  b whether the sleep may FIT the estimate's own few parameters (the leaf's scale, the cut, the playout's choice) against the outside engine, the way the prior is fitted: the fitted
    numbers would be the engine's own parameters, yet they are learned from the outside engine's verdicts, so this is his call under the leak rule;
  c the human table;
  d richer keys than the units (facts the lemmas already name), so that "positions like this" means something between exact and units;
  e a sharp signal from the reasoning chain (in B the wake called almost nothing sharp while the judge called about half of the sampled positions decided).

#### 78.28 PLAYOUTS TO A REAL RESULT, DIAGNOSED AT SLEEP: WHERE A PLAYOUT THREW THE RESULT AWAY, FIND THE MOVE AND MINE THE RULE (2026-11-10; Kaveh: "a play out, if it's a Monte Carlo
     play out, should go into a win, draw, or loss ... ask Stockfish, what was this position? ... you started with a winning position and you went into a draw ... find the point at which
     you went to the draw ... why does this move go into a draw and why does that move not ... then there's a rule"; "And all of this should happen in sleep.")

  THE RULE, RESTATED  A playout ends in a win, a draw or a loss, not in a material count. At SLEEP the outside engine says what the start of the playout was worth; where the result is
            worse, the sleep walks the playout to the move where the verdict turned, compares that move with one that keeps the verdict, and mines a rule from the difference with the
            lemma machinery that exists (cards, climb, held-out check). The next playouts follow the stored rules, so they stop making that mistake, and the win / draw / loss numbers
            improve because the playouts play better. Nothing is fitted to the outside engine's numbers; the wake carries only rules.
  DESIGN
  1 THE PLAYOUT GAME  one playout from a position to a real result (a cap in plies only as a guard, said when hit), its moves kept. Its policy: the stored rules first (the lemma
            prior that exists, rust/engine/decision/src/lemma_prior.rs), the careful capture test where no rule speaks.
  2 THE TURNING MOVE  the outside engine's verdict (win / draw / loss class for the mover) along the playout; the first ply where the class drops for the side that moved is the
            turning move; the keeping move is one of the outside engine's best there. Training only.
  3 THE RULE  the turning positions enter the lemma sleep as its seeds, beside the ones from the real games; admission is unchanged.
  4 THE NEXT PLAYOUTS  read the new snapshot. Measured per cycle: the share of playouts whose result matches the outside engine's verdict of their start, and the turning moves found.
  5 WHERE   all of it in the sleep. The wake is not changed by this plan.
  6 THE PROBLEM MUST GO AWAY (Kaveh, same day: "in the sleep period, we should also be able to reason ... the shortcomings of our reasoning in the sleep is what gives us the
            dilemma ... at the end of the sleep period, after the new lemma, the reasoning now works ... you add something during the sleep that makes it better and makes the problem
            go away. And then in the wake, now the problem doesn't exist anymore until you hit a new problem")
            A PROBLEM is a position where the engine's own decision (its full reasoning, as the wake runs it) loses the outside engine's verdict. The sleep runs that same reasoning
            on the problem BEFORE it adds anything (it fails, and how it fails is the diagnosis), adds (a rule, or the statistics), then runs it AGAIN with the new snapshot. Solved
            means the decision now keeps the verdict. The sleep reports problems, solved, still open; the problems are kept in the sandbox and re-checked every later sleep, so a
            solved problem that comes back is seen. The wake meets only what the sleep left open or has not met yet.

  READING
  1 THE LOOP RUNS: playouts end in a real result, the sleep finds turning moves, drops the ones the engine's own decision already gets right, keeps the rest as problems, hands them
    to the lemma sleep, and checks every problem again after it. The problem file carries over the cycles.
  2 NO PROBLEM WAS SOLVED. Ten problems after three cycles, all open. The lemma sleep admitted one rule in three cycles and it does not speak at any of the ten. Most of the ten
    are of one family (the unit that should wait is advanced before the one that should lead), read off the problem file by hand; two look like noise of the verdict at depth 12
    late in a long game and should be re-judged deeper before they count.
  3 WHY (to be shown, not yet shown): the lemma sleep is a statistical miner over many cards; a turning position enters as one seed among dozens and its candidate must then pass a
    held-out precision bar. Nothing in it is aimed at ONE problem until that problem is solved. October's way was (seed from one position, simplest rule, diagnose the failing
    condition, repair, drill with counter-positions). That targeted miner is the piece the cycle lacks.
  4 The playouts follow the one rule where it speaks (56 plies of 120 playouts); the share of playouts matching the verdict of their start did not move beyond noise.
  NEXT (not started): aim a targeted miner at each open problem (the played move against the keeping move, the smallest condition that separates them, drilled against
  counter-positions), admit only if the problem's check passes; re-judge problems deeper before filing them.

  2 A rule tested only near its problem (A, B) solves the problem and is wrong in the games: one-literal bodies fire at every decision, the audit refutes them, regret rises.
    Solving the problem cannot be the only bar.
  3 With the lemma sleep's own bar on held-out log positions (C) the targeted miner admits nothing: its repair goes from a rule that fires everywhere to one that fires nowhere.
  4 As forced seeds (D) every problem is confirmed and nearly every one is climbed; most candidates then die with a perfect record on too few firings (the per-seed lines in
    scratchpad run_f.out: precision 1.0 on one to seven firings, the lower bound under the bar). The log of one wake does not hold enough positions where a candidate speaks.
    The rules the sleep did admit hold in the audit.
  5 So the open piece is EVIDENCE ON DEMAND: for a candidate that is right on the few positions it has, find more positions where its body binds (the playouts of the sleep
    visit tens of thousands) and ask the rank source there, then apply the same bar.

#### 78.32 WHAT OCTOBER HAD: A FIXED EXAM, EXACT TRUTH WITH A FULL DRILL, AND A RULE INDUCED FROM EXACT LABELS (2026-11-11; Kaveh: "look at the October runs ... we were on a
     path to improvement there. We were just not general enough. But here, we're not improving"; on who proposes rules: no outside LLM call in the loop, a locally trained agent
     is acceptable, and Claude in the session steps in by hand only "when we end up going in circles")

  WHAT OCTOBER DID (read from plans 41 to 72 and the journal): the same puzzle sets re-run after every change with the changed decisions listed; exact proof as the truth; one
            failed position at a time, the failing condition named, a generic repair, a drill with zero disagreements allowed. Its rules were written by hand; its automatic
            miner proved almost nothing. The cycle of 78.27 to 78.31 has none of the first three: fresh games each cycle, a sampled outside verdict with an accuracy bar, a
            problem only as a seed of a statistical search.
  DESIGN
  1 THE EXAM   a set of positions fixed once for a game and a size (non-trivial: some legal move keeps the result and some does not, by the exact labeller), graded after every
            sleep with the wake's own decision: kept N of M, the decisions that changed since the last grading listed. Graded twice with the same snapshot once, to print the
            spread of the clock. Training data; the wake never reads it.
  2 THE EXACT LABELLER AND THE FULL DRILL   at the sizes the tablebase covers, the result class of a position is exact and cheap. A corpus of distinct positions (generic
            sources: the starts, playouts, random legal play), every move of each labelled keeps / loses, cached. A rule is run over the WHOLE corpus: right where every named
            move keeps, wrong where any named move loses, trivial where every legal move keeps. ADMISSION: zero wrong on a development part and on a held-out part (split by
            start), a stated minimum of non-trivial right firings, the problem's own check, no solved problem broken.
  3 INDUCTION  local and deterministic: from a problem, heads the keeping moves have and the losing moves have not; the body found by a covering search over lifted literals of
            the vocabulary against the corpus's exact labels (most non-trivial right firings subject to zero wrong, conjunctions up to a stated size). No sampled bar.
  4 THE CYCLE  wake, playouts, problems, induction on the open problems, the exam; the curve of the exam over the cycles is the result.
  LATER, NOT NOW  a locally trained policy that orders the literals the search tries, rewarded by the drill, when the search is the bottleneck.

  BUILT  discovery/exact.py (ExactLabeller; SyzygyChess: cursed wins and blessed losses count as draws), corpus.py (the labelled corpus, drill / drill_many), exam.py (build, grade,

#### 78.33 RELATIVE POSITION FIRST, THEN ABSOLUTE POSITION AS BOARD STRUCTURE (2026-11-11; Kaveh: "there is some notion of translational invariance in chess. Basically, a pin is a
     pin, no matter where it is ... in some cases, naming the square is important ... the fact that there's an edge is important ... every rank is not the same ... consider the
     relations of the units independently, and then consider the relations of the units in the context of their position in space. First is relative position, and then it's
     absolute position")

  WHAT 78.32 SHOWED OF THIS  a body literal is written two ways today: every constant lifted to a variable, or the constants kept (a square by its name). The rules induction lost on
            the held-out part were of the second kind. The hand rules that passed are relations between units (a king's distance to squares placed relative to a pawn, one
            king nearer than the other) with two facts of the board's structure inside the word (not a rook file; the pawn's advance).
  DESIGN
  1 THREE TIERS OF BODY LITERALS, tried in this order by the induction search (a wider tier only when the narrower one gives no rule that passes both parts of the drill):
            RELATIVE   relations between units with every coordinate a variable; constants of a DISTANCE sort stay (a distance does not change when the position is shifted).
            STRUCTURE  the relative literals plus where a coordinate stands in the board: its distance to the nearest edge of its axis, and to the goal end of the axis for the
                       side (the promotion rank). A coordinate is described, never named.
            NAMED      the constants kept, as now. Last.
  2 THE BOARD'S STRUCTURE FROM THE DESCRIPTION, generic: the vocabulary file names the game's AXES (a coordinate sort and its successor relation; optionally the relation that
            gives a side's last coordinate on it). Code that knows no game writes the rules-delta for them: the edge distance of every coordinate of an axis (an edge is a
            coordinate with no successor or no predecessor), and the goal distance per side. A game with no axes has an empty STRUCTURE tier.
  3 EVERY RULE SAYS ITS TIER  (meta.tier), and induction prints, per problem, the tier that gave the rule or how far each tier got.
  4 MEASURE  the same three cycles and the same exam as 78.32, with the hand rules as seeds: rules admitted per tier, the near misses per tier (wrong on the held-out part), the
            exam curve.
  LATER  relations over two hops (the square a unit reaches in two moves, said without naming it); an exception at the edge as an ordinary rule with one STRUCTURE literal more.

  BUILT  discovery/board_structure.py (game-free: from the vocabulary file's `axes` and the description's successor facts, a rules-delta of ground facts edge_gap_<sort> coordinate
         distance and goal_gap_<sort> side coordinate distance; signatures_of / sorts_of say which argument of a relation is a coordinate); game_store composes it when the
         vocabulary file has `axes` (vocabulary.keys.json has; the other vocabularies are byte for byte as before); induce.tiered_candidates and the widening search (setting
         `tiers`), meta.tier; tests/test_plan78_33_tiers.py. HEADS are not tiered: a head can still carry a rank constant.

#### 78.35 WORDS BUILT FROM WORDS AND GIVEN A NAME; GENERAL AND GAME KNOWLEDGE TOLD APART BY A PROGRAM; USE BEFORE GENERATION (2026-11-11)

  KAVEH (after the look back at October's vocabulary: base_vocabulary.py, terms.py of plan 76.4c, the ontology shelf, the 130 lemma entries; nearly all by hand, in Python,
        the second game never run): a richer vocabulary is welcome if what is chess knowledge and what applies outside chess are cleanly apart. A concept is CONSTRUCTED
        from the vocabulary when it can be; when the construction is long it is defined once and given a short NAME from a static list of names (like the names of
        storms), also for a concept people have no term for. October's words ran in Python: here they run in Rust. Mining will not find everything and help by hand with
        words and lemmas is accepted; the question first is USE: given the words and lemmas, does the engine reason with them. Use and generation are kept apart.

  READING  on this exam the failures are a missing rule, not a rule unused: read by hand they are two families, both king and pawn: the side with the pawn pushes it where
        the king must go first while its king is NOT nearer the key squares than the other king (the hand rule asks nearer), and the side without the pawn does not head
        for the squares that hold the draw (rook pawns among them, which the hand words leave out). This exam asks one decision; it does not test a chain of rules.
  DESIGN
  1 A WORD IS A TERM  a small term language over the relations of the description and of the vocabulary (literal, and, or, not, exists, compose, via: the middle kept,
        reach in at most k steps, closure, restrict), October's constructors of plan 76.4c kept where a rule can say them. A term COMPILES to rules of the description's own
        language with a signature, so the Rust evaluator that reads every other word reads it too: nothing of a word is evaluated in Python on the decision path.
  2 A NAME  a term used by an admitted rule, or an admitted body longer than a set size, is defined once and named: the next unused name of a static list
        (rules/concepts/names.txt). The registry of a store says for each word its name, its term, its expansion in base words, who made it (hand, generated, mined).
  3 GENERAL OR GAME, BY A PROGRAM  a word is GENERAL when its definition, followed down to the description's relations, names no constant of the game (sides by role and
        distances aside); else it is GAME knowledge. Computed from the rules, not declared. Every word of a vocabulary and every rule (by its words) carries the label; a
        run reports its rules and its exam by label.
  4 USE  the split above as a standing measurement beside every exam grade.
  5 GENERATION, after  the induction asks for terms, smallest first under a cap, only where its search fails; a word stays only with a rule that passes the drill.
  ALSO  78.34's open point 5 (the audit calls a rule refuted where the drill of the same wake's positions does not) is to be settled in this slice.

         word_registry.py (words.json of a store: define with one definition one name, delta; analyse / layer_of / layers: GENERAL or GAME from the rules; rule_layer,

  2 The two `toward` rules are right far more often than wrong on the held-out part and are dropped by the zero-wrong test (their drill lines). A rule that is nearly

    The general layer has 4 of the 16 words. The split is now measured; it is not yet good.
  5 The family of the side WITH the pawn (pushing where the king must lead while its king is not the nearer) was not attempted here.

#### 78.36 USE: A RULE THAT CLAIMS A RESULT, AND A SEARCH THAT WORKS TOWARD IT (2026-11-12; Kaveh: get the use of the lemmas right; "Yes go")

  WHERE USE STANDS (read from rust/engine/decision/src/lib.rs): a rule's named moves are already only the ORDER the ledger search reads the root in. But the ledger's judge
        is material: where no line changes material within its horizon every move is equal and the first in the order is played. So a rule decides exactly where the search
        cannot check it, and a rule that is nearly always right (78.35 reading 2) cannot be kept. And a rule names one move: nothing says what a line of moves is FOR.
  DESIGN
  1 A CLAIM  a second kind of rule: IF body THEN the position's class for the side to move is win / draw / loss. Admitted like every rule: the full drill on both parts of
        the exact corpus, zero wrong, enough right. It is a statement about a position, not about a move.
  2 THE SEARCH TOWARD CLAIMS  an operator of the decision, game-free: a bounded AND-OR search whose leaves are the game's own outcome and the claims of the snapshot. A
        forced line to a claimed win is played. Otherwise each root move gets the class the other side can force against it within the depth (unknown where no claim
        speaks); the ledger then reads first the moves of the best known class and LAST the moves a claim refutes, so a response rule's named move is a suggestion that
        this search can overturn. With no claim in the snapshot the decision and its trace are what they were.
  3 THE CHAIN, MEASURED  a CONVERSION exam beside the one-decision exam: from fixed held-out positions the engine plays the game out against the exact labeller's defence
        (an opponent of the training kit: it only plays, nothing of it reaches the wake); counted: games in which the engine never drops the class, and wins finished.
  4 BY HAND FIRST  claims on the key-square words written by Claude in session and admitted by the drill; induction of claims by the machine is a later stage.

#### 78.37 to 78.39 THREE MORE APPROACHES: SURPRISE ON FULL GAMES AS THE MEASURE, LEARNING BY CONSTRUCTION, A GOAL TAKEN APART BACKWARD (2026-11-12; Kaveh: "we want the rate of surprise to go down ... if you fix this one and then you break another one, what's the point?"; "what happens with a single piece on the board? ... you just add pieces"; "if the bishop can get here, if the knight can get here, I can mate")
WHY NOW. 78.36 reading 3: the exam at three units is a test of the clock. The pool has to widen and the measure must not reward a local fix.

78.37 SURPRISE ON FULL GAMES (the measure and the food)
  POOL       games from the game's own start, from a pluggable source: the engine against itself, the engine against an outside engine, a file of game records. The human game
             files stay unread until Kaveh says so; the source interface takes them without a change.
  TWO READINGS at every position of a game, both from the mover's side:
    OURS     what the engine's decision at the stated clock says: the value of its search by the judge in use (the `value` of the decision's steps), whether a step proved the
             goal, and the class a claim rule gives when one speaks.
    JUDGE'S  an outside engine at a fixed depth, in its own units, cached on disk. Training kit only: no number of it is written into anything the wake reads.
  COMMON UNIT both readings are mapped to an EXPECTED RESULT between 0 and 1 by one monotone curve per reading (the judge's by its own win, draw, loss model where it has one;
             ours by the same curve over the judge's units per unit of worth, fitted once on the games and stated). A change near a decided game is small, a change that
             turns a win into a draw is large: the weight Kaveh asked for comes from the unit, not from a hand table.
  JUMP       the change of a reading across one move, in expected result, at least a stated threshold.
  SURPRISE   a move where one reading jumps and the other does not, or they jump in opposite directions. Kinds: MISSED (the judge jumps, we do not), FALSE (we jump, the judge
             does not), and by whose move it was (ours: a mistake we did not see; theirs: a chance or a danger we did not see). WEIGHT: the size of the judge's jump.
  A STANDING GAP (the readings differ and neither moves) is counted apart: it is a wrong level, not a surprise.
  THE MEASURE on FRESH games every cycle (new seeds, so nothing is held out by hand): surprises per 100 positions, the weighted rate (summed weight per 100 positions),
             the mean loss of our own moves in the judge's units and in expected result. Stated with the clock, and with the no-rules store beside it at more than one clock.
  FOOD       the surprises, heaviest first, become the problems of the sleep (the problem file of 78.28, the pool of 78.34 with the judge as labeller where no exact table
             reaches). A rule is kept when the weighted rate on fresh games does not rise: the gate is the rate, not the one position.
  STAGES     1 the meter and the ranked list (this slice); 2 the sleep fed from the list; 3 the cycle gated on the rate.

78.38 LEARNING BY CONSTRUCTION (the ladder)
  LADDER     unit sets generated from the game description in order of size: what the game cannot do without (78.22 `required`), then one more unit of each kind and side,
             then two. Nothing names a chess unit: kinds and sides are read from the description.
  OBSERVE    for each set, positions are sampled and their result is OBSERVED: by the exact labeller where a table reaches (training kit), and by the engine's own exhaustive
             search where the set is small enough, the two compared. The set's SUMMARY: the shares of win, draw and loss by side to move, and whether a result other than a draw
             exists at all.
  CLAIMS     a set where one class holds for nearly every position gives a CLAIM rule by machine (78.36), its body in the counting words of the units present, drilled on the
             set's positions; the exceptions are the next problems (the body grows a condition, relative words first, board structure second: 78.33).
  CARRY      a set with a capture or a promotion falls to a smaller or a known set: the claims of the sets below are the leaves of the search in the set above. This is where the
             search toward claims has something to reach, and it is the answer to 78.36 OPEN (claims are few).
  ORDER      a set is opened when the sets it can fall to are summarised. For each open set with wins, the cycle of 78.34 runs on it with the rules of the sets below loaded.
  STAGES     1 the ladder, the summaries, the set-level claims and their drill (this slice); 2 the cycle per set with carry; 3 four and five units.

78.39 A GOAL TAKEN APART BACKWARD (the scenario)
  WHAT EXISTS the census of defects (78.6) and the reasoning chain (78.25) read a threat that is one or two moves from working. What Kaveh describes is further back: no
             threat exists yet, and the question is what would have to be true.
  GOAL       a terminal condition of the description (the game's own goal first). Its HOLES in a position: the conditions of the goal that do not hold now, each tied to a
             location (for the game's goal: every location the target unit can still go to, and its own).
  SUPPLY     for each hole, the units of ours that could close it: a unit whose kind can act on that location from some location it can reach, with the number of moves, read
             from the move relations of the description (the `reach` words of 78.35). A fixed unit (one that moves rarely or one way) is read as structure, not as supply.
  CONTEST    for each supply, what of theirs denies it: a unit of theirs that acts on the supplying location or on the path, and whether an exchange of equals removes both.
             A supply with no equal of theirs in range is an OPPORTUNITY.
  SCENARIO   an assignment of distinct supplying units to all holes: "if this unit gets here and that one there, the goal holds". None exists: the goal is out of reach with
             the units present, and the same reading from their side says our own target unit is SAFE from that direction, and stays safe until the units change.
  USE        a scenario is a target for the search (the search toward claims of 78.36 with the scenario as the claimed state) and an order of moves (the supplying moves
             first); from their side it is the list of threats to watch.
  STAGES     1 holes, supply, contest and scenarios for the game's goal as a report, in Rust beside the census (speed), measured for cost per position; 2 the scenario as a
             search target; 3 other goals (a unit won).
ORDER OF WORK. 78.37 stage 1 and 78.38 stage 1 are built side by side (different files); 78.39 starts with a reading of the census and the chain to see what stage 1 can reuse.
