## 78.52 THE GRAPH, LAYER 1: concepts and basic facts derived from the rules (SYSTEM_SPEC section 11; Rust first)

Serves: the one graph (sections 2 and 11). Kaveh's go of 2026-11-15. Nothing here plays; it is the base the mined
concepts (layer 2) and the claims and conditions (layer 3) attach to.

A. WHAT THE RULES GIVE. Read how the rules state the board: the places, and the step relations between them by
   direction (chess.gdl states steps by direction). Find how the engine can ask the rules for these statically, through
   the existing crates and the bound names (as the sheet's medium of movement is bound), without touching the
   protected files. If it cannot be done without them, stop and report; do not work around it.
B. THE NODES, derived, none supplied:
   - place: one per place of the rules.
   - direction: one per step relation.
   - line: a maximal chain of places under one direction and its reverse. (For chess the ranks, files and diagonals
     come out of this; no name of them is written anywhere.)
   - edge: for each direction, the set of places with no next place under it; and the edge distance of a place per
     direction (steps until the chain ends). The edge is a concept node; a place links to the edges it lies on.
   - kind: one per kind of unit of the rules; unit: one per unit standing, per position.
   Plain links: place on line (with its index along the line), place next to place by direction, place on edge,
   unit on place, unit of kind, unit of side.
   Relation nodes (they will be pointed at): unit bears on place / on unit, with the line it runs along where the
   bearing follows one line, and the units standing between where a line is shut (from the existing why_not).
C. FORM. A game-free Rust module in an existing crate: the static part built once per game, the per-position part
   built from a state through `Placed`, with stable ids (a node's id is its definition, not a counter). A Python
   entry returns the graph as node and link lists; a small Python mirror reads it for inspection.
D. CHECKS. On chess and one other variant with a different board or movement: counts of places, directions, lines and
   edge places against what the rules imply; every bearing of `Placed` appears as exactly one relation node; the
   static part is identical across positions. The names rank, file, diagonal appear only in a TEST's expected counts
   for chess, never in the module.
E. THE STATEMENTS OVER THE GRAPH. Re-express the 26 statements of 78.49 as counts over the graph (equal numbers,
   tested), and add the ones 78.49 could not state: units by edge distance, pairs of own units bearing on each other
   along one open line, the open length of a line. Unmoved units need the game's record and are left for layer 3.

Not in this plan: derived concepts dcN (layer 2), claims and conditions as nodes (layer 3), any network.

78.52 BUILT (branch worktree-agent-a5b0e5910717155cf, 2026-11-15 11:40 by the builder agent; stages A to E). Nothing is wired into any player; nothing is fitted; no match, no fit.
A. HOW THE RULES ARE ASKED. `Placed::steps` (a default method of the trait, rust/engine/game/src/placed.rs, `read_steps`) loads the game's description (cs_gdl `Program`), takes from the graph vocabulary's bound names
   (rules/learned/<game>/graph_vocabulary.json: its static relations and its objects) the one static relation whose signature is a direction sort followed by two places (the object's component sorts twice), reads
   its rows (static, no state) and the place object's component sorts, joins the components of a place to its text and requires the set to equal the game's own `place_names` (else an error). No protected file was
   touched; no geometry written; no place name parsed (the components are joined, as the medium's tables join them). The text of the description and the bound names are handed in by the Python entry (as the medium
   is); a variant without a description of its own reads the first game's (as 78.49's tests do).
   Reused: the description reader (cs_gdl `Program`), `Placed` (cells, bearing_from, reach_from, why_not), `Names`, `PlaceSet`, the graph vocabulary's bound names, game_store.graph_spec_texts. Not reused: decision/graph.rs
   (cs_decision; terms and facts of the description, not the board's lines, edges and units; cs_tactics cannot depend on it) and fact_graph.py (the term / fact / move graph; it holds the static `step` rows as facts, which is
   the same source, but has no line, edge or relation node): this graph sits beside them.
B. NODES (ids are their definitions): place:<text>, direction:<word>, line:<first direction word of the pair>@<id of its first place>, edge:<direction word>, kind:<word>, side:<role word>; per position unit:<side>:<kind>:<place>;
   relation nodes bear(<unit>,<place>) (each bearing `Placed::bearing_from` reports, once), may_move(<unit>,<place>) (`reach_from`), shut(<unit>,<place>) (for the side to move: a line the unit runs along, shut beyond its
   farthest bearing, where `why_not` says LineShut; units standing between). Plain links: on_line (index), next (by a direction), on_edge, edge_distance (steps until the chain ends under the direction), line_along, reverse,
   edge_of, unit_on, unit_kind, unit_side; relation links by, at_place, at_unit, along (the line it runs along where from and to lie on one line; none for a leap), between. may_move and shut are additions to the plan's list:
   the statements need the move relation, and the plan names the shut line.
C. Rust: cs_tactics sheet/base_graph.rs and base_statements.rs (the sheet's module directory: it already holds the other readings of `Placed`); py/src/base_graph_py.rs `cs_engine.BaseGraph` (static_part, position, dump, bearings,
   statements, open_lengths, measure); Python mirror catspace/incubator/analyst/discovery/graph_layer1.py; measure catspace/incubator/analyst/discovery/graph_layer1_measure.py. The extension was rebuilt in this worktree.
D. tests/test_plan78_52_graph_layer1.py (19) and three Rust unit tests (a board of four columns and three rows written as a description: not the game's board). Second variant: racingkings (same board by the rules, different
   movement and start; no description of its own). Edge distance per direction, counts of places, directions, lines and edge places, one relation node per bearing, byte-identical static part, ids across two builds: tested.
E. The 26 statements as counts over the graph equal `subgoal.rs` on random positions of both variants (tested). New statements, each with one line of text: units_on_edge, edge_distance_nearest, edge_distance_<direction>
   (one per direction, named from the rules' own words), goal_edge_nearest, open_pairs (pairs of its own units bearing on each other along one line with no unit standing between), and for the board open_lines,
   open_length_longest, open_length_total (the open length of a line: the longest run of places with no unit on them). Unmoved units need the game's record: left for layer 3.

## 78.53 THE GRAPH, LAYER 2: concepts mined bottom-up as patterns over the graph (SYSTEM_SPEC sections 4, 6, 11)

Serves: the first sleep's bottom-up analysis (section 4) in the form of section 11, layer 2. A measurement and a store
in a sandbox; nothing is wired into play and nothing is written to the real store.

A. WHAT A CONCEPT IS. A small connected PATTERN over the layer 1 graph: a few variables standing for units, places and
   lines, joined by the graph's own link and relation types, with the side of each unit given only as "mine" or
   "theirs" (relative to the side the pattern is counted for), and the worth of a unit given only relative to another
   unit of the pattern (less, equal, more) or as "the goal kind". No kind, place or line is named: placing is relative,
   and absoluteness enters only through edge distance (section 4).
B. BOTTOM-UP ENUMERATION by size. Size is the number of relation nodes in the pattern. All patterns of size 1 that
   occur in the games, then size 2 grown from size 1 by one more relation node sharing a variable, then size 3. A larger
   pattern is kept as its own concept only if it is not implied by its smaller parts' counts (its count is not a
   function of theirs on the fit games); otherwise it is recorded as REDUCED to them. Canonical form so the same
   pattern met two ways is one concept. The enumeration is cut by a named fuse on patterns per size, the most frequent
   kept; say how many were dropped.
C. NAMES. A concept's identity is the hash of its canonical definition. Its display name is dcN, N by order of first
   mining, written with the hash and the definition text to a concepts file under the experiment directory, with an
   empty column for our name. A separate mapping file (hash to our name) is read if present; none is written by us.
D. EVIDENCE. Each concept is counted per side per position (ours less theirs) on the kept games. On the even games:
   the sparse fit of 78.49 on the arrival target, now over the concepts (with the 26 base statements as the baseline to
   beat). On the odd games: the fit's rank correlation with bands, beside the 78.49 fit; and per kept concept its own
   correlation and weight. Print the top concepts with their definition text in plain words.
E. A CHECK BY EYE, without telling the miner: print which dcN, if any, fires on a few hand-made positions that hold a
   pinned unit, a line opened by moving the unit between, two units of theirs borne on by one of ours, and a unit of
   theirs behind their goal unit on one line. These are positions in a TEST file; the names stay in the test.

Rust for the matching and counting (hot path); the enumeration may start in Python if it is not the cost, and says so.
No oracle, no human game, no puzzle.

unit variable carries mine / theirs and its kind as the raw symbol the rules give, read from the graph. Patterns are
enumerated with kinds bound and with kinds free; a kind-bound pattern that adds nothing to its kind-free parent is
recorded as reduced to it. For the top concepts, a plain table of which kinds each side had lost 8 plies later, beside
the same table over all quiet positions. See SYSTEM_SPEC section 12. The October work on frames and intermezzos is

78.53 BUILT (branch worktree-agent-af7ecd931e7a96755, 2026-11-15 13:27 by the builder agent; stages A to E). A measurement and a concepts file in a sandbox; nothing is wired into any player, nothing is written to the real store, no oracle, no human game, no puzzle.
CHANGE FROM THE PARENT, made while this was being built (user's direction of 2026-11-15): NO WORTH in the pattern language. A unit variable carries mine / theirs, goal unit or not, and (at level 3) its KIND as the raw symbol the rules give (the layer-1 `kind:<word>` node,
   read from the graph at run time; no kind is written in any module, the source scan in the test finds none). The relative-worth attribute was built first and REMOVED, not kept beside. Kind-free and kind-bound patterns are both enumerated (levels 0, 1, 2 kind-free; level 3 the
   kind-bound children of the level 1 pattern of the same atoms) and the reduction test of a kind-bound pattern also reads its kind-free parent's count. The 26 base statements keep their worth inputs unchanged (only the baseline). No worth table enters a concept or its count.
A. THE LANGUAGE (rust/engine/tactics/src/sheet/patterns.rs; mirror catspace/incubator/analyst/discovery/graph_layer2.py; docstrings hold the full text). Variables: units, EMPTY places, lines. Atoms are the layer-1 relation nodes: bear(u,t,l), move(u,t,l) (may_move),
   shut(u,t,l,b) (the one unit b between), the line absent where the relation follows none; two atoms naming one object share the variable. Size = the number of relation nodes. Levels of what is said of a unit, relative to the side counted for: 0 mine/theirs; 1 + goal unit of its side or not;
   2 level 1 + on an edge (nearest edge distance 0: the only place absoluteness enters, as a small class); 3 level 1 + the kind. SHUT: the shut relation nodes exist for the SIDE TO MOVE ONLY (why_not answers for it alone). Extending base_graph to the other side through `Placed::without` was tried
   (`Static::first_blocker_shuts`, kept as a diagnostic, NOT in the graph): the game refuses the hypothetical board where taking the blocker off leaves the side not to move exposed to a line, so it misses exactly the cases that matter; `BaseGraph.first_blocker_check` measured the gap against why_not on the
   mover (printed in the test: 357 relations by why_not against 331 by the hypothetical board over 3 random games). So shut patterns are counted for the mover only, and only with exactly one unit between; every other atom is read for both sides. A relation holding two lines takes its first.
B. ENUMERATION (Python orchestrates, Rust matches and counts: `cs_engine.BaseGraph.pattern_freq`, `pattern_count`, ESU enumeration of connected sets of relation nodes over rayon-free std threads). Size 1: every pattern found; size k grown from the kept patterns of size k-1 (a candidate needs one connected part of one
   relation node less in the kept set). CANONICAL FORM: variables renamed by first appearance, the least encoding over the orders of the atoms, then over swapping mine and theirs (a mirrored pattern is the same concept, its sign flips; a self-mirror counts nothing); tested: the same set of atoms in any order is one key (Rust),
   no definition appears under two keys (Python), the engine's counts equal a brute-force matcher over the layer-1 Graph (catspace/incubator/analyst/discovery/graph_layer2_match.py) on up to 9 positions and 40 sampled patterns of sizes 1-3 and every level, a position and its colour mirror have equal values.
   THE FUSE (named, not tuned): FUSE = 100 patterns kept per size and per level, the most supported on the fit rows (support = fit rows it occurs in), ties by key; a budget of the fit's columns (about 1000), chosen before the run. THE REDUCTION TEST (stated before it was run): on the fit games, split by game id (id mod 4 = 0 half A, the others half B), a pattern of size 2 or 3 is REDUCED
   when the vector of the counts of its kept parts (for a kind-bound pattern also its kind-free parent) determines its count on half A (no vector with two counts) and every vector seen on half B was seen on A with the same count, counts per side per position; no threshold. Reduced patterns are in reduced.tsv with their parts, not concepts.
C. NAMES. Hash = sha256 of the canonical definition text; dcN by order of mining (size, level, support); concepts.tsv (dcN, hash, size, level, definition in plain words, our name EMPTY), concept_keys.json (the engine key and encoding of each, for evaluation), reduced.tsv; a mapping.tsv (hash, our name) is READ if present (none exists; no code of ours writes it).
D. Games, reads and table as 78.49/78.48 (games_s5016_n500, reads_fuse5000.jsonl, opp_table_n500.npz), even games fit, odd test, the quiet rows of 78.49; the fit of 78.49 over the 26 base statements (same code, same penalty path: the line is reproduced exactly), over the concepts alone and over both; the concept fits use a SHORTENED penalty path
   (30 penalties down to 1 pct of the largest, `fit_wide`) because the full path over about a thousand columns did not finish in reasonable time (a first attempt with 3500 columns on 50 games ran 13 minutes of wall before it was stopped): a coarser fit than the base statements' own. One run, directional.
E. tests/test_plan78_53_graph_layer2.py (13 tests; the concepts of the test file's own mining are from random play and never saw the hand positions), added to scripts/gate.py. The hand positions live in the test file; the assertion is only that some concept of size 2 or 3 tells each position from its twin; it also prints which dcN fire, for the test's own throwaway concept set and for the concepts file of this run.
   Reading, directional: in the run's concepts no concept that fires on the pinned-unit position is specific to a pin (the three that hold there and not in the twin are generic combinations of bearings and moves along lines); the positions with a shut line by an own unit fire shut concepts (dc288, dc303, dc325 and others); of the position with two units of theirs borne on by one of ours only the first six of the concepts that hold there and not in the twin were read, and they are bearings among own units and empty places off the edge, none naming two targets of theirs; nothing was written to make a named tactic fire.
Timings (one run, 10 threads): the mining, counting and reduction are in Rust except the reduction test (Python, single thread). Output kept at artifacts/experiments/graph_layer2_78_53/games_s5016_n500/ (obs.txt, concepts.tsv, concept_keys.json, reduced.tsv; never staged).

78.53 READ (2026-11-15, by the main agent, merged as 7a2cce4e; the 78.52, 78.53 and 78.49 test files pass on main after the rebuild, 59 tests; the engine gate was not run).
What was built is a correct pattern matcher over the layer-1 graph with hash identity, dcN names and an empty name column. What it found is not yet a vocabulary:
1. SELECTION WAS BY SUPPORT. The fuse kept the 100 most frequent patterns per size and level and dropped the rest untested (at size 3 level 3, 100 of 55036). The most frequent patterns are plain bearings of own units on own units and empty places. A pin, a fork or a line through to a second unit is rare by nature and was cut before it was looked at. The builder's numbers (obs.txt of the run) show the concepts beside the 26 statements with overlapping bands at every horizon; one run, a direction only.
2. THE OUTCOME WAS READ PER SIDE, NOT PER UNIT. The lost-unit table counts kinds lost by each side 8 plies later. It does not say what became of the units the pattern binds, which is the question of SYSTEM_SPEC section 12.
3. SHUT LINES FOR THE MOVER ONLY. The line through one unit to a second is known only for the side to move, so a line held by the side that has just moved is invisible. The hand position of that kind could not be shown.
The next plan answers the three.


PLAN 78.54: WHAT BECOMES OF EACH UNIT A CONCEPT BINDS (SYSTEM_SPEC sections 11 layer 2 and 12; pieces 3 and 7). Written 2026-11-15 by the main agent. A measurement and a concepts file in a sandbox; nothing wired into a player; no oracle, no human game, no puzzle; nothing written to the real store.
Purpose, in the user's words: "learn what happens when each piece is left behind"; "query the statistics in this unique condition where these unique tactics exist"; a static value is the baseline and the concept gives a correction.
A. LINES THROUGH ONE UNIT, BOTH SIDES. A relation node for "u bears on b along line l, and the next occupied place on l beyond b is t", for either side, read from the static step relation and the bear relations of layer 1 without a hypothetical board. It must be principled: the unit is one that continues along that line (state how this is known from the rules or the graph, not from a list). Check against the rules' own answer for the side to move over random games and print agreement as OBS counts. Limits stated.
B. UNIT FATES ALONG A GAME, in Rust, game-free. Follow each unit from position to position by the difference of consecutive graphs. For a unit present at ply t and a horizon h (4, 8, 16): STAYED (same place), MOVED (same side and kind elsewhere, taken as the same unit), TAKEN (gone and a unit of the other side stands on its place; record the taker's kind), OTHER (gone otherwise, or changed kind; counted and printed, never guessed). Base rates per kind, per side to move or not, over all quiet positions.
C. FATE PER VARIABLE OF A PATTERN. For every match of a pattern, the fate of each unit variable at each horizon. A pattern's record is, per variable, the rate of each fate beside the base rate of units of the same kind and same side-to-move state (for kind-free patterns, the base mixed by the kinds actually bound).
D. SELECTION BY DEPARTURE, NOT SUPPORT. Candidates: all patterns of sizes 1 to 3 with at least a stated minimum support on half A (state the minimum before the run; the fuse by support is removed or raised far enough that rare patterns are read; say what was still cut). Score on half A: the largest departure of a variable's TAKEN rate from its base, in standard errors. Keep those that hold their sign and at least half their size on half B. Reduction: a pattern whose departure is explained by a part of one relation less (same variable, departure within noise of the part's) is recorded as reduced to it. Report the kept concepts on the odd games (the test half), sorted by departure, with definition, support, rates and base. concepts.tsv as in 78.53 with the fate columns added; the name column stays empty; the mapping file is read if present.
E. BASELINE AND CORRECTION. For each kept concept: the net of kinds lost (theirs less ours) h plies later where the concept holds, less the same net over all quiet positions with the same side to move. This is the correction of section 12, printed as counts by kind; no worth table multiplies it.
F. CHECK BY EYE. The four hand positions of 78.53 E and the one that needed the side not to move: which kept concepts fire, and what their records say. The test asserts only that the both-sides line relation is present where it should be and absent in the twin.
G. Optional, if time: the 78.49 fit with the kept concepts as columns beside the 26 statements, same split and bands.
Rust for following units, matching and counting. Mirror in Python for one position pair. Tests: the tracker against hand sequences of positions (a move, a taking, a unit changing kind, two units of one kind swapping roles is counted as it falls and stated); the line relation against a brute walk; fates of a pattern against the readable matcher on a few games; a source scan that no module names a unit or a place. All cores. Short run on 50 games before the 500.
NOT in this plan, next as 78.55: the sequences inside a frame with their fate records and the pass that links two frames, carried over from fates.py (Fate, Outcome, outcomes_table, with_passes, compose), Race.lean (withPass, frame_sound_pass, far_stays_off) and waiting.rs, onto the graph and game-free. The statistics of this plan say which frames matter; 78.55 reasons about what can happen in them.

78.54 RULES (stated by the builder agent on 2026-11-15, BEFORE the 500-game run; the same text is the docstring of catspace/incubator/analyst/discovery/unit_fates_measure.py). The 50-game run before it only exercised the code; its numbers are not used.
Rows: the quiet positions of 78.49. Halves by game id: A = id mod 4 = 0 and B = id mod 4 = 2 (together the even games, the fit half of 78.49), T = the odd games (the test half). A selects, B confirms, T reports; a half's base rates are taken over that half's own quiet positions.
MINIMUM SUPPORT: MIN_SUPPORT = 30 quiet positions of half A that a pattern occurs on. The fuse by support of 78.53 is gone: sizes 1 to 3, all four levels, every pattern with that support (a pattern's parts occur wherever it does, so growth from the parts loses none). Still cut: a pattern with fewer than 30 positions on A, and a pattern none of whose cells is readable.
CELL = (pattern, unit variable, horizon of 4, 8 or 16). READABLE on A: MIN_CELL_N = 30 distinct units bound, over positions, in at least MIN_CELL_GAMES = 10 games. DEPARTURE d = the taken rate less the base rate of being taken for the kinds and side-to-move states of the units actually bound (the mean of the units' own residuals). STANDARD ERROR from the games' summed residuals, not the units' (a unit stays in many rows): se = sqrt(sum over games of (the game's residual sum)^2) / n; z = d / se.
SCORE of a pattern on A = the largest |z| over its readable cells; that cell is its SELECTED CELL.
CONFIRMED on B: the selected cell has at least MIN_B_N = 15 units on B, d of the same sign, and |d| at least half of its size on A. B is not searched for a better cell.
REDUCED (on A): a confirmed pattern is reduced to a part (one relation node less, connected, holding the variable) when |d_pattern - d_part| <= 2 se_pattern at the same horizon, the variable matched through the canonical variable maps the matcher records. Reduced patterns go to reduced.tsv with their part; they are not concepts.
KEPT = confirmed and not reduced. Reported on T, sorted by |z| of the selected cell on T. A reference line, not a filter: sqrt(2 ln N) for N readable cells on A. Concepts whose selected cell on T has the same units' fates as a higher ranked one are marked (same_units_as), not removed.
The line through one unit (A) needs a profile of the kinds; it is learned from the bear nodes of every position of the first 50 games of the file (a kind and heading that never bears two steps away in them is read as not continuing).


78.54 BUILT (branch worktree-agent-ac7e6cae9980da26e, 2026-11-15 by the builder agent; stages A to F; G, the 78.49 fit with the kept concepts as columns, NOT built). A measurement and a concepts file in a sandbox; nothing is wired into any player, nothing is written to rules/learned or data/derived/snapshots; no oracle, no human game, no puzzle. The rules of selection are the "78.54 RULES" note above, stated before the run; they were not changed after it.
A. THE LINE THROUGH ONE UNIT, BOTH SIDES. Layer 1 has a new relation node `through(<unit>,<place>)` (base_graph.rs): the unit bears on a unit b along a line (a bear node), the unit's kind CONTINUES along that line family in that heading, and the next place beyond b that holds a unit is the node's place; links by, at_place, at_unit, along, between (b). No hypothetical board. HOW A UNIT IS KNOWN TO CONTINUE: from the bear nodes alone. `Static::learn` marks (kind, line direction, heading) as continuing when some unit of that kind, in some position of a sample, bears on a place two or more steps away along a line of that family (the places between are passed over). The sample is every position of the first 50 games of the file. No list of units or movements is written; the 16 entries it found are in the first OBS line below. Limits: it is a sample (a kind and heading never seen bearing two steps away reads as not continuing); a unit that jumps others (more than one unit between actor and end) gets no node; a relation holding two lines takes the first in patterns. In patterns.rs it is the atom through(u, t, l, b), item type 3; the matcher mirror graph_layer2_match.py and the brute walk unit_fates.through_walk read it from the graph and equal the engine (tested).
   AGREEMENT with the rules' own answer for the side to move (shut nodes, `why_not` = LineShut, one unit between, end place held by the other side; the rules say nothing when it is held by the unit's own side, so those are left out of both): see the OBS "A agreement" line. For the side NOT to move there is no rules answer; the line is tested present in the hand positions and absent in the twins (tests/test_plan78_54_unit_fates.py), and counted by side in the "A through relations held" line.
B. THE TRACKER (rust/engine/tactics/src/sheet/fates.rs), game-free, by the difference of consecutive unit lists: same (owner, kind, place) stays; gone and the same owner and kind appeared = moved (several of one owner and kind paired in list order and COUNTED: the plies' units paired that way are in the tracker OBS line); gone and a unit of another owner stands on its place = TAKEN by that unit's kind; gone otherwise (nobody there, or an owner and kind not matched: a change of kind) = OTHER. A fate at horizon h follows the chain: taken or other ends it; alive after h steps is STAYED where the unit stands where it began, else MOVED; a horizon past the end of the game has no fate. Limits: a unit that goes and returns is STAYED; two units of one owner and kind that swap places in one step read as staying; a taking by en passant or a promotion reads as OTHER (counted, never guessed). Python mirror unit_fates.py; Rust unit tests for pairing; the test compares them on hand sequences (a taking, a change of kind, a return) and random games.
C/D. FATE PER VARIABLE, SELECTION BY DEPARTURE. Rust: `fate_cells` (per pattern, variable, horizon: units bound, fates by class, expected by class from the base rates of the same kinds and side-to-move states, and per-game residual sums so the standard error is from games); `pattern_mine` (mining by minimum support, every part must be in the set below, the maps of the variables into the parts); `fate_base`. Measure: catspace/incubator/analyst/discovery/unit_fates_measure.py (reuses split_rows, layout, goal_kind_of, quiet_indices, read_mapping, canonical_text/hash). concepts.tsv has 78.53's columns, the name column empty, then the selected variable and horizon, support, units / taken rate / base / z on A, B and T, and same_units_as. Output under artifacts/experiments/unit_fates_78_54/games_s5016_n500/ (obs.txt, concepts.tsv, concept_keys.json, reduced.tsv, fate_records.tsv: every variable, horizon and class on T; hand_positions_obs.txt). Never staged.
E. BASELINE AND CORRECTION: printed as "E dcN" lines for the distinct top 15: the net of kinds lost (theirs less ours) h plies later where the concept holds (for each side that holds it: the side to move, or the other, mirrored), less the same net over all quiet positions with the same side to move; per instance, by kind, test half; no worth table. A concept that holds for both sides in one position at once (a mutual bearing) nets to zero by construction.
F. THE FIVE HAND POSITIONS (the four of 78.53 E and the pinned unit with the other side to move; the one that needed the side not to move is the fourth): the test prints which kept concepts of the run fire and their records (hand_positions_obs.txt); the through relation is a node of the graph in all but the leaping unit's position (where it is correctly absent) and absent in every twin. The test asserts only that, and prints the rest.

Reading, directional (one run, one set of games; no verdict): (1) The units a pattern binds depart from their kind's base rate of being taken by far more than the plain bearings of 78.53 did: the top concepts are mutual bearings (my unit bears on theirs and theirs may move to mine) where my unit is taken at about three quarters within 4 plies against about 6 pct for pawns in general, mostly by a pawn, i.e. an exchange coming; the effect is in the standard errors from games, and holds on B and T. (2) The kept list is large and highly redundant (see the counts of reduced, same-units); the top is not a vocabulary of tactics; concepts with the line through one unit are among the kept (concepts.tsv, the words 'going on past it'); one, dc22 (two parallel lines of own units), is in the top 15. (3) The corrections of kinds lost are small per instance (a few hundredths of a pawn at most), the largest being a pawn for the mutual-bearing concepts; many top concepts have corrections that are zero by construction (they hold for both sides at once). (4) most of the confirmed patterns are reduced to a part under the stated rule (see the counts of confirmed, reduced and kept above); the rule is lenient where a cell has few units (the standard error is wide), so reduction here says 'no departure beyond noise from the part's', not that the part explains it.

78.54 READ (2026-11-15, by the main agent, merged as e1f87713; the 78.52, 78.53 and 78.54 test files pass on main after the rebuild, 46 tests; the engine gate was not run; stage G was not built).
What holds, from the run's own lines (obs.txt, concepts.tsv, hand_positions_obs.txt of unit_fates_78_54/games_s5016_n500; one run, directions only):
1. The line through one unit now exists for both sides and agreed with the rules' own answer on every relation of the sample for the side to move. How a unit is known to continue along a line is learned from a sample of positions, so a kind never seen bearing two steps away reads as not continuing.
2. Following units works: a small share of steps fell in OTHER, none were ambiguous pairings on these games.
3. Selection by departure finds different things from selection by support. The top of the list is the exchange: two units of opposite sides that can take each other, where the bound unit is taken within 4 plies far above its base. The line through their unit to a second of theirs (dc3018) shows the unit between taken at about twice its base.
What does not hold yet:
4. TAKEN CONFLATES. A unit that takes and is then retaken reads as TAKEN, the same as a unit lost for nothing. The fate needs TOOK (what it took, before it was taken) for the record to tell an exchange from a loss.
5. THE LIST IS NOT A VOCABULARY. 36152 kept, most of them one relation seen at several levels or with an idle relation added. The reduction test ("within noise of a part") is too weak with these counts. To be redone as: a concept is kept only for what it adds over its best part.
6. THE CORRECTIONS ARE NEAR ZERO for the top concepts, by construction for the mutual ones (they hold for both sides at once) and because an exchange changes nothing net.
7. THIS IS WHAT THE PLAYERS DID, NOT WHAT CAN HAPPEN. The statistic says an exposed unit tends to be taken. It does not say what each side can force inside the frame. That is the October work of SYSTEM_SPEC 12.1, and it is the next plan.


PLAN 78.55: THE FRAME, ITS SEQUENCES AND FATE RECORDS, AND THE PASS THAT LINKS TWO FRAMES, ON THE GRAPH (SYSTEM_SPEC sections 11 layer 3, 12 and 12.1; pieces 2, 3 and 7). Those modules are bound to one game; this plan is their game-free form in rust/engine over Placed and the layer-1 graph. A sandbox measurement; nothing wired into a player; no oracle, no human game, no puzzle; nothing in the real store.
0. TOOK. The tracker of 78.54 records, for a unit, what it took and when before its own end. Fate classes become STAYED, MOVED, TOOK (kinds taken), TAKEN (by kind), and their combinations in order. Small; done first because E reads it.
A. THE FRAME. From a seed (the units and places a concept match binds, or any set of unit and place nodes): the frame is those units and places plus every unit that bears on a place of the frame, to closure or to a stated bound, as square_frame does. A frame is a graph node (`frame:<hash of its sorted members>`) with links to its members. Two frames are IN CONTACT when they share a unit or a place, or a unit of one bears on a place of the other; frames in contact are joined and read as one (the October lesson: reading one frame's threats inside another fails).
B. SEQUENCES INSIDE THE FRAME. Moves of frame units to frame places, sides alternating, each side allowed to PASS (a pass stands for a move outside the frame; the Lean lemmas withPass and frame_sound_pass say when that is sound, and the test mirrors their statement). Legality comes from the game through Placed, never from a rule written here; say how a pass is made on a real position and what it cannot represent (a side with no move outside the frame, a side in a forced state). A fuse on positions; a line cut by the fuse ends UNREAD and is counted, never guessed.
C. THE OUTCOME is a fate record: per unit of the frame, alive or taken, by which unit, at which ply, standing where. The table of all outcomes of the frame with the line that reaches each.
D. WHAT EACH SIDE CAN FORCE, WITH NO WORTH TABLE. Outcomes are compared only by inclusion: one outcome is at least as good for a side as another when that side loses no unit the other outcome keeps and the opponent loses every unit it loses there. What a side can force is then a SET of outcomes none of which is beaten (kept as a set; never collapsed to a number). A CLAIM is "this side can force an outcome in which unit x of theirs is taken and none of ours is" and the like, stated over fates.
E. THE PASS COUNT AND THE CONDITIONAL CLAIM. with_passes: the forceable set as a function of who is to move and of how many passes each side may spend. A claim that holds only if the opponent passes once is a THREAT; a claim that holds only after one named board change (a unit of ours arriving on a named place, read by trying each move of ours into or onto the frame) is a CONDITIONAL CLAIM, and its condition is a subgoal. These are layer-3 nodes: `claim:<frame>:<statement>`, `condition:<claim>:<change>`, linked to the frame, the units and the place. This is the waiting-frame idea of waiting.rs in game-free form.
F. TWO FRAMES AND THE INTERMEZZO. compose: for two frames not in contact, a pass in one is a move in the other. The forceable set of the pair is computed from the two pass tables, and CHECKED against the joint read of the union frame on sampled positions; agreement and disagreement are printed as counts, with the disagreeing cases kept for reading. No Lean theorem covers this composition (12.1), so it is reported as checked per position, not proved, and nothing downstream may treat it as proved.
G. THE MEASURE. On the quiet positions of the test half of the 500 games, frames seeded from the top concepts of 78.54 (stated before the run: which and how many): (1) cost: positions read per frame, share UNREAD, time per position; (2) do the reasoned fates foretell the observed ones: the rate at which a unit was in fact taken within 4 and 8 plies where the frame says it can be forced taken for nothing, where it says it is safe, and the base (from stage 0 fates); (3) the same for conditional claims: how often the named change was played, and what followed; (4) the F agreement counts. No verdicts from one run.
H. CHECK BY EYE. The five hand positions of 78.54 plus one with two frames far apart and one move in between: the frames found, the forceable sets, the claims and conditional claims in words.
Rust for frames, sequences and the tables; a readable Python mirror for one frame; tests against the mirror, against fates.py on positions both can read (where they differ, say which is right and why), and the source scan. All cores. Short run before long run. Stages 0 to E are the core; F, G, H follow in that order and a stage not reached is said so plainly.
Owed after this, not in it: the reduction test redone as "what a concept adds over its best part"; the fit of 78.49 with claims and conditional claims as columns; the correction to the baseline read from forceable sets rather than from played games.

Lean states the lemma with the claim-holder having no pass and the other side passing; here a side that has no frame move takes a FORCED pass (frame_sound with the pass among our moves, `hours` read on the real position: a pass is made only when some move outside the frame leaves the frame's projection as it was).
A THE FRAME: seed units and places; P = the seed's places and its units' places; members = units standing on P, units that bear on P (layer-1 bear nodes), and to a fixed point units that bear on P through a member (layer-1 `through` nodes); more than 12 members is refused and counted. Node id `frame:<hash of sorted members and places>`. IN CONTACT (shared unit or place, or a unit of one bears on a place of the other): joined and closed again. LIMIT, found by the test: the engine sees one unit behind one unit; for a battery of three the October lifting rule (and the mirror) finds the third and the engine does not. The lifting rule is right (it is the definition: a unit that bears once the frame's units leave); the engine's is a narrower, cheaper reading (test_a_battery_of_three...). LIMIT 2: when a join is refused for size, the frames left are not joined among themselves (66 of the 258 kept composition disagreements show a unit in both frames: this).
B SEQUENCES. A move of the frame: a legal move of the game (Game::moves) of a member onto a place of P, or a PASS. Pass = `Game::pass` (the same position, the other side to move, nothing played) AND realisable: some legal move of a non-member leaves the frame's projection (member cells, closure from P) as it was. It cannot represent: a side that must answer a threat to its goal unit or a game that has ended (the game refuses a pass; counted), a side whose every legal move changes the frame (counted `pass_unrealisable`), and what the game drops with a pass (a right that lapses). THE LEAVE: a member moving to a place outside P, or a non-member move that changes the projection, is one option for the side NOT being read; the line ends with the units as they stand (nothing is claimed beyond it). Consequence, stated: a unit that can step away is never forced taken unless it is taken at once or cannot move; claims are thin by design. Depth = one ply per member plus one (BOUNDED, counted); fuse = positions read per reading (UNREAD, counted, valued as the worst for the side read). A side with no frame move and no pass is STUCK: the worst for the side read, as it stands for the other.
C OUTCOME: per member alive (standing where) or taken (by which member, at which ply); `outcomes_table` gives the distinct outcomes with the first line reaching each (hand position tables in hand_positions_obs.txt).
D NO WORTH. An outcome is (members the side read loses, members the other loses). One is at least as good as another when the side read loses no member the other keeps and the other side loses every member it loses there. What a side can force = the set of guaranteed outcomes no other guarantee beats (an antichain, kept as a set; unit ids only in every output). At the reading side's node: the unbeaten of the options; at the other side's: the unbeaten of the meets (union of its losses, intersection of the other's). Claims: `take_free` (unit taken, none of the reading side's lost), `take_any`, `safe` (not taken within the frame's horizon).
E PASS COUNT. The forceable set is read per (side read, who moves first, passes each side may spend: 0, 1, 2, every ply). Sound form = the reading side spends none, the other may pass at every ply. Status: forced (holds in the sound form at the root); threat (side read not to move, holds with it to move, i.e. the other passed once); waiting (side read to move, holds with one pass of its own); conditional (not forced, holds after one arrival of a unit of the side to move on or onto the frame, found by trying each such move; the condition is the arrival (kind, place)). Layer-3 node kinds added: `frame`, `claim` (`claim:<frame>:<role>:<claim>:<unit id>`, only for a claim that holds in some form), `condition` (`condition:<claim>:arrive:<kind>@<place>`); links has_unit, has_place, in_frame, about_unit, at_place, condition_of, arrives_at, arriving_kind. Only the side to move's arrivals are tried (the other side's by its pass are the threat status).
F COMPOSITION: for two frames not in contact, the sound-form sets of each frame, the guarantees united. NO LEAN THEOREM COVERS IT; CHECKED per position, not proved, and nothing downstream may treat it as proved. Run against the joint read of the union frame (pairs of at most 9 members together, fuse 5000; every 5th row with two frames apart).

HAND POSITIONS (hand_positions_obs.txt; in words): (1) the pinned knight, white to move: the frame holds the rook and the knight; white forces the knight taken for nothing; black has no frame move (a pass is forced and nothing can be claimed for black). (2) the line opened by moving the unit between: the frame is the two own units; no taking is forced either way; both can leave. (3) the fork: white forces either the queen or the rook taken, in both lines losing the knight (the rook or queen retakes): taking and losing, not free; both `take_any` forced. (4) a unit behind their goal unit, black to move: black has no frame move; nothing is claimed. (5) the pinned unit, black to move: as (1) with the same claims for white. (6) the juicer defended by a rook: white forces the bishop taken, not for nothing (the rook retakes), as fates.py says; black forces the rook safe. (7) the conditional: a blocked pawn that cannot leave; `take_free` and `take_any` are `conditional` on a rook arriving on a5 (the only arrival). (8) two frames far apart (knight/bishop/rook and rook/knight/pawn): the composition says white wins both the bishop and the knight (losing the first knight and the rook); the joint read says one or the other: COMPOSED MORE (the tempo each exchange costs); for black they are equal.

78.55 READ (2026-11-15, by the main agent, merged as 183e272b; the 78.52 to 78.55 test files pass on main after the rebuild, 75 tests; the engine gate was started at this commit and its line is appended below when it ends).
What holds, from the run's own lines (obs.txt, class_table.tsv, disagreements.txt, hand_positions_obs.txt of frames_78_55/games_s5016_n500; one run, directions only):
1. THE REASONED CLASSES ORDER THE OBSERVED FATES. A unit the frame says can be forced taken for nothing was in fact taken far above its base; a unit it says is safe was taken below its base; threat and contested fall between. This is the first time a reasoned statement about one unit, with no worth table and no oracle, has been checked against what then happened.
2. Layer 3 nodes exist: frame, claim, condition, with deterministic ids. The fate record, the outcome table, the pass, and comparison by inclusion are carried over from October and tested against a readable mirror and against fates.py.
What does not hold yet:
3. THE INFORMATIVE CLASS IS TINY. About one member unit in a thousand is LOST and most are SAFE. The cause is the LEAVE rule: the side not being read may end the line by moving a member away, so nothing is forced against a unit that can step off. That is the sound reading of the Lean lemma, and it throws away the chase (the unit steps off and is still lost where it lands).
4. NO CONDITIONAL CLAIM AROSE on the games, for the same reason. The one hand position shows the machinery.
5. THE COMPOSITION OF TWO FRAMES IS WRONG ABOUT TEMPO. In the kept disagreements the composed read often claims both gains where the joint read gives one or the other. That is the October lesson again: a move spent in one frame is a pass in the other, and the composition as built does not charge it everywhere. Two more faults read from disagreements.txt: a STUCK line is written as every member lost, units of both sides in one list, which then compares as an outcome; and a unit present in both frames appears twice (the join after a size refusal is not finished). So the agreement counts of stage F are not usable as they stand.
6. FRAMES ARE TOO LARGE AND TOO DEAR. Over eight members on average, a fifth refused for size, about two seconds per position. October's frames were a few units around one square.
7. The closure sees one unit behind one unit; the lifting rule of fates.py sees further and is the right definition.


PLAN 78.56: A GAME-FREE CORE FOR THE LEAN LIBRARY (SYSTEM_SPEC 12.2; AGENTS rule 11). Written 2026-11-15 by the main agent on Kaveh's word that the October chess-bound Lean work be considered for generalization, the race among it. Lean only; no Rust, no Python engine code, no extension rebuild.
A. BUILD STATE FIRST. Find out whether lean/ideas builds today (lake build, offline; do not update or fetch dependencies). Report the state before changing anything. If it does not build for a reason outside this plan, stop and report.
B. THE CORE. A directory of files that import no chess (Ideas/Core/ or the name that fits the project), holding the already generic results MOVED there with their proofs unchanged: Reach and forced_by_measure and its companions (ForcedByMeasure.lean is already free of imports), race_sound and race_first, frame_sound, withPass and frame_sound_pass, the Game structure and its generic lemmas, neglect / neglect_step / frame_of_diff, claim_mono and the judge and route lemmas of Forcing.lean, the generic half of Draws.lean with the move count as a parameter. The old names stay available where they were (re-export or a one-line alias) so nothing that cites them breaks; docs/LEAN_INDEX.md is rebuilt.
C. THE BOARD STRUCTURE. One structure over an arbitrary type of places and of units: a static step relation, kinds, sides, a goal unit per side, bear, and the five properties of 12.2 (touch, line, footprint, goal unit, distance) as fields or hypotheses, each stated once. The lemma that shortest path in a kind's step relation changes by at most one per step.
D. RESTATE, in this order, stopping where the time runs out and saying where: far_stays_off, far_not_bearing, deny_sound, plan_sound, overload_sound over places (a rename; proofs should carry); path_lemma, attack_unchanged, lost_path_lemma; frame_unchanged; discovered_attack and skewer_attack over a `through` relation; checkmate_of_unmeetable_check as "the goal unit is borne on and nothing meets it".
E. CHESS AS AN INSTANCE. Show the chess kernel satisfies the structure from lemmas that exist, and recover at least one old chess theorem from its generic form as a check that nothing was lost. No `sorry` anywhere in the core; an instance field that cannot be proved in the time is left out and named, never assumed.
F. NOT in this plan: the passer race (needs a relation the graph lacks: a unit advancing toward a place where it changes kind; write down in the note what that relation would have to say), the exchange law (never proved; compares by worth), a theorem for composing two frames (wanted, and the 78.55 read shows the composition as built is wrong about tempo; state the theorem that WOULD be needed, with the tempo charged, as a comment or an unproved statement kept outside the core and marked as such).
Proofs by reasoning, never by enumeration over boards. Tests: the Python mirror tests that cite the moved theorems still pass.

PLAN 78.57: THE FRAME READ REPAIRED (SYSTEM_SPEC 11 layer 3, 12). Written 2026-11-15 by the main agent from the 78.55 read. A sandbox measurement as before.
A. SMALL FRAMES. A frame is the seed's units and places plus the units that bear on those places, with the closure through a member done by the lifting rule of fates.py (bears once the frame's units leave), and NO further ring. A frame over a stated size is SPLIT at the seed (the seed's own units and the places between them) and the split counted, not refused.
B. THE UNIT THAT STEPS OFF. In place of the LEAVE that ends a line: when a member moves off the frame, the read follows it for a stated small number of steps with the frame moved to where it lands (the frame of the same seed pattern re-closed there), under the same fuse. A line is ended as LEFT only when the fuse or the step bound says so, and LEFT is counted apart from SAFE. Say what this does to soundness against frame_sound_pass: a claim reached through a follow is a claim about the larger read, and is marked so.
C. STUCK AND SHARED UNITS. A STUCK line is its own word, never an outcome with every member lost. Frames left in contact after a size refusal are split or joined, never both read with a unit in common.
D. THE TEMPO IN THE COMPOSITION. compose charges every move: a line that spends a move in one frame spends a pass in the other at that ply. Checked against the joint read as in 78.55 F, with the same counts, and the disagreeing cases read by hand for the first twenty.
E. CONDITIONAL CLAIMS. With B in place, the arrival of one unit of ours on or onto the frame, for both sides. How often the named change was played, and what followed.
F. THE MEASURE of 78.55 G again, same seeds, same rows, old numbers beside new: share of member units in each class, the observed fates per class, cost per frame and per position.
Short run before long run; fuses stated before the run.

So those are the only options you analyze"; "the questioner ... should know to ask the right questions and not spend an eternity in the frame"; "the frame should not be bound to the square. The frame should be bound to the piece ... if the piece moves ... now it's in a new location ... can we trap it? Can we chase it?"; the October chase and cornering work "need[s] to be looked into, because otherwise we will be rehashing those exact same problems"; "damaging the structure ... is a sub-goal in itself".

WHAT OCTOBER ALREADY LEARNED ABOUT THE CHASE (read before building: plans 52.10 to 52.13, 52.17, 52.18, 52.23, 59, 61, 64.1, 72.3, 72.9, 72.10 in this file, and the code they name; the BUILT note says what was carried and what was not):
 1. The cost of a chase is the NUMBER OF QUESTIONS. After each reply the old chase re-asked the whole board, about 25 questions where one was needed (72.10). After a move ask three: does the claim still hold on what the move touched; what new threats of theirs pass through what it touched; what delays do they have off the frame.
 2. A chase needs an END that is a reason, not a depth: a taking or another move that cannot be undone is progress; otherwise "did we get closer or are we going in circles" (52.23, the capture clock; the irreversible-move note of 2026-10-22). More forcing moves that only give the chased unit more room are not progress (52.17, the region kill).
 3. A static balance is never a result until the OTHER side has been asked from there (52.13: a false claim credited a gain with no question from their side).
 4. Whether a unit is trapped is read on QUIET routes only; read under a forcing move, everything looks trapped (52.10 bug).
 5. Keep searching only while no move in hand keeps the status (plan 59). A move that holds is the stop.
 6. A slow plan dies to a NAMED in-between move of theirs, and the kill should carry that name (the tempo note of 2026-10-21). A tempo is worth what the other side proves with it (72.3).
 7. Answers are kept with the relations they read; an unchanged read set means the same answer (52.12, 52.19).

A'. THE FRAME IS BOUND TO UNITS. A frame is a set of units (the seed's, plus those that bear on them or on the places between them, by the lifting rule). Its places are derived from where those units stand and bear NOW. When a member moves, the frame is the same frame at the new position: its places are derived again, and units that now bear on it join. Identity is the seed's units, so a claim about a frame survives the move.
B'. THE READ BY QUESTIONS, in place of the table of all sequences. For the side to move in a frame:
   Q0 what stands to be lost here if nothing is done (their takings that are pure gain by inclusion).
   Q1 the candidate moves, which are ONLY: a taking that is not a pure loss; a move that answers Q0 (move the unit away, put a unit between, add a bearing, take the taker); a move that makes a new Q0 for the other side. Every other move of a member is not asked about.
   Q2 for each candidate, the other side's answer, asked the same way from their side (lesson 3). A candidate that ends in a pure loss for the mover is PRUNED, and the prune is kept with its reason (which unit is lost, to which reply).
   Stop as soon as a candidate keeps the status (lesson 5). The chase of a unit that steps away goes on only under lesson 2.
   Comparison stays by inclusion (pure loss and pure gain need no worth). An UNEQUAL trade is neither; it is reported as a trade of kinds and left open in this plan. The baseline that would settle it is the statistic of SYSTEM_SPEC 12, not a hand table, and is not built here.
   Count and print: questions asked per frame, positions read, candidates pruned by reason.
E'. THE PRUNED BRANCH AND THE OTHER FRAME. A pruned candidate is reopened only by a claim in ANOTHER frame that the same move serves: the move loses a unit here and, as a move, is the arrival or the forcing move of a claim there. That pair is the conditional link between frames, written as nodes: `prune:<frame>:<move>:<reason>` and a link `reopened_by` to the claim. The tempo is charged as in stage D: the gain there counts only if it is still forced after the other side has taken here. Arrivals for conditional claims are tried for both sides, and a claim may name a change of structure as its gain only as a statement the graph can make (for instance: a unit of theirs no longer borne on by any of theirs), never a named shape.
TRAP. One question for any unit, the goal unit included: on quiet routes, has it a place to go that is not a pure loss (lesson 4). The goal unit's case is the game's own end. The October cornering lemmas are looked up in docs/LEAN_INDEX.md and mirrored where they apply; nothing new is claimed proved.
F stands, with the question counts added: old 78.55 numbers beside new, per class and per frame.

WHAT THE SHORT RUN SAYS.
1. THE AIM OF A FEW QUESTIONS IS NOT MET. Questions per frame 2244.8; 149 of 1711 frames took 30 questions or fewer, 816 took over 1000.
2. WHERE THE QUESTIONS GO: questions that follow a TAKING are 0.785 of all; a threatened member stepping away 0.103; adds a bearing 0.046; a new threat 0.019; a block or arrival 0.008. By ply below the root: plies 4, 5 and 6 hold 0.245, 0.245 and 0.307. So the cost is the tree of takings, deep, each taking restarting the quiet count. The main agent had guessed the quiet threat and arrival classes; that guess was wrong.
3. WHY: with comparison by inclusion only, a taking of a guarded unit is never a pure loss or a pure gain, it is a trade, so no taking can be pruned and every order of takings on a place is read out. A person answers an exchange on one place with one question, by the order of what stands on and bears on it; that needs an order of kinds. This is the open trade of the 78.57 change note, and it is what the estimator of SYSTEM_SPEC 13 is for.
4. BY SIZE: frames of 2 to 5 members took 341 to 744 questions each, frames of 7 to 10 took 2572 to 3341; 914 of the 1711 frames sat at the cap of 10 members.

SAFE still sits below its base (0.0120 against 0.0293).

PLAN 78.58: THE ESTIMATOR FROM SELF-PLAY, THE ORDER OF KINDS IT GIVES, AND THE EXCHANGE ON ONE PLACE AS ONE QUESTION (SYSTEM_SPEC 12, 13; the 78.57 read). Written 2026-11-15 by the main agent. A sandbox: nothing in the real store, nothing wired into a player, no oracle, no human game, no puzzle.
Why now: the 78.57 read shows the frame read spends 0.785 of its questions under takings, deep, because without an order of kinds no taking can be pruned. The estimator is what gives that order, and Kaveh has said it may be trained from any source; self-play needs no further word of his.
A. THE DATA. Every self-play game record already on disk whose players read no teacher and no oracle (the 500 games of opportunity_78_44; the match games of subgoal_play_78_50 and 78_51; any other found by search, each with its provenance checked and listed). State how many games and positions, and split by game into fit and test. If they are too few for stage B to be read at all, say so with the numbers and add playouts: from sampled quiet positions, games played out by the cheapest existing self-play mover, all cores, their count and cost stated.
B. THE ESTIMATOR. Interface fixed first: in, the parts of a position as counts for each side (units by kind as raw symbols; then, as a second set of inputs, the distinct kept concepts of 78.54 and the trap and frame classes of 78.55 and 78.57 where cheap); out, the probability of each result for the side to move; beside it, a record of its source, its data and its date. First form: a regularised logistic model, read only at QUIET positions (the quiet rows of the forcing reads where they exist; otherwise say what quiet means for the new positions). Reported on the test games: log loss and a calibration table, for (1) the base rate alone, (2) counts of kinds, (3) kinds and concepts; with bands by bootstrap over games. The fitted terms of the kinds are printed as the ORDER OF KINDS with their bands; say plainly which pairs of kinds the data cannot order.
C. THE EXCHANGE ON ONE PLACE, ONE QUESTION, in Rust. For a place and the units that bear on it, with those behind them on the same line taken from the through relation as they are uncovered: the sequence of takings with the least kind first for each side and the right to stop, valued by the terms of stage B. Exchange.lean (the generic lists: value, cheapest, cheapestXF and their lemmas) is the reference and is mirrored with a test; the order of kinds is an INPUT read from the estimator record, never written in the code. Its answer is an ESTIMATE and is marked so wherever it is used.
D. THE FRAME READ WITH IT. In the question read of 78.57: a taking whose exchange on its place loses by the estimate is pruned with that reason (mark: pruned by estimate); a taking whose exchange wins or is level is read as ONE question with its result, and the line goes on below it only if the taking changed a bearing off that place (something uncovered, a unit drawn away from what it guarded). A claim that rests on a bound, a prune or an estimate is given the status READ, not forced; forced is kept for claims with no such mark. Roots: the seed units and what bears on them, capped at a stated small number; the rest split.
E. THE MEASURE. The 40-game short run of 78.57 again, then the 500 games if the short run is in order: questions per frame with the split by class and ply; the share of frames at 30 questions or fewer; the observed fates per class (LOST, SAFE, the new READ classes) beside 78.57 and 78.55; the hand positions; time per position.
F. NOT in this plan: any other source for the estimator; the estimator at the leaf of the search; frames as inputs beyond the cheap classes.
Tests: the exchange against a brute read of every order of takings on small hand cases and against the Lean lists; the estimator record round trip; the question read never calls forced a claim that carries a mark; the source scan of tests/test_plan78.py.

STAGE C (the exchange on one place, one question): rust/engine/tactics/src/sheet/exchange.rs (new), bindings in base_graph_py.rs (`set_kind_values`, `exchange_taking`, static `exchange_plain`, `exchange_rays`), tests in tests/test_plan78_58_estimator_exchange.py, tests/plan78_58_lean_exchange.json.
AS BUILT. Two layers in one file. (1) THE LISTS, a function-by-function mirror of lean/ideas/Ideas/Exchange.lean over integers: `value_f`/`value` (the minimax of the capture game, either side free to choose the capturer or to stop), `cheapest_f`/`cheapest` (least kind first, the right to stop is the `max 0`), `reveal` (the unit behind the capturer joins its owner's list, cheapest first, the new one before equals), `cheapest_xf` (the static exchange over rays), plus `cheapest_xf_line` (the same recursion that also returns who takes, in order: a tie stops) and `brute_xf` (every order of takings, for the tests). (2) THE PARTICIPANTS OF A PLACE read from the layer-1 graph: `estimate_taking(part, place, taker, kv)`: the units that bear on the place (`bears`, direct) of each side, and behind each the units on its line from the `through` relation (the unit w with through(w, place of the unit in front) and the one unit between = the head; repeated, at most 8 deep), uncovered as the front ones take; the worth of each kind is `kv[kind]`, a table of integers that is an INPUT: the code writes no worth and no kind (a test swaps two worths and the answer changes; a source scan finds no chess word and none of the fitted numbers in the code). The answer is the worth of what stands on the place less what the other side's best answer takes back (a side stops where that is better); negative means the taking loses. It is an ESTIMATE: nothing else is in it (a pin, a threat elsewhere, an in-between move, the king's legality as a later taker). The goal kind's worth is the record's rule value.

In words: the queen that takes a pawn the pawn guards loses the queen for the pawn; the pawn that takes a guarded knight wins the knight for the pawn; knight for knight is level; the doubled rook, uncovered by the first taking, takes the pawn back (twice the pawn less the rook, against the pawn less the rook when the graph has no profile of the kinds and so no unit behind); an unguarded pawn is simply won. The `through` relation holds one unit between, so a chain of three behind is read one step at a time; where a position needs more the exchange is read shorter than it is (limit).
STAGE D (the frame read with the exchange): rust/engine/tactics/src/sheet/questions.rs, rust/engine/py/src/questions_py.rs, base_graph_py.rs, discovery/frames_questions_measure.py; tests in tests/test_plan78_58_estimator_exchange.py (D part). The order of kinds enters as an input: `BaseGraph.set_kind_values([(kind, worth)])`, read by the measure from the estimator record's `kind_values`; with none set the read is exactly the 78.57 read (the 78.57 and 78.55 test files pass unchanged).
AS BUILT, in `QReader::solve` and `expand_new`. (1) A candidate that is a plain taking carries the exchange estimate of the place it takes on (`Est`: the worth to the taker and the units that take in the line the estimate reads). (2) A taking whose exchange LOSES by the estimate is not asked: it is PRUNED BY ESTIMATE (counted: `est_pruned`; every result of that node carries the mark `pruned_by_estimate`), for either side of the read. (3) A taking that wins or is level is read as ONE question with its result: the takings of its line are played by the game (the least kind first, each side with the right to stop) and the position after them is the child; the result is the units lost on the way. If the line cannot be played (the game refuses a move) the taking is read the old way (`est_unplayed`). (4) THE LINE GOES ON BELOW the exchange only if the taking changed a bearing off the place, on the frame's places (`bearings_changed`): a unit that stands there still and is borne on by another number of units than before (a unit drawn away from what it guarded, or one that now bears on it from the place of the exchange), or a place the exchange vacated or left empty that a unit outside the exchange now bears on (something uncovered). Then the child is read normally (`est_cont`); otherwise the exchange is the result and the node is not read further (`est_read` counts both). Everything that rests on (3) carries `exchange_by_estimate`. (5) READ, not forced: a claim that holds and carries a bound (`ended_by_bound`), a prune (`prune_used`), or an estimate mark (`pruned_by_estimate`, `exchange_by_estimate`) has `status_read` = "read" in the report (no other key), "read" in the layer-3 claim node, and the measure classes it READ_LOST, READ_SAFE, READ_BOTH; `status` keeps the 78.57 meaning so the 78.57 test file still reads it; forced is the word for a claim with none of these marks (and the test asserts that no claim with a mark is called forced). Flags widened from u8 to u16 (two new bits). Roots: the cap of the frame at its root stays ROOT_CAP = 10 members (a frame made from a seed or by joining two; a bigger one is split, never read with a unit in common); a smaller cap is a separate run, not made here.
LIMITS: the exchange is read on one place; a line the estimate does not see (an in-between move, a pin) is not read below a taking with no changed bearing; the estimator's order is the point estimate (the bands are in the record, not used to hold a prune back); the through relation reaches one unit behind at a time.

78.58 READ (2026-11-15, by the main agent, merged as 23d55f0a; tests test_plan78, test_plan78_58, _57, _55 pass on main after the rebuild, 74; the engine gate was started at this commit and its line is appended when it ends). From the run's own lines (estimator_78_58/full/obs.txt and heads_obs.txt; frames_78_58/short40 and n500 obs.txt; one run each, directions only).
What holds:
1. AN ORDER OF KINDS CAME OUT OF RESULTS ALONE. The players that made the games count every unit as one. Fitted on who then won, the terms order the five kinds with no pair left unordered, and counts of kinds lower the log loss on test games well below the base rate. No table was supplied anywhere. The top term is likely inflated (few games differ in that kind except those of the random mover), and the terms are what decides self-play between these players, not human practice.
2. The concepts of 78.54 add a little over the kinds, with a band that excludes zero; small.
3. The exchange on one place is built as a mirror of Exchange.lean, equal to Lean's own evaluation on the fixture and to a brute read of every order on random cases. The order of kinds is an input.
4. With it the frame read asks about a third of the questions of 78.57 and the share that follows a taking fell from about four fifths to two fifths.
What does not hold yet:
5. STILL NOT A FEW QUESTIONS: about 600 per frame; a tenth of frames at 30 or fewer. Most exchanges read as one question still go on below (the rule "a bearing changed on the frame" is nearly always true).
6. NO LINE ENDS FOR A REASON. Every claim carries the mark ended-by-a-bound, because every line stops at a depth or a count of quiet plies. So nothing is forced, everything is READ, and READ does not tell a claim that stopped because nothing was left to ask from one that was cut. This is October lesson 2, not built in 78.57 and still not built.
7. The units read as lost are taken at about a third within 4 plies; the exhaustive read of 78.55 was near nine in ten on the few it claimed.
8. The arrival head on kinds alone explains almost nothing; expected, since the 78.49 fit drew on the 26 statements, which are not among these inputs.
9. The bands of the estimator are stored and not used: a prune is decided by the point estimate.


PLAN 78.59: THE HEADS FROM HUMAN GAMES (SYSTEM_SPEC 13; Kaveh 2026-11-15: "Yes, human games can be read"; "stockfish cannot be read in. It has to be statistical"; "I would much rather do the prediction of future tactical opportunities ... multiple heads"; "We can even condition on ELO"). Written 2026-11-15 by the main agent. Python over the installed extension; NO Rust change and no rebuild of the extension. A sandbox: nothing in the real store, nothing wired into a player.
The data: data/records/lichess_2019-01 (97 shards, columns game_id, white_elo, black_elo, result, n_plies, time_control, termination, moves; the manifest says 19354162 games). No column of it holds an engine evaluation; if any field or comment inside `moves` does, it is dropped unread and the count of such games printed. data/lichess is NOT used (one file there is named for evaluations).
A. THE SAMPLE. Stated before the run: which shards, how many games, which time controls and terminations are kept (games ended by the clock or by abandonment are a different thing from games decided on the board; say what is done with them), the bands of rating, and the split into fit and test by game. A short run on a few thousand games first.
B. THE INPUTS at quiet positions (quiet as in 78.58: no unit of either side borne on by the other side and not by its own): counts of kinds per side; the 26 statements of 78.49; the distinct kept concepts of 78.54 on a thinned set of rows as in 78.58; the two ratings as the mean and the difference; the ply.
C. THE HEADS, in the record format of 78.58 with source "human games" beside the self-play heads, never overwriting them:
   result: the probability of each result. Reported: log loss and calibration on test games for the base rate; ratings alone; ratings and kinds; then with statements; then with concepts; bands over games. The order of kinds printed beside the self-play order, and again per band of rating (does a kind's term move with rating).
   kind_baseline: the kind terms from human games.
   arrival: the head Kaveh prefers. A threat that the forcing read CONFIRMS arrives for the mover within 8 plies, less the other side's, as in 78.49, on a sample of games small enough for the forcing read's cost (about a twentieth of a second a position; state the sample and the time). Reported as in 78.49 (rank correlation on test games with bands) for kinds alone, statements, statements and concepts, with and without the ratings. Beside it the same fit from self-play (78.49) for comparison.
D. THE CORRECTION, in his words "whether the value of piece is more or less than that and by how much": for the twenty concepts with the largest terms in the result head, the change in the probability of the result when the concept holds, kinds held equal, with bands; and for each kind, how its term moves when the concepts are added.
E. WHAT A ROUTE COMPARISON WOULD READ. For 200 test positions with the move played and one other legal move chosen at random: the heads at the two positions reached, and how often the played move is the higher on each head, by band of rating. A reading only; no move is chosen by it.
Cautions to carry in the note: what players did is not what was forced; a concept present may mark the stronger side rather than cause the result; rating conditions only part of that.
All cores; the rows written as compact arrays, with the disk checked before each write (under 7 GB free at the time of writing).

PLAN 78.60: A LINE ENDS FOR A REASON (the 78.58 read, points 5, 6, 7, 9; October lessons 2, 3 and 5). Written 2026-11-15 by the main agent. Rust in sheet/questions.rs; a sandbox as before.
A. SETTLED. A line of the frame read ends SETTLED when, at a position, the question "what stands to be lost here" has an empty answer for BOTH sides on the frame's units (asked from each side, lesson 3), and no member is trapped by the trap question. A SETTLED end is a reason, not a bound; a claim all of whose lines end SETTLED, with no prune and no estimate on the way, is FORCED WITHIN THE FRAME. A line cut by depth, by the count of quiet plies or by a fuse stays BOUND. The measure counts ends by kind.
B. PROGRESS. A line goes on past a quiet position only for a move that cannot be undone (a taking, or what the rules give as a change of kind) or for a reply to a standing loss. A line that returns to a set of bearings on the frame already seen on that line ends as CIRCLING, with no claim from it.
C. THE EXCHANGE GOES ON BELOW ONLY FOR A NAMED CAUSE: a unit that took part was the only guard of another member (named), or its leaving uncovers a line onto a member (named, from the through relation). Not for any change of bearing. The cause is kept with the question.
D. THE BAND OF THE ESTIMATE. A taking is pruned by the estimate only if it loses at both ends of the stored bands of the kinds involved; otherwise it is read.
E. THE CLASSES. FORCED WITHIN THE FRAME; READ BY ESTIMATE (rests on the exchange or a prune by estimate, lines otherwise settled); BOUND (some line cut). The observed fates per class beside 78.58, 78.57 and 78.55; questions per frame with the split; the share of frames at 30 or fewer; the comparison test against the exhaustive read run WITH the exchange on.
F. SMALL ROOTS. The seed units and what bears on them, capped at 6, the rest split; the same measure at the cap of 10 beside it.
Short run on the 40 games, then the 500.
