78.70 READ (main agent, 2026-11-16; merged, RUST CHANGED, the extension rebuilt on main; touched test files pass on main; one run each, directions only; numbers are in the builder's note above and artifacts/experiments/threats_78_70/). SPEC CHECK: serves SYSTEM_SPEC 8 (the threat list) and 4 (carrying). Interface threat_list(moves, ply, reader, ...) returning rows for both sides with class, frames, response, how the line ended, read set, stake, two bands; Rust QReader::answers and BaseGraph.questions_threats. Departures from the spec: none in form. In substance the list does not yet do what section 8 asks, see 1.
1. I READ THE TEN PRINTED POSITIONS AGAINST THE BOARD, AND MOST ROWS ARE NOT THREATS A PLAYER WOULD NAME. (a) An even exchange is printed as a unit lost (positions 2, 5, 9: a unit that can be taken and is retaken). (b) Units are printed as lost with no unit bearing on them (positions 1, 7, 8, 10), resting on a bound, not on a line. (c) The first response named can lose far more than the unit it saves (positions 6 and 8 name a move that gives up the strongest unit; position 4 names a taking that loses a unit for less). (d) Threats to the goal unit are absent: position 10 has a forced end of the game in a few moves for the other side and the list shows one row about a unit in the corner. (e) Of about 25 thousand rows 53 ended concrete; the rest rest on a bound, an estimate or nothing. Rows that look right: position 3 (a unit attacked three times and guarded once) and the threat row of position 4.
2. THE CHECKS AGREE WITH THAT READING. Every band has more takings soon than positions with no row, and the shuffled control is flat, so the list is not noise. But the top band is not the highest, by either way of drawing the line, and a named response was the move played in about one row in eight. On the puzzles the first move was by a bearer of a top-band row in 23 percent against 6 percent for a random unit: above the control, far from usable.
3. CARRYING, THE TRUE TEST. A claim whose read set did not change was held again two plies later in about half the cases; in most of the misses no frame held the unit at the later ply, a miss of attention and not a change of mind. About one in eleven claims first seen at a ply had its read set already in place two plies before. So the read flickers, and carrying the list from move to move would mend a measurable part of it.
4. WHAT IS WRONG IS THE SAME THING FOUR TIMES: THE ROW IS A CLASS OF THE FRAME READ, NOT A LINE READ TO ITS END. Spec 4 says chess is concrete and a line ends for a stated reason; these rows end "quiet" by a mapping the builder had to invent. The mend is plan 78.72: every row and every response is read concretely to a settled end by the tools that exist, and is printed as confirmed, an exchange, refuted or unread.
5. FOR THE SPREAD AGAINST RANK: neither is shown better; left open until the rows are concrete.
NEXT: 78.72, ahead of 78.71, since the subgoals of 78.71 read this list.

PLAN 78.72: THE THREAT LIST MADE CONCRETE (SYSTEM_SPEC 8 the threat list, 4 "chess is concrete" and how a line ends, 3 the exchange; the 78.70 read). Written 2026-11-16 by the main agent. Extends threat_list.py; reuses the forcing read (78.46 to 78.48), the search with the record of worths as judge (solve_batch, 78.61, the generation-2 record: measured, not assumed), the exchange mirrored from Lean (78.58), the settled end (78.60). Rust where a reading must be added; a sandbox, no player changed.
INTERFACE: threat_list rows gain {the line (the moves read), the outcome (which units each side is left with at the settled end), the verdict: CONFIRMED, EXCHANGE, REFUTED, UNREAD, and the reason the line ended as spec 4 names it}. A row is a threat only when CONFIRMED or UNREAD (printed as suspected); an EXCHANGE is printed apart; a REFUTED claim is dropped and counted.
A. EVERY CLAIM IS READ TO A SETTLED END. For each row of 78.70: the taking line played out with the best replies by the forcing read or the search, to the settled end. What the taker is left ahead by is judged by the measured record of kinds or by the kinds reading's chance, never by a table. Budget per row stated; when it runs out the row is UNREAD.
B. A CLAIM WITH NO UNIT BEARING ON IT is a row only if the reading names the move that makes the threat; then it is a threat in two moves and is printed with that move. Otherwise it is dropped.
C. EVERY RESPONSE IS READ THE SAME WAY. A response is kept only if after it the reading no longer wins the unit and nothing of larger stake is lost by it; responses are ordered by what each side is left with. The count of responses dropped is printed.
D. THREATS TO THE GOAL UNIT. The forced end of the game within the forcing read's reach, for either side, is a row of the highest stake, with its line.
E. THE LIST CARRIED FROM MOVE TO MOVE: a claim whose read set is unchanged is kept without being asked again; a claim whose read set changed is asked again. Measured: the flicker of 78.70 E(3) again, and the time saved.
F. THE CHECKS OF 78.70 D AGAIN on the same held-out games and the same puzzles (a measure only), with the verdicts: the rate of a unit then taken for CONFIRMED against EXCHANGE against UNREAD; whether the top band is now the highest; how often a kept response was the move played. THE SAME TEN POSITIONS printed again, each beside its 78.70 list, plus ten new ones by the same rule.
STATUS: written; next. 78.71 after it.

78.72 BUILT, stages A to F (builder agent, 2026-11-16; branch worktree-agent-a953ea5b24ab53643; one run each, directions only; numbers only from the OBS lines below, which programs printed; whole files in artifacts/experiments/threats_78_72/ (read_obs.txt, measure_obs.txt, carry_obs.txt, puzzles_obs.txt, print.txt), untracked, a real directory in this worktree's artifacts; the 78.70 rows and the record were read through links to main's artifacts). SPEC CHECK: serves SYSTEM_SPEC 8 "The threat list" under 4 (where a concrete answer can be reached it is reached; how a line ends) and 3 (the exchange; a sacrifice needs a reason); the piece is the frame read's view for the wake, one step on from plan 78.70. A sandbox: no player changed, nothing on by default, nothing in rules/learned or data/derived. RUST CHANGED: a new module rust/engine/tactics/src/lines.rs (game-free: a line read to a settled end by the ledger search with the measured record as judge, the forced end of the game by the search that counts nothing confirmed by the exact forcing read `wins_in`) and its binding rust/engine/py/src/lines_py.rs (`cs_engine.read_lines`); lib.rs of the tactics crate and of the binding register them; no Cargo change; no decision-path crate depends on cs_learn. THE EXTENSION WAS REBUILT FROM THIS WORKTREE (`maturin develop --release --offline`), so the shared editable install points here; the parent rebuilds main after the merge. A LINKER NOTE: the loader of this host refused the freshly built library ("mis-aligned LINKEDIT string pool", the pool's offset not a multiple of 8, which depends on the parity of the library's imported symbols); lines_py.rs therefore ends with one imported datum (`pad_probe`) that moves the parity; the first build loaded without it on main by luck of the count; remove it if a later toolchain does not need it. Code: catspace/incubator/analyst/discovery/threat_concrete.py (the list; interface in its doc comment), threat_concrete_measure.py (read, measure, carry, puzzles), threat_print.py (`--concrete`: the print of the twenty positions), threat_list.py (band_of counts a deferred answer and an unverified candidate of an UNREAD row as a response); tests/test_plan78_72_concrete.py (in scripts/gate.py; includes the scan of the new Python and Rust for game words).
INTERFACE. Rust: `read_lines(variant, games, queries, worth, depth, fuse, end_plies, end_fuse, threads)`; a query is (game, mode, passed, me_first, a, b, c); modes: 0 the takings on a place, 1 one move, 2 every legal move, 3 the quiet moves that make a taking stand (the other side passing once) each read as a whole-board line with the other side's best replies, 4 the forced end of the game for the mover, 5 the moves after which the other side finds no forced end, 6 and 7 a response (or every move) read two ways (the whole-board line, and the taking lines of the unit after it, with the move's own taking counted in them), 8 the best line of the mover. Python: Record.load (the measured generation-2 record of 78.61: its integer worths by the game's word for the kind, the judge, and the half width of each kind's confidence interval, its RESOLUTION), Lines.ask, verdict_of, response_of, concrete_lists(items, lines), same_read_set. A row of the list gains line, outcome (what the taker takes and loses), verdict, net, resolution, ended and its reason, lead (the move of a threat in two moves), response (the kept responses, each a line), resp_read and resp_unread.
A. EVERY CLAIM IS READ TO A SETTLED END. The taker is the side that does not own the unit (for the side to move's own unit: the other side after one pass of the game; where the game gives none the row is UNREAD with that reason). Each legal taking on the unit's place is read as a line (the ledger search, the record as judge, best replies, the captures resolved at the horizon of six plies, a node fuse per line) and the best for the taker is the row's line; the line is shown up to its last capture. VERDICT BY THE RECORD, NOT A TABLE OR A COUNT: the sum of the worths of what the taker took less what it lost, against the RESOLUTION of the record for the units in that ledger (the half widths of the record's own intervals added in quadrature): above it, CONFIRMED; below its negative, REFUTED (dropped, counted); between, EXCHANGE when units were traded (printed apart); the end of the game itself decides concretely; a line the fuse cut is UNREAD (no forced claim is made from a cut line). HOW A LINE ENDED (a choice of this build, the spec does not map it): CONCRETE the game ends in the line, QUIET the settled end (no capture left to either side at the horizon), OUT OF BUDGET the fuse cut it; LOST BEYOND DOUBT is a verdict of section 6's readings and is not produced. The resolution is coarse: a net up to about one pawn is not told apart from an exchange, so a line that wins a pawn and a rook for a bishop can print as an EXCHANGE (position 6 of the print).
B. A CLAIM WITH NOTHING BEARING ON IT is a row only if one quiet move of the taker makes a taking stand (a threat in two moves) AND the whole-board line of that move, the other side's best replies read, still ends ahead for the taker; the row names the move. A first version took the pass as the reply and made a queen attacked by a queen into a threat; reading the best reply (the attacker is simply taken) removed it. Otherwise the claim is dropped and counted. A threat in two moves has its answer after the taker's first move, so no response is read for it now (marked deferred; banded as having one).
C. EVERY RESPONSE IS READ THE SAME WAY, TWO WAYS: the taking lines of the unit AFTER it (the move's own taking counted in them; is the unit still won?) and the whole-board line of the move. KEPT only if the taker is no longer CONFIRMED on the unit (or no taking is legal) AND the taker's whole-board line is not better for it than what it could count on had the owner passed (nothing larger is lost by it); STILL WON, WORSE THAN PASSING and UNREAD are counted. The candidates are the frame read's answers (read to the full depth) and, because the frame read stops at its first sound answers, every legal move of the owner (the sweep, at a shorter horizon and fuse, said in each response); a move is listed once. Ordered by what the taker is left with, the least first. The count read and dropped is printed per row and in the OBS.
D. THE GOAL. The forced end of the game for either side: the search that counts nothing (ledger::Nothing) deepened ply by ply to a stated number of plies, the first move then confirmed by the exact forcing read (every reply of the other side); PROVED, or SUSPECTED (printed as UNREAD) when the exact read could not confirm within its fuse; the row is of the highest stake with its line; responses are the moves after which the same search finds no forced end (by the pruned search, not exhaustive: said). No name of the goal in any layer: the game's own outcome through `Game::outcome`. On the 78.45 puzzles the instrument found a forced end in a share of positions and in every such case its first move was the solution's (a check of the instrument, see the OBS).
E. THE LIST CARRIED FROM MOVE TO MOVE, measured on the same 150 games and plies as 78.70's carrying run: the claims whose read set is unchanged two plies on, how often the carried verdict is the one a fresh read gives, the flicker of the 78.70 E(3) again, and the share of the line-search nodes the carried rows would have cost. Wired into nothing: `same_read_set` is the test and the measure is in `carry`.
F. THE CHECKS OF 78.70 D AGAIN on the same 1000 held-out games and 33362 settled rows, by verdict; the ten positions of 78.70 printed again (the same games and plies) with their old and new lists, plus ten new ones by the same rule in the games the first ten did not use; the puzzles as a measure only. Time per position is printed (the wake will call it).
READING OF THE RESULTS (directions, one run). The rows are now lines: an even exchange prints as an exchange, a unit with nothing bearing on it is gone or carries a named move, a response that gives up more than it saves is not kept, the first response named no longer gives up the strongest unit. THE TOP BAND IS STILL NOT THE HIGHEST: by the spread and by the rank, with and without the goal rows, the bands of low stake or with a response show a higher rate of a unit then taken than band 1; a likely cause is that the event (any unit of the side taken) is a trade that happens whatever the stake, and a high-stake row with no answer found is, for the human sample, often a row the side then answers by a move the lines did not hold (the played move was a kept response in most rows against the mover, see the OBS), but this is a guess and was not tested. The rate of a unit then taken is highest for CONFIRMED and EXCHANGE rows and lowest with no row; UNREAD sits between. Carrying by read set keeps the verdict in less than half the cases: the read set is the frame read's, while a line is read on the whole board, so the verdict can change with nothing in the read set changing. WHAT IS STILL WRONG: (1) the resolution of the record makes the EXCHANGE class wide; (2) the sweep reads at a shorter horizon than the rows, and its cut lines make some responses UNREAD; (3) the lines come from a depth-limited search, so a claim that needs more than the horizon is read as it stands at the horizon (QUIET) and is not a proof; (4) 'the taker ends ahead' is judged on the whole board, so a claim is confounded by anything else the line wins or loses; (5) the print shows no goal row at position 10, the position the 78.70 read said had a forced end for the other side: the instrument reads seven plies for either side there and finds none (a probe at nine plies and the exact read at three moves found none either; the probe is not an OBS line of the files), so that claim of the 78.70 read is not borne out by this instrument. NOT BUILT: the rule for choosing a move (plan 78.71 reads this list); the wake calling the list; stage E wired into the wake.

### 78.72 READ (2026-11-16, main agent, after merge 7257f83c)

Serves SYSTEM_SPEC 8 (the threat list) under 4 (how a line ends) and 3 (exchange). The numbers are the builder's OBS lines in
artifacts/experiments/threats_78_72 (one run, directions only). I read all twenty printed positions against the board.

WHAT IS NOW RIGHT. The four faults of 78.70 are gone in the ten old positions: the even exchanges of positions 2, 5, 9 print
apart as exchanges; the claims with no bearer in 1, 7, 8, 10 are dropped; the responses that gave up the strongest unit in 6
and 8 are gone. The rows that stay are ones a player would name: the unit attacked by a lesser unit in 4, 13, 14, the
strongest unit attacked in 15, the unit bearing more attackers than guards in 3 and 20. The named response was the move played
far more often than in 78.70, and far above its control.

A CORRECTION OF MY OWN 78.70 READ. I wrote that position 10 holds a forced end of the game in a few moves. The builder's exact
read finds none, and on rereading the board I find none either. That line of my read was wrong and was not checked by a program.

WHAT IS STILL WRONG, from the print:
1. THE RESOLUTION IS TOO COARSE AND GROWS WITH THE LENGTH OF THE LINE. In position 6 the taker wins a unit of the second kind
   and a least unit for one of the third kind and the row prints as an exchange. In positions 5 and 13 two units of the same
   kind are traded and the resolution still grows, though like for like cancels exactly whatever the record says.
2. RESPONSES ARE NOT ORDERED BY HOW THEY END, AND SOME KEPT ONES GIVE UP A UNIT. Position 4 prints a response that gives a unit
   for two least units ahead of the plain retreats. Position 15 keeps three responses that each give up a unit and does not
   show the plain retreat of the attacked unit; why the retreat was dropped is not known and must be found.
3. THE BEST REPLIES IN THE SWEEP LOOK WRONG IN PLACES (position 20, the first response's line gives two units away). The
   sweep reads to 4 plies on a whole-board ledger.
4. FEW ROWS. Eleven of twenty positions print no row at all. Threats that need one quiet move first are rare in the print;
   position 6 holds a uncovering move against a unit in the corner that no row names.
5. THE TOP BAND IS STILL NOT THE HIGHEST by either line. The section 8 line between high and low stake stays not shown.
6. CARRYING BY READ SET IS WEAK HERE: an unchanged read set gave the same fresh verdict under half the time, and few nodes are
   saved. Either the read set is too narrow for a concrete line (the line touches more than the frame), or the depth cut makes
   the verdict unstable. Not wired into play.
7. PUZZLES: no gain over 78.70 on the first move.
8. A LINKER WORKAROUND sits in rust/engine/py/src/lines_py.rs (one imported datum to flip the alignment of the string pool).
   Kept for now; it may fail again when the count of imported symbols changes. To replace with a build setting.

NEXT: PLAN 78.73 (small), then 78.71.

### PLAN 78.73: THE VERDICT AND THE RESPONSES OF THE CONCRETE LIST (2026-11-16)

Serves SYSTEM_SPEC 8, piece: the threat list, same interface as 78.72 (threat_concrete.concrete_lists, Lines.ask, verdict_of,
response_of). No new interface; the row gains fields only.

A. VERDICT. Units of the same kind taken and lost cancel exactly before the net and the resolution are computed; the resolution
   is built only from the kinds left after cancelling. Print how many EXCHANGE rows change verdict.
B. RESPONSES. Every kept response carries its own end (what the responder loses and takes in its line). Order: responses that
   lose nothing first, then by the net. A response that loses more than the threat would take is dropped. Find and report why
   the plain retreat in position 15 of the 78.72 print was dropped, and fix the cause.
C. THE SWEEP'S REPLIES. For the 20 printed positions, check each printed response line with a deeper read (depth 6 as the
   rows); print how many first replies change. If many, the sweep reads to the rows' depth.
D. STABILITY. On the carry sample, for rows with an unchanged read set whose fresh verdict differs: print the share where the
   two lines differ only beyond the depth cut, and the share where a move outside the read set changed the line. This tells
   which of the two causes in read point 6 holds.
E. Reprint the same twenty positions, old 78.72 beside new, and rerun the checks by verdict and by band, the response played,
   and the puzzles.
Not in this plan: more rows from quiet first moves (read point 4), the line between high and low stake (point 5). They wait for

### PLAN 78.75: THE RULE FOR CHOOSING A MOVE, IN A SANDBOX (2026-11-16)

Serves SYSTEM_SPEC 8 ("the rule for choosing a move", the wake's steps) and 7 (holding a subgoal), under rule 7: a subgoal
orders and never adds to the value. A sandbox; the shipped player is not changed.

PIECE AND INTERFACE. choose(position, tied, lists, goals, held) -> (move, reason, held'). `tied` is the set of moves the search
holds equal (the 78.50 form, solve_equals_batch, as plan 78.67 used it); `lists` the concrete threat list of both sides
(threat_concrete); `goals` the ranked goals (subgoal_goals, subgoal_units); `held` the subgoal carried from the last move or
none. It returns one move of `tied`, the reason in words of the graph (which threat, which answer, which goal, which fact),
and the subgoal now held. It never returns a move outside `tied`: the search's value decides, the rule only orders. Called by
the match harness of 78.67 (tiebreak_measure.py) as one more tie-break.

THE RULE, his guide of spec 8 made exact:
1. THREATS FIRST. If a CONFIRMED row against us exists: a move of `tied` that is a kept response to the row of the highest
   stake is preferred; among several, one that is also a step of the held goal. A counter-threat counts as an answer only when
   it is a kept response of the concrete read (decided 2026-11-16).
2. NO THREAT, OR THE THREAT ALREADY ANSWERED BY EVERY TIED MOVE: advance the subgoal. A move advances a goal when it is the
   first move of the goal's line, a step that brings a unit to bear, or makes one of its unmet facts true (asked of the graph
   after the move). The held goal is kept while its unmet facts do not rise; else the first-ranked goal is taken up.
3. A BIG THREAT WITH NO KEPT RESPONSE IN `tied`: refuting it becomes the held subgoal; the reason says so.
4. NOTHING APPLIES: the search's own choice.
The ranking of goals counts stoppers, not facts (the 78.74 read).

A. choose() and its tests on built positions, one per branch of the rule.
B. THE TRACE. For the twenty positions: the decision printed as a line of thought (this threat, that answer, so this; or no
   threat, this goal, this fact, so this move). The builder judges five against the board; the main agent judges them again.
C. MATCHES in the 78.67 harness, same sides and openings: the rule against (1) the search's own choice, (2) a random
   tie-break, (3) the arrival number of 78.67. Also the rule with step 2 off (threats only) and with step 1 off (goals only),
   so each half is priced. Cost per move printed. Short match first. Timed matches need a quiet machine.
D. HOW OFTEN each branch fired, how long a goal was held, how often a held goal's facts came true, how often the unit was
   then won, against goals not held.
Not here: sacrifices for an attack when the threat is small; the sleep. After this plan: 78.68.

### 78.75 READ (2026-11-16, main agent, after the merge)

Serves SYSTEM_SPEC 8 (the rule for choosing a move) and 7 (holding a subgoal). Numbers are the builder's OBS lines in
artifacts/experiments/move_rule_78_75 (one run, 120 games a match, reading not charged, machine not fully quiet, many games
unfinished and counted as draws; directions only). I read the trace of position 18 against the board.

- THE RULE DID NOT HELP IN PLAY. Against the search's own choice, a random tie-break and the arrival number of 78.67 its score
  is at or under half; against the first and the third the interval lies under half. It costs half a second a decision. The
  arrival number, which costs milliseconds, was above half against the same control in 78.67.
- THE THREAT HALF WAS NOT TESTED BY THIS HARNESS. A threat was the deciding branch in under one tie in a hundred: where a
  threat is real the search already holds one move best, so no tie is left. As a tie-break the threat list is redundant with
  the search. Its use, by spec 8, is to say where the time goes and what is carried, and that is a test of cost at equal
  strength, not of a tie-break. Owed.
- THE GOAL HALF CHANGED THE MOVE IN MOST TIES AND DID NOT GAIN. The aims are not yet a player's (ranking by stoppers still
  puts far units behind several units first), and a goal is held for one decision on the mean, so nothing is pursued.
- QUESTIONS A DECISION (the count spec 4 now asks for): about twenty line queries and on the order of a hundred thousand nodes
  a decision. A human asks a handful. This is the number to bring down.
- JUDGED AGAINST THE BOARD: a taking with tempo that also answers a threat is not among the kept responses (position 13), so
  the read is too strict about trades. The list has no row for a unit about to change kind on the last rank (position 18):
  it reads takings only, though spec 6 names the events of the rules. A CORRECTION OF THE BUILDER'S SELF-CHECK: in position 18
  it called the rule's move plainly wrong for leaving the file; the move stays on the file and holds the far place, so the
  move is sound. The missing row is the fault, not the move.
- THE MATCH IS A BLUNT TOOL HERE: at this clock a quarter to two thirds of games do not finish.

WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT THE ORDER OF WORK. Five builds on the list and the proposer ended in a player no better than a random
tie-break. Three causes recur under all of them and none is in the list or the proposer: the measured worths are coarse, the
heads are weak (the stake ranks worse than chance), and nothing learned tells a good aim from a far one. All three are the
sleep's work. NEXT: plan 78.68, as ordered. The move rule stays as the sandbox the sleep's products are tested in.

### 78.68 LADDER READ (2026-11-16, main agent, after the merge)

Serves SYSTEM_SPEC 9, the ladder and the list of surprises. Numbers are the builder's OBS lines in
artifacts/experiments/ladder_78_68/full (400 positions, one run, a loaded machine; directions only). I read case 9 against the
board.

- HOW THE POSITIONS DIVIDE: our reasoning alone reaches an accepted move in under two in five; the head as tie-break in one
  in five; deeper reading in one in ten; nearly a third stay open at the longest clock.
- THE HEADS ADD NOTHING AT RUNG 2. The arrival head picks an accepted move exactly as often as the search's own first move,
  both a little above a random pick. Rung 2 as counted is mostly the luck of a tie-break.
- THE OPEN SURPRISES ARE QUIET MOVES IN FULL POSITIONS. Nearly half the positions with many units stay open; the accepted
  moves there are almost all quiet; hardly any answers a listed threat. At the longest clock the search still holds many moves
  equal. The judge at the leaf counts kinds only, so it cannot tell quiet moves apart. This is a weakness of the estimate at
  the leaf, not of the depth of reading.
- THE WORTHS, SEEN PLAINLY (case 9, corrected from the builder's reading): the accepted move gives the strongest unit for two
  units of the second kind, a plain gain to a player. Our reading at the longest clock declines it. The record of generation 2
  does not price two of the second kind above one of the first.
- THE GROUPS SAY LITTLE YET: the largest holds half the list and is only "open, with quiet frames". The features do not
  separate causes. Grouping needs what our deep reading found, which is thin when the reading finds nothing.
- COST: rung 3 takes most of the time; a position that needs it costs on the order of three quarters of a minute.
- A choice of the builder I keep: the oracle's move types stay out of the list (they would leak the answer into the groups).

THE DIAGNOSIS, in the ladder's own terms: the weakest part is statistics, the estimate where the reading ends, then the worths.
Reasoning is not the first bottleneck on these positions. NEXT: 78.68 stage G (heads fitted on our own deeper thinking and
playouts, read AT THE LEAF and not only as a tie-break) scored by stage H on this list (surprises resolved less created, on a
part of the list the fit never saw).

### PLAN 78.76: THE LADDER UNDER EACH MEASURED WORTH RECORD (2026-11-16, main agent; SYSTEM_SPEC 5 "learn from results" and the odds games, 9 the ladder as the diagnosis, 6 the judge where the line ends)

WHY. Every reading since 78.67 (search, lines, threat list, ladder, stage G and H) judged by the generation-2 odds record of 78.61, whose printed worths put the second-strongest kind below both minor kinds and the weakest kind near two thirds of it. Two other measured records exist and were printed with the order a player expects: the 78.58 self-play record (estimator_78_58/full/estimator.json) and the kind terms of the human result head of 78.59 (results of human games only, which the 2026-11-15 decision allows). Searching history shows no run of the ladder or of a match under either. The cases of the ladder and of stage H that I read against the board fail on exactly this (a strongest unit declined for two of the second kind; a second-kind unit given for a minor one called even).
WHAT (a measurement, no new method, a sandbox). (1) The record becomes a parameter of the ladder's Tools and of Record.load (path and a name); default unchanged. (2) Two record files written in the same layout from the stored fits, never from retyped numbers: the 78.58 record and the 78.59 human kind terms, each with its half widths from its own printed band; if the fitted file of either is missing, refit it with the script that made it and say so. (3) The ladder's rungs 1 to 3 rerun on the same 400 positions with the same answers file under each record: the division by rung, the moves held equal per position, the hit of the search's own first move, the stage H control on the scored part, and the same counts by units on the board. (4) The printed cases: the fixed positions of the ladder's cases file under each record, side by side, with at least five judged against the board.
INTERFACE. Record.load(path=None, head=None) -> Record as before; Tools(record=...) ; ladder_measure run --record <name>; outputs to artifacts/experiments/ladder_78_76/<name>/. Nothing else changes.
THE WALL as in the ladder: answers read only by the scoring. No oracle number anywhere.
READ BEFOREHAND: a record that orders the kinds as a player does should shrink the tie sets and move positions from open to rung 1 or 3. If the division does not move, the worths are not the cause and the leaf's inputs are next.

THE JUDGEMENT AGAINST THE BOARD (the builder's, in words; the fixed set of twelve in ladder_78_76/cases.txt: the first six open surprises of the 78.68 list in file order and the first six positions whose rung differs between records; set A case 3 and set B case 1 are one position, and so are set A case 2 and set B case 2, so ten distinct positions):
- A6 (a rook and a far pawn against three pawns): the quiet winning move is the rook to the back rank, which wins a pawn with check next and guards the queening square; every record holds the rook to the seventh rank instead, which blocks its own pawn. The best line of all three ends with the pawn queened, and the ledger of captures cannot see a queening, so the worths of any record cannot tell the two apart. A weakness of what the judge counts, not of the worths (I did not read the ledger code; this is my reading of the printed events).
- B3 (a pawn on the seventh against a rook): I think every promotion draws once the rook takes it and the kings are left; gen2 holds all four promotions equal, the two new records hold the queen and the rook only. A player would not look at the other two, so the new records are the closer reading (the accepted list has the knight promotion and not the bishop, which I cannot explain).
- A3 (a forced king move in a rook ending; the king is in check and must move): the move to the second rank, which defends the rook and attacks the enemy rook, is what a player plays. gen2 holds it equal with the first-rank move and picks the first-rank move; in the re-read for the printed cases both new records hold only the second-rank move at 64 s (in the ladder's own run the self-play record stayed open, so the search is clock-bound and not repeatable). The best line printed under every record still starts with the first-rank move: the line read and the search disagree again.
- B5 and B6 (a rook up with pawn pushes; a rook ending with a pawn two steps from queening) go the new records' way: the self-play record singles out an accepted move in both and the human record in B6, where gen2 holds two or eight moves equal and picks one that is not accepted. I could not solve B6 and I do not call B5's rook attack on the loose pawn wrong; it is not on the accepted list.
- B4 and A2 go the other way. With the pawn cheap against the rook (about a fifth to a quarter of it, against 65 pct in gen2) the new records hold more moves equal: a rook on the back rank 7 against 2, and the first move is a rook corner move where a player plays the rook to the file of the loose pawn; a king walk with a knight up 6 against 1 (all six win, I think; a player would say so too, and gen2 singled out the king walk).
- A5 (a bishop up, rook ending): 15 moves tied under every record, the same fifteen. A strong player would hold a handful; that is my judgement, not measured. Quiet positions with no capture in reach are untouched by the worths.
- A4 (lost position, a knight and king against a rook, knight and pawn): no judgement possible; the picks are not chosen by anything a player would name.
I am unsure of B6 (a rook ending where a pawn is two steps from queening; I did not solve it) and of the exact reason for A1 (the accepted bishop move), where all three records give the same single move.
READ (directions, one run each): THE DIVISION DOES NOT MOVE. The records that order the kinds as a player does change the rung of 71 and 76 positions, about ten times the change between two runs of the generation-2 record, and those changes go both ways: open rises by 5 and 2, rung 3 falls by 8 and 7, rung 1 and 2 each rise by 1 to 3. The tie sets do not shrink (mean 6.54 against 7.13 and 7.15); the hit of the search's own first move is level inside a band of about plus or minus 4. The worths are not the cause of the open positions: the open surprises are quiet positions where no capture is in reach (A5, and A6 where the gain is a promotion), and a ledger of captures prices nothing there; the promotion of a pawn is no capture. Next, as the plan said: the leaf's inputs, and what the judge counts where nothing is taken (units made by promotion).
STILL OPEN: one run per record on a loaded machine (the control's own difference from the 78.68 run is 7 positions); the clocks set the tie sets (equal moves at a fixed number of seconds depend on the nodes reached, so a loaded machine moves them); the heads are the same under every record; the opportunity to refit the heads' inputs on a record is not taken.

### PLAN 78.77: THE LINE AND THE SEARCH AT THE ROOT; A UNIT CHANGING KIND AS A LEDGER EVENT (2026-11-16, builder, for the main agent; serves SYSTEM_SPEC 4 "how a line ends" and "concrete", 5 worth, 6 the judge at the line's end)

WHY. The 78.76 READ named two faults: (a) a unit that changes kind by the rules is not an event of the capture ledger; (b) the best line the line read prints (mode 8) often starts with a move the search does not hold equal. Pieces: the line read (rust/engine/tactics/src/lines.rs, bound in py/src/lines_py.rs), the ledger judge (tactics/src/ledger.rs), the ladder's tools (discovery/ladder_measure.py Tools, threat_concrete.py Lines).
READ BEFORE BUILDING (code and one probe, before any body): the ledger ALREADY holds the event of (a). `Game::changed` (game/src/lib.rs, default `units_changed`: the mover's units before and after a move, the kinds that left paired with those that arrived, no game named) is read by `Search::gain` through `Judge::change` (`Worth::change` = worth of the new kind less the old, for the side that moved, from the same record) since plan 78.5 (b), commit 2e5caa04. A probe on a position where a move changes a unit's kind: the search and the line read score the move at the new kind's worth less the old, and a position where it cannot at 0. What the 78.76 builder saw is the PRINT: a line's events list (`LineRead.events`) shows only the units taken, and the settled length stops at the last taking. So (a) is not "add the event"; it is "make the event visible, and make its effect measurable by taking it away". No forbidden file (gdl/src/lib.rs, game/src/gdl_game.rs, game/src/kernel.rs) needs a change.
WHAT, (a). INTERFACE: `ledger::NoChange<J: Judge>(J)`: a judge that reads every `delta` and `worth` as J does and every `change` as 0 (the ablation: a unit changing kind adds nothing). `LineRead.changes: Vec<(bool, String, String)>` (was it `me`'s, the kind left, the kind arrived; "" = from nothing) beside `events`, the same ledger read for kind changes along the line; python `reads[i]["changes"]`. A parameter `kind_change` (bool) on `CE.read_lines` and `CE.solve_equals_batch`, DEFAULT TRUE = the behaviour of every earlier measurement (the default lives in the two pyo3 signatures, and in Python in `threat_concrete.Lines(kind_change=True)` and `ladder_measure.Tools(kind_change=True)`); False wraps the judge in `NoChange`. Called by: the ladder's Tools only (a sandbox). The Python mirror: `Record.change_of(from, to)` (worth of the new less the old) used by a test against Rust.
WHAT, (b). INTERFACE: read_lines mode 9: the line that starts with the LAST move of the game list (`read_line` from the position before it, for the side that played it): names with that move first, its events, value, end, settled, as any read. `Tools.line(position, scale)` reads mode 9 after the move the search chose at the clock just read (`last_move`), and falls back to mode 8 when none. A parameter `line_from` ("search" default of the PRINT, "root" the old mode 8) so the old print is reproducible. It decides no rung; it feeds `deep` and the features of rungs 3 and 0 only.
MEASURE. First the diagnosis of (b) on the 400 positions at the same clocks (1 s and 4 s): the share of positions where the line's first move is inside the search's equal set, before (mode 8 at the ladder's depth and fuse) and after (mode 9), and, for those where it is not, whether it is once the line is read to the search's finished depth with a large fuse (depth and fuse versus something else). Then rungs 1 to 3 on the same 400 positions and answers under gen2 and selfplay_78_58, each with kind_change True and False (ladder_compare for the division, ties, first-move hit and the rung-change table), and the 12 fixed cases of 78.76 and the first six positions whose rung changes with the event off, printed by ladder_print.py.
THE WALL as in the ladder. No oracle number in any fit or in anything the engine reads. One run each: directions, not verdicts.

FAULT (a) WAS NOT WHAT THE READ SAID. The ledger already scores a unit changing kind: `Game::changed` (default `units_changed`, derived by comparing the mover's units before and after a move, no game named), read by `Search::gain` through `Judge::change` (`Worth::change`: the new kind's worth less the old, for the side that moved), since plan 78.5 (b). A probe and tests show the search and the line read score a move that changes a unit's kind above the same position where it cannot. What was missing is the PRINT: `LineRead.events` lists only units taken. So the event was NOT added (it would duplicate a piece that exists); it is now listed (`LineRead.changes`, `reads[i]["changes"]`) and it can be TAKEN OUT: `ledger::NoChange<J>` and the parameter `kind_change` of `CE.read_lines` and `CE.solve_equals_batch`. THE DEFAULT IS TRUE (the event in the judge), which is the behaviour of every earlier measurement; this differs from the brief's "default to the old behaviour with the new event off": the old behaviour already had the event. Where the default lives: the two pyo3 signatures (rust/engine/py/src/lib.rs `solve_equals_batch`, lines_py.rs `read_lines`) and, in Python, `threat_concrete.Lines(kind_change=True)`, `ladder_measure.Tools(kind_change=True)`; a run is named `RECORD@on` or `RECORD@off` (`ladder_measure.split_run`). FAULT (b). The line read (mode 8) and the search are two readings of different depth: the line is read to a fixed depth (the ladder's DEPTH + 2 x the clock's index) while the search deepens to what its clock allows, and the search can decide by the forcing read, an operator the line read does not have. Not a bug: with the depth and the fuse matched the line's first move is inside the search's equal set in all but a handful. The print now follows the move the search chose: `read_lines` mode 9 (the line that starts with the LAST move of the game list, from the position before it, with that move's own events) and `Tools.line` reads it after `last_move` (`line_from="search"`, the default of the print; "root" is the old print). It decides no rung. The file line_root_measure.py (new) holds the diagnosis.

- B4 (black pawn on b2 about to queen, white pawn on d7 about to queen, kings a4 and c4; black to move): with the event off the search holds a pawn push and all four promotions equal and picks the pawn push; with it on it picks b1=Q alone, which the accepted list has. - A7 (black pawn c2, black king d2, white king f3, white rook c6): off holds three moves equal and picks c1=R; on holds the four promotions equal, picks c1=Q. The tie among promotions is the honest reading.

The accepted list has a5 only. A player would also like winning the knight; I am not sure black cannot stop the pawn, so I do not call off wrong, only note that the event moves the pick to the accepted queening line.

- A1 (black king b6, bishop e6, pawn f6 against a white king g7 and bishop d3): on holds Bg4 alone (accepted); the line it prints ends with the bishops traded and a lone king against two white pawns, which looks lost for black, so I do not trust that line's end as a reading of the position. The off run picks f5, not accepted and with no purpose I can name.
- A4 (black knight, king f3 against rook, knight, h-pawn): the h-pawn queens in every line (kind change printed); I cannot judge which knight move is best and trust neither pick.

### PLAN 78.78: THE SUBGOAL RULE SCORED ON THE OPEN SURPRISES (2026-11-17, main agent; SYSTEM_SPEC 7 holding a subgoal and navigating toward it, the hint; 9 a rule is scored by surprises resolved less created)

WHY. The open surprises are quiet moves among moves the search holds equal (78.68, 78.76, 78.77). By the spec the choice among them is the opportunity policy's: a subgoal as a HINT ordering the moves, never a value. The rule of 78.75 was measured only in matches, where its bands could not tell it from the control. It has not been scored on the list of open surprises, which is the sharper yardstick and already built (deep_heads.score, the scored part of the split).
WHAT (a measurement; a sandbox; no new method unless named here). Candidates, each a pick among the tied moves of a position, handed to deep_heads.score and hit_rate on the scored part: (1) move_rule.choose as built (threats first, then advance the held goal; no held goal at a single position, so the first goal of the order); (2) goals only; (3) for each of the first three goals of 78.74's order, the tied move that lowers layer one's count of own moves still needed the most (subgoal_goals.layer_one), ties to the search's first move; (4) the same over every goal, summed; (5) controls: the search's first move, a random pick. Also printed: for each open surprise whose accepted move is in the tie set, whether the accepted move lowers the count for ANY goal of the list, and for which rank of goal. That last number says whether the goals the proposer builds contain the reason for the accepted move at all, which is the ceiling of this whole approach.
INTERFACE. goal_pick(position, tied, goals, facts, mode) -> move, in a new file subgoal_pick.py; called by a measure script subgoal_pick_measure.py that reuses deep_heads.prepare, score, hit_rate, split_part and the ladder's Tools. Nothing else changes. The wall as in the ladder.
CASES. Twelve fixed positions chosen by rule before reading results, printed with the goals, the count per tied move and the accepted moves; at least five judged against the board.
READ BEFOREHAND: if the accepted move lowers the count of some listed goal in most open cases, the goals hold the reason and the work is ranking them. If it does so in few, the proposer does not yet build the goals a player plays quiet moves for, and that is what to build next.


### 78.78 BUILT (builder agent, 2026-11-17; serves SYSTEM_SPEC 7 "holding a subgoal and navigating toward it", the hint, and 9 "a rule is scored by surprises resolved less created"; one run on the scored part (206 positions), directions only; numbers only from the OBS lines in artifacts/experiments/subgoal_pick_78_78/full/ (obs_run1.txt, obs.txt, cases.txt, preps.pkl), untracked)

PIECE: the opportunity policy's choice among the moves the search holds equal. INTERFACE (written in the doc comment of subgoal_pick.py before its body): count_table(position, tied, goals) -> {"before", "after"} (per goal: layer one's own-moves count and the stoppers still in the way, recomputed on the graph after each tied move), goal_drop, drop, goal_pick(position, tied, goals, facts, mode, lists=None, scale="own") -> a tied move; modes rule, goals, top1, top2, top3, all; silent hint = the search's first move. subgoal_pick_measure.py: prepare_position, candidates, ceiling (reads the answers: beside the score, never seen by a pick), silence. ladder_print.py gained `--pick TAG` (the cases). No Rust change. Tests: tests/test_plan78_78_goal_pick.py (13, registered in scripts/gate.py).

COUNT AFTER A MOVE: a fact the graph tells true on the position after it is met (move_rule.fact_true); a step the move made is one move shorter (gone when none is left); subgoal_goals.layer_one is asked again. A goal with no count (layer one is None) counts as limit+1 so a move that makes it reachable lowers it. The table's before-count equals the goal's own_moves for every goal read (OBS: 0 differ).

WHAT THE RUN SHOWED (directions; one run):
- Layer one's count is not defined for most goals: None before the move for 1128 of 1254 goals of the scored part's ties. The hint by layer one is silent in 120 of 142 tied positions (84.5 pct); by the stoppers scale in 14 of 142 (9.9 pct).
- Net against the search's own first move (paired, 90 pct bootstrap), STAGE H lines: rule as built -2.0 [-10.0, +6.0]; goals only -1.0 [-9.0, +7.0]; layer one top-1 +0.0 [0, 0]; top-2 +0.0 [-2.0, +2.0]; top-3 +1.0 [-1.0, +4.0]; all goals +1.0 [-1.0, +4.0]; extras on the stoppers scale: top-3 +1.0 [-5.0, +7.0], all goals +4.0 [-5.0, +13.0]. Every band holds zero.
- Ceiling (65 open positions with an accepted move among the tied): by layer one, an accepted tied move lowers a count of some goal in 5 (7.7 pct), of the first three goals in 4, of the first goal in 1. By the stoppers: any goal 37 of 65 (56.9 pct), first three 14, first goal 1. THE BASE RATE: per tied move, accepted 31.0 pct [25.2, 37.4] against not accepted 29.0 pct [26.3, 31.8] (any goal, stoppers); first three goals 9.7 against 10.6; layer one any goal 3.2 against 2.3. The accepted moves are not separated from the others by the goals.
- READ BEFOREHAND, answered: the goals do not hold the reason in most open cases once the base rate is taken off; the proposer does not yet build the goals the quiet moves are played for (cases below). The 56.9 pct is mostly the base rate (a position has many tied moves, most of them move something).
- The cases (twelve fixed before reading: the first six open surprises with an accepted move in the tie set, the first six resolved positions the best candidate breaks), judged against the board in the report of this build: the purposes of the accepted quiet moves were of four kinds the goals do not list or cannot count: a unit of ours kept guarded or made safe (own pawns, own king against a check route), a square denied to their unit, a long march of a unit toward a target (goals for the targets exist, ranks 1 to 4, but the proposer counts only units within two steps of bearing, so a king march or a two-move bishop route lowers no count), and plain placement (nothing listed). The candidates that move the count pick captures and attacks on guarded units (stoppers scale) or a step that brings a unit to bear on a guarded pawn.


### 78.78 READ (2026-11-17, main agent; SYSTEM_SPEC 7, 9)

Merged; tests on main: test_plan78_78_goal_pick 13, 75_move_rule 24, test_plan78 17, all passed. No Rust changed. Full gate still owed.
SPEC CHECK of the builder: no departure. Its two extra candidates on the stoppers scale and the ceiling living in the measure file are accepted; move_rule._unit_stepped should get a public name when that file is next touched.
READ (one run, 206 positions, directions): the answer to the plan's question is the second branch. The goals as built do not hold the reason for the accepted quiet move. By layer one's count an accepted move advances some goal in 5 of 65 open cases, and layer one is undefined for about nine goals in ten, so the hint is silent in about 85 pct of tie positions. By the stoppers scale an accepted move advances some goal in 37 of 65, but a move that is NOT accepted does so as often per move (31.0 against 29.0 pct), so the scale carries no signal. No candidate separates from the search's first move.
MY READING OF THE CASES AGAINST THE BOARD (subgoal_pick_78_78/full/cases.txt). Set A case 1: I read the accepted move differently from the builder. The other side's far pawn is its only way to a new strong unit, and the accepted move puts our unit on the line that pawn must cross, so the purpose is to STOP THEIR GOAL, not to reach one of ours; the builder read it as a route toward their unit. Case 2: a long walk of our goal unit toward two far pawns, which are goals 1 and 2 of the list; the goal is there and the count cannot see a walk of five moves. Cases 3, 4 and 6 as the builder says: keeping our own units guarded and taking a place away from their unit.
WHAT IS MISSING, in the spec's terms: (1) every goal is "win one of theirs"; none is "stop one of theirs", though the proposer run for the other side would list exactly those, and a move of ours that adds a stopper to their goal or removes their step is the defence. This is the spec's opponent's veto read from the other chair. (2) Layer one is a count of own moves, and as built it is cut at two and undefined when any other fact is unmet; a walk of several moves is not counted as nearer. (3) The stoppers scale rewards bearing on a guarded unit and takings with no reply read.
NEXT: plan 78.79, the same proposer for the other side with our moves scored by what they cost its goals, and layer one as a true count of own moves with no cut at two, both scored by the same yardstick with the same base-rate check.


### PLAN 78.79: THE OTHER SIDE'S GOALS AS OURS TO STOP, AND LAYER ONE AS A TRUE COUNT (2026-11-17, main agent; SYSTEM_SPEC 7 reachable has two layers, the hint; 8 the threat list as the near case; 9 the score)

WHAT. (1) subgoal_units.every_unit and subgoal_goals.goals are run with the sides exchanged, giving the other side's goals at the position (no new proposer). For each tied move of ours, what it costs those goals: stoppers added, a step removed or lengthened, a goal no longer buildable. (2) Layer one as a count of own moves with no cut at two: for a goal whose only unmet facts are of bearing, the fewest own moves for some unit of ours to bear on the target, over the graph's own move relation, the other side not moving, up to a stated limit of the search and not of the design (print how often it is hit). A tied move is nearer if it lowers that count. (3) The stoppers scale with a reply read: a drop counts only if the line read after the move (mode 9) does not lose the unit that made it.
CANDIDATES for deep_heads.score on the scored part, with the two controls and the base-rate ceiling of 78.78 for each signal alone: defence only; long count only; replied stoppers only; defence first then long count; the sum. Nothing is fitted.
INTERFACE. subgoal_pick.cost_to_theirs(position, tied, their_goals, facts) -> table; subgoal_pick.long_count(position, goal, facts, limit) -> count or None; new modes of goal_pick. Called only by subgoal_pick_measure. The wall as before.
CASES. The twelve positions of 78.78 again, with the other side's first five goals in words and the cost of each tied move to them; five judged against the board.
READ BEFOREHAND: the test of each signal is its share among accepted tied moves against its share among tied moves that are not accepted. A signal with no gap there is dropped whatever its net.

### PLAN 78.80: SYMBOLS THAT GO WITH WINNING, AS SUBGOALS; FACT PATTERNS FIRST (2026-11-17, main agent; SYSTEM_SPEC 7 "subgoals as symbols that go with winning", 9 the score; Kaveh's idea and his word on the order: "sure your rec is good")

REUSE (history searched): the layer-2 patterns of plan 78.53 (patterns over the layer-1 graph matched and counted in Rust, sizes 1 to 3, kind-free and kind-bound, canonical form, the concepts file); the human sample and result head of 78.59; solve_equals_batch for the tie set; the base-rate test of 78.78; deep_heads.score for the ladder's list.
THE WIDER YARDSTICK. Positions from held-out human games (the 78.59 file) where the search at the wake's clock holds two or more moves equal and the move played is among them; several thousand, split by game into a FIND part and a CONFIRM part; endgame coverage printed. The ladder's 400 are in neither.
A SYMBOL is a pattern instance bound to its units; what a move does to symbols is the set of patterns it makes true and the set it makes false for each side (counted on the position after the move against the position before).
TEST ONE (goes with the result): on the find part, a head of the result on the count of units by kind, then the same with the pattern's count for each side added; the pattern's term and its band over games; confirm on the other part.
TEST TWO (the move played reaches it): per tied move, the share of played moves that make the pattern true against the share of the other tied moves that do, and the same for making it false; patterns chosen on the find part by a stated rule with the count of patterns tried printed, then read once on the confirm part with intervals. A pattern passes when both tests hold on the confirm part.
THE PICK: among tied moves, the one with the highest sum over passing patterns of a weight fixed on the find part (the log ratio of test two); ties to the search's first move. Scored three ways: agreement with the move played on the confirm part against the search's first move and a random pick; deep_heads.score on the ladder's scored part; the hit against accepted moves there. Nothing reads the oracle but the last two scorings.
INTERFACE. symbols.py: deltas(position, tied) -> per move the patterns made true and false; find(rows) -> passing patterns with weights; symbol_pick(position, tied, patterns) -> move. symbols_measure.py runs the stages. Game-free; the printing of cases in ladder_print.py.
CASES: the twelve positions of 78.78 with the passing patterns each tied move makes true, in words, and ten of the strongest patterns each shown on three positions; judged against the board: is the pattern something a player would call a purpose.
NOT IN THIS BUILD: the count of own moves until a pattern holds (layer one) and the pattern as an event class (layer two); they follow if patterns pass. No graph network.

THE CASES AND MY JUDGEMENT AGAINST THE BOARD (cases.txt: the twelve positions with, per tied move, the passing events in words; the ten strongest patterns each on three confirm positions with the units of one instance in brackets). I read each board twice (the printed board, then the move against it).
THE TEN STRONGEST. (1, 2: "their unit bears on an empty place and another of their units may move to that same place": two units of theirs contest one empty place.) Drawn on a black pawn d5 against white pawns d4 and e4 (the board is the position before; a6 pawn, Nc6, d6 and e5 pawns for black; I read the move as d6-d5): the move occupies the square the two pawns contest. A strong player would call it a central strike; the pattern is a side effect of that. The same pattern on Nxe7+ and on dxe4 is a capture removing one of the two units: an artefact of taking. (3, 7, 8: two of their units bear on the same empty place.) Drawn on Nxd5 (a bishop taken) and Bxd2+ and Nxe5: each is the capture of one of the two; an artefact of taking (62.3 and 57.8 to 58.0 pct of the carrying tied moves take a unit, by the report's lines). (4, 5, 6, 9: "their unit may move to / bears on an empty place", size 1, the four levels: the count of squares their units reach.) Drawn on black g4 (a pawn thrust that takes a square a white pawn on h3 controlled and attacks Nf3 and h3), black d5, a capture and a king move that takes the square a pawn could advance to (white Kb3, which attacks Na3 and the b4 pawn at once): these read as "restrict the opponent", which is a real strategic idea at the level of words, but in the drawings it is carried by pushing into a controlled square, by captures and by the side effect of a different purpose (the double attack); only 10 to 16 pct of its carriers take a unit, so it is not only taking. A purpose when it is a pawn thrust or a blockade, a side effect elsewhere. (10: "their unit bears on my unit and may move along that line"): the pattern is made false when my attacked unit leaves the line, is guarded off it, or the attacker is taken. Drawn on Nxe7+ (my knight leaves the queen's line with a capture and a check: a side effect of the tactic), on black f5 closing the c2-h7 diagonal of the white bishop (a real defensive purpose: shut the line to my h7 pawn; I would name it exactly so) and on hxg6 (taking the pawn that attacks my h7 and leaving the queen's file): of the ten this is the one a player would call a purpose of the move, relief of an attacked unit. Its test-one term is small and negative (the other side's count goes with my loss).
THE TWELVE POSITIONS (five read closely). A set 1 (black bishop, king b6 against the far h pawn and the a6 pawn; accepted Bg4): the pick is Ka7, because king-to-a7 blockades the white a pawn ("their pawn may move to a7" made false); the purpose of the accepted move (the bishop covers h5 against the far h pawn) is named by no passing pattern, and Bg4, Bd7 and Bh3 carry the same events (the bishop leaves e6, three equal sums); a miss, and it shows the patterns cannot see where a unit goes, only what it takes or blocks. A set 2 (the endgame with king f8 against pawns; accepted Ke7, Kf7): the pick Kf7 is accepted; the events are "my unit bears on two empty places along one line", which only a unit that goes along lines can carry, so every king move carries them and no knight or pawn move does: an artefact of the unit's kind (the pick says "move the king", which is right in this endgame and would be wrong in many). A set 3 (white rook b4 against king d5 and rook e3; accepted Rc4, a5, Kb2, Rf4): the pick Rc4 (accepted) rests on twenty near-identical events at about +1.9 each ("their king bears on my unit and may move"), i.e. a rook put next to the king and guarded by the b3 pawn; in a rook ending that is the real idea of cutting the king off, but the pattern does not ask whether the unit is guarded, and twenty twins add up as if they were twenty reasons (the sum 39.88 against 5.8 for Rf4, also accepted). A set 4 (black king f6 attacked by a knight g4; seven king moves tied; accepted Ke6, Kg6, Kg7): the pick Ke7 is not accepted; its events are the king's count of empty places going up on a more central square, a geometric fact (a king in the middle sees more empty squares) and no reason; an artefact. B set 3 (black Nd5 attacked by a pawn; accepted Ndf4, the single accepted move): the pick Ndf4 is accepted; its events are my knight bearing on a square next to their king and their pawn losing a move: Nf4 leaves the attacked square with a threat on d3 and e2, g2, which is exactly its purpose (a move with tempo toward their king's side); the patterns name the contact with their king, not the tempo. Of the twelve the pick is an accepted move in 6 (A2, A3, A5, B3, B5, B6) and not in the other six; I do not read that as a number to lean on.
WHAT A PLAYER WOULD NOT AGREE WITH: (a) a pattern every move of one unit kind makes true or no move of another kind can (the "two empty places along one line" events), (b) the capture families (any pattern that two or more of their units share loses an instance when one is taken), (c) near-identical patterns counted as separate reasons (twins and levels of one idea add their weights), (d) the mobility count, true of a king on a central square and of any piece with more free squares: no reason, (e) contact with their king taken without whether the unit is guarded.

STILL WRONG: the weights are the find part's log ratios of events that overlap heavily, so the sum is dominated by one idea counted many times (no reduction of twins beyond the 78.53 canonical form; a reduction test of 78.53's kind on the events is the next piece); the endgame is thin (about 3 pct of the kept positions at 8 units or fewer) and generated games were not added; the tie sets are wide in the opening (mean 12.6 moves; a few positions with 30 or more tied moves where the search at the wake's clock holds nearly everything equal), so the played move's share against "the others" there is a different question from the ladder's; test one's head is held and not refitted with each pattern; a pattern's term is fitted on all head rows with a free class shift, so a pattern that marks a phase gets credit (the head holds the units by kind, rating and ply, not the phase); the pick has no length (a purpose is a count of own moves until it holds: layer one, not built); a symbol that goes with winning is found, not shown to be a goal (nothing here says it can be reached or that reaching it helps: that is the layers of SYSTEM_SPEC 7 and the plan's "not in this build").
DEVIATIONS from the plan: (1) the head rows of test one are every fourth ply of every held-out game, not the tie positions alone; (2) test one is an offset fit with free class shifts, not a refit of the head's coefficients with each pattern; (3) the intervals of test two are cluster-robust delta-method intervals (games as clusters, a floor of the independent binomial variance), the shares smoothed by one half; (4) a forked pool hung after the head's fit had used the maths library's threads, so test one runs on a spawned pool; (5) the first full run was stopped in the deltas stage, before any CONFIRM row was read, to fix the two statistics (an interval that collapsed for an event that never occurs, and a term that took the head's miscalibration on the rows where the pattern occurs), and the later stages were run from there; the sample was kept (obs.txt holds both starts); (6) a stage `report` and the function `strongest` were added after the first look at the numbers, to measure the taking confound; it changes no pick; (7) the pattern level is sizes 1 and 2 at all four levels, size 3 not run (cost above). No Rust change, no change to rules/learned or data/derived, no oracle number outside the two ladder scorings of stage f.

### PLAN 78.84: WHY THE SEARCH HOLDS A MOVE THAT GIVES UP A UNIT EQUAL, AND THE HINT AFTER A ONE-REPLY READING (2026-11-17, main agent; SYSTEM_SPEC 5 the tactical reasoner decides and the hint only orders what it holds equal, 7, 8)

WHY. 78.83's worse picks are moves that lose a unit to the next reply, which the search held equal to sound moves. The spec's rule is that the reasoning decides and the hint chooses only among what the reasoning cannot tell apart. A move that loses a unit to one reply is something the reasoning can tell apart.
PART ONE, a measurement, no new method. On the tie decisions stored in the 78.82 and 78.83 match files (every tie decision that can be rebuilt, at least a thousand per band, by a fixed rule), read each tied move with the line reading that exists (threat_concrete Lines, read_lines, the same record and settings as the matches) and count: how often the tie set holds a move whose line gives up a unit for nothing while another tied move does not; by band of unit count; and for those, what the search's own numbers for the two moves were and at what depth, so that we can see why they were held equal (the depth reached, a bound instead of a value, a position already decided, or the way equality is read). Print twenty such cases through ladder_print with the line, and judge them against the board.
PART TWO, only reuse. A player whose tie set is first cut by that reading (a tied move is dropped if its line gives up a unit for nothing and some other tied move does not), then the reasons pick among the rest. Its time is CHARGED to the clock. Matches on sets A and B, same settings: this player with the hint in all bands against the control; the cut alone with the search's first move among the rest against the control; mid and few window with the cut against the control. The full gate is not run.
INTERFACE. symbols_play.py: a function sound_ties(position, tied) -> tied subset, built on Lines; MoverReasons(cut=True). If part one shows the cause is a plain fault in how the search reports equality, STOP after part one and report; do not patch the search.
READ BEFOREHAND. If the cut alone scores above half, the search at this clock is leaving material in its ties and the first debt is in the reasoner, not the hint. If the cut plus the hint lifts the mid and few windows, the reasons are worth more than an opening rule once the reasoner has done its part. If neither, the middle game needs purposes the reasons do not hold.

PART ONE (3600 tie decisions, 1200 a band; OBS lines). The match files keep a tie decision as its ply and size and the full tie set only where the pick differed, and keep none of the search's own numbers; so each decision is a POSITION taken from the stored games and the search is PLAYED AGAIN on it at the match's settings (0.2 s, ledger share 0.4, 9 workers); the tie set found again is the stored one in 802 of 860 (few), 766 of 825 (mid), 744 of 848 (many) where there is a stored set. WHAT THE SEARCH REPORTS: for a position the depth it finished, its value and whether the clock cut the equal reading; a root move is held equal by a null window "at least the best at depth D", a bound, and no value per move is reported. So the two moves' numbers are read as the search reads them: the position after the move searched with the ledger capped at depth D - 1 (its own gain added); that number for the search's own move equals the search's value in 156 of 163 / 333 of 340 / 354 of 357 flagged decisions (the instrument's consistency; a first pass had a wrong gain for a taking and was rerun, its file kept as reads_first_pass_own_gain_bug.jsonl).
CAUSES of the 862 flagged decisions (few / mid / many): the line's own value is NOT BEHIND although the events on its printed line show a loss 105 / 266 / 322; BELOW BEST (the move's value at the search's own depth is under the search's value: the equal reading holds it at a best it is not at) 34 / 39 / 8; BEYOND DEPTH, the bad move falls under the best two plies deeper 7 / 37 / 26 (one more not seen); SEARCH DEEPER THAN LINE 17 / 0 / 0; none DECIDED, none UNREAD. The clock cut the equal reading in 5 / 3 / 27 flagged decisions (a cut list does not say why a move is in it). In 118 / 282 / 342 of the flagged decisions the events of the bad move's printed line disagree with the line's own value (the line search's own number); the good move's line is above the search's value in 15 / 21 / 10 (the line is shallower than the search).
TWENTY CASES (cases.txt, 7 few, 7 mid, 6 many, the first flagged of each band in hash order), each read against the board with the units attacked and guarded printed: the move really gives up a unit for nothing in THREE (7: Rd3 leaves the pawn e6 to the king while c3 keeps it, BELOW BEST by a pawn; 12: e4 puts a pawn on a place a pawn attacks, no guard, BELOW BEST; 17: Ke7 steps onto the diagonal of a bishop behind a pawn, c6+ then takes the bishop on f8, found two plies deeper, BEYOND DEPTH); one unsure (14: Ke7 lets Qb4+ then Qxb8 take the unguarded knight, the line says the other knight on f3 falls in return); sixteen NOT: three are a change of kind or a gain the events leave out (1 and 2: a pawn runs to the last rank while the king takes a pawn, the events count the pawn lost and not the new unit; 3: Qh8 forgoes taking a knight, it hangs nothing), two are the printed line stopping in the middle of an exchange (6: the recapture is one ply past the line; 18: the queen is taken, the recapture comes after the printed line, the good move's line shows it), one is the line shallower than the search (4: a bishop that never leaves the king's reach, found by the search 13 plies deep), and the rest (5, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 15, 16, 19, 20) hang nothing by my reading, the line's own value is level with the best, and the loss shown is a pawn or knight traded off after the printed line. The stated cause was right in all twenty except where the measure first named the clock cutting the equal reading (6, 15, 16, 18), which says nothing of why the move is in the list; that cause was taken out of the order and counted apart.

The cause of most flagged decisions is not how the search reports equality but how the line reading's events are made (read off the printed line, which stops in the middle of an exchange, leaves out a change of kind and is shorter than the search): the events disagree with the line's own value, which is the search's own number, in 742 of the 862. WHY. The hint may only order what the reasoner holds equal, so the equal set must be right at the search's own depth; and every measurement that reads a line's verdict (ladder, threat list, the cut) needs the verdict to agree with the line's value.
PART ONE, the equal reading. Reproduce the BELOW BEST decisions of 78.84 (decisions.json and reads.jsonl hold them) as a fixed test set, with a fresh table and a node limit instead of a clock so that the result repeats. Find why ties() answers "at least the best" for a move whose exact value at the same depth is under it: candidates are table entries used across windows or depths, bounds stored from a pruned or reduced reading, the gain of the first move added twice or with the wrong sign, the stopped flag. Name the cause with one position traced step by step. If it is a plain fault, fix it in rust/engine/tactics (never the three protected files), with a Rust test from the traced position, and print before and after: the share of the test set still wrong, the size of the tie sets, the search's nodes and depth at the same clock. The verdict's net counts a unit changing kind (the event has been in the ledger since plan 78.5b and is carried by read_lines mode 9), and a line that ends inside an exchange is read on to a settled end or marked UNSETTLED instead of REFUTED. HOW IT WAS RUN: no clock in part one (a fresh table and node limits: deepening 150000 nodes, as the stored searches spent 110 to 130 thousand; fresh readings 8 million). The Rust extension was built with `maturin build --release --offline` into a private wheel and unzipped into a scratch folder first on PYTHONPATH; main's .venv extension was never replaced and needs a rebuild after the merge (new functions and a changed read). Some untracked artifact folders of main were symlinked into the worktree for reading (not committed).

PART ONE, THE CAUSE. The test set is the 81 decisions that 78.84 called BELOW BEST (testset.json). The fault repeats without a clock: the equal reading as it was holds a move that the reference puts under the best in 39 of 81 decisions (97 moves), mean equal set 6.56. REFERENCE = the same null-window question on a fresh table with the late-move reduction and the null move both off (alpha-beta and the table alone); it did not finish within 8 million nodes for some root move in 14 of 81 decisions (those moves are not counted). Readings that differ in one thing: a fresh table (cold) 39 of 81 (100 moves), so the table the run leaves is NOT the cause; null move off alone 39 (94 moves); late-move reduction off alone 18 (29 moves); of the 39 faulty decisions the fault is gone with the null move off in 3 and with the late-move reduction off in 24. The CAUSE is the forward pruning, mostly the late-move reduction, a deliberate heuristic that is not exact: a late quiet reply is read two plies shallower and the shallow answer is kept when it does not look better for the side to move. Asked "does this move hold at least the best at depth D", the reduction reads the other side's late quiet reply that wins a unit deeper at depth D - 2 and misses it, and the parent's bound is stored in the table at the parent's full depth. The null move accounts for most of the rest.
TRACED POSITION (decision 05b81540 of the test set; position text 8/8/3k4/7P/6K1/3N1P2/8/1r6 w: white king g4, knight d3, pawns h5 and f3, black king d6, rook b1; the deepening finished depth 12 at value 0): the move h5h6. Step 1, the child after h5h6 is asked in the window (-1, 0) at depth 11: pruned 0 (8256 nodes), null move off 0 (42781), late-move reduction off -56 (237245), both off -56 (1282029). Step 2, each of its 20 replies read in full (depth 10) and at the reduced depth (8): 19 replies give the same at both; the king step d6e6 gives -56 at depth 10 and 0 at depth 8. So the reply that refutes is read at the reduced depth, 0 is not under the window, and the node answers "holds". A Rust test of this position is rust/engine/tactics/tests/equal_reading.rs (the probe is at least 0 with the reduction and under 0 without it; `verify` drops the push).
THE FIX (ties() asks without the unsound pruning; the search keeps it): `Search::ties` reads in two steps. The first reading as before (warm table, the search's pruning; cheap) names the candidates; each candidate is asked again by `verify` on a fresh table with the late-move reduction AND the null move off; the moves that hold are returned. A move the first reading did not name is not asked again (a false negative of the first reading is a smaller set, not a false equal; the audit counts them). Where the clock or the fuse stops either step only the moves verified so far are returned (a cut is a smaller set, never an unverified move). Before and after on the 81 (same deepening, 150000 nodes): the equal set holds a move the reference puts under the best in 39 of 81 decisions before, 1 of 81 (1 move) after; mean equal set 6.56 before, 5.23 after (the reference's own 5.78); the reference holds 73 moves at the best that the new set leaves out (the first reading's false negatives); nodes of the equal reading mean 89479 before, 2692385 after (about thirty times); stopped by the node limit in 0 decisions. With the late-move reduction off only (null move on): 15 of 81 (23 moves), mean 5.52, 487566 nodes; so turning off one of the two is not enough.
THE COST AT THE MATCH'S CLOCK (ties_before.jsonl by main's extension, ties_after.jsonl by this build; 1200 positions, every third of 78.84's 3600 decisions, 0.2 s, ledger share 0.4): mean equal set 10.78 before, 4.32 after (few 8.78 / 4.78, mid 9.40 / 3.38, many 14.16 / 4.80); moves of the old set not in the new 7814, new not in old 62; depth of the ledger 7.36 / 7.35 (the same); nodes of the decision 87949 / 124521; seconds of the equal reading 0.035 / 0.097; equal reading cut by the clock 42 / 774 of 1200; equal sets of one move 31 / 479. At the match's clock the second reading is cut in most decisions, so the sets are sound but small.
OTHER READINGS THAT SHARE THE CAUSE (named, not fixed): `Search::gainers` (null window; the census), the census, the deepening's own value and line (the same pruning, at the root's window), every `read_line` / `read_lines` value (a fresh `run` with the pruning on: the line search's own number, so the verdict's `net_search`), and the density prior and the quiet wdl pick, which read `ties` in the engine's decision (cs_decision, operators.rs LedgerOp): they now get the verified sets and, at a short clock, smaller ones. The table is not the cause (a fresh table gives the same count of faults).

PART TWO, THE VERDICT (the 862 flagged decisions of 78.84, the bad move of each pair; `verdict_of` on the line read as it is now against the stored read; the line search's own number is the same in 862 of 862). Two changes. (1) `verdict_of`'s net counts a unit changing kind (`kind_change_net`: the mirror of `Worth::change`, for the side the line was read for; 0 when the read was made without the event). (2) The printed line of the search (the table's best moves) stops at the horizon, while the search counts the captures resolved there. `lines::settle_tail` reads the line on through them by the same rule (stand or take on; alpha-beta; a named fuse of 16 plies and 20000 nodes) and the events of the line then include the recapture; a tail the fuse stops marks the line `unsettled` and `verdict_of` says UNSETTLED instead of REFUTED. OBS: events and the line's own value disagree in 742 of 862 before and 7 after (few 118 to 3, mid 282 to 4, many 342 to 0); the bad move still gives up a unit by the events alone in 143 (862 before) and by the events and the line's own value in 133 (154 before); the kind change enters the net in 67; unsettled 10; decisions where the bad move still gives up and the good does not 141; the good move's line gives up in 2. A first tail without alpha-beta marked 130 lines of the many band unsettled by its node fuse; it was replaced (verdict_first_tail.jsonl).

### 78.85 READ (main agent, 2026-11-18; one run each, directions only; numbers from artifacts/experiments/reasoner_debts_78_85/full/)

MERGED, with one change of mine at merge: the second step of the equal reading is OFF by default (Params::default, Search::new, Search::with_fuse, LedgerOp::new, and the two binding signatures). Rust tests of cs_tactics and cs_decision passed; the extension in main was rebuilt; ten touched Python test files passed. The full engine gate is still owed.
THE CAUSE IS NAMED. The equal reading's fault is the search's own forward pruning: a late quiet reply read two plies shallower, and the null move. The table is not the cause. Traced on one position by the builder; I did not retrace it myself and take the trace from the printed values.
WHY OFF BY DEFAULT. Played against itself with the second step on against off, the engine scored level, with the same depth. The second step costs about two and a half times the seconds of the equal reading, is cut by the clock in about seven equal readings of ten at 0.2 s, and leaves an equal set of one move in nearly six of ten. A cut set is small because the clock ran out, not because the other moves were shown to be worse, so at this clock the switch mostly removes the hint's and the prior's room to choose without buying anything in play.
