### PLAN 79.03: THE SEARCH'S VALUE UNDER THE BEST IT COULD READ AT ITS OWN DEPTH (2026-11-19, main agent; SYSTEM_SPEC 4 the tactical reasoner's deepening and its prunings, 12 the debt of plan 78.84)

WHY. 79.02 found positions where a root move's full value at the finished depth is above the value the deepening reports, so the search plays a worse move than it could read in the same depth. Counted only in the firm room so far. If it is common in play it costs games directly, whatever the choice among equal moves.
SEARCH FIRST. The code of the deepening at the root (ledger.rs and the search under it): how a root move searched at a reduced depth or with a narrow window is handled when its answer comes back above the window (is it asked again at the full depth and the full window before the depth is called finished), and what the null move does at the root and one ply under it. Plans 78.84, 78.85, 78.97 for what was measured with the prunings off. State it in plain words before measuring.
PART ONE, the count (no engine change). On all sampled positions of 79.00 (not the room only), at the play clock under the human-result record: the share where some root move's full-window value at the finished depth D is above the reported value v, by how much in the judge's integers (a unit of the weakest kind or more, apart from less), by band; which pruning the played line passed through; and, from 79.00's stored labels, how often the played move loses the oracle's class in those positions against the rest. Node budgets for the audit, as in 79.02.
PART TWO, the mend, only if part one finds a cause that is a fault and not a price knowingly paid: behind a switch OFF by default in Params, with a Rust test, the binding row's first elements unchanged. The standard repair is the one to try first: a root move whose reduced or narrow answer is above the window is asked again unreduced with the full window before D is finished.
PART THREE, the measure. Depth reached and the share of positions with the fault at the play clock, switch on against off and off again as noise; the first move keeping the oracle's class on all positions with stored labels. Then play only by a rule written before the numbers are read: the stack's player (human-result record, 78.82's pick) with the mend against without, sets A and B, 0.2 s, min_pairs=60, sanity first.
JUDGE. Position 2 of 79.01 and fourteen more where the gap is a unit of the weakest kind or more: what the search plays, what it could have read, read against the board.
INTERFACE. Part one a measure module over the bindings (reuse cut_count, equal_trace). The mend in rust/engine, switch off by default. Outputs artifacts/experiments/best_79_03/. Nothing in play changes by default; nothing written to the real store.
READ BEFOREHAND. If the fault is rare over all positions or small in size, the reasoner at this clock is sound enough and the work goes to the value's inputs, on Kaveh's word. If it is common and the mend pays in play, it is a repair of the reasoner, put to Kaveh as a default with its size.


### 79.03 BUILT (builder agent, 2026-11-19 03:09, branch worktree-agent-a801c89e0ebe8f157; serves SYSTEM_SPEC 4 the tactical reasoner's deepening and its prunings, 12 the debt of plan 78.84; piece: tactical reasoning; part one and the measure are MEASURE modules, the mend is an engine change behind a switch `root_full` OFF by default; one run each, directions only; every number is an OBS line of artifacts/experiments/best_79_03/full/obs.txt, untracked; no oracle call was made, the wall test is kept; no match was played because the rule written beforehand was not met)

WHAT THE CODE DOES AT THE ROOT (first line of obs.txt, before any number): a quiet root move that comes fourth or later (not the table's best) is read two plies shallower first; if that answer is above alpha it is read again at the full depth with the same window, which at the root is open above, so a reduced answer above the window IS already asked again unreduced (the plan's standard repair is in the code). If it is not above alpha it is kept as a fail-low and never read at the full depth: that is where a root move can be lost. The null move is never tried at the root and, in the deepening, not one ply under it either (it needs a finite beta and the root's beta is infinite); it first applies two plies under the root. In the equal reading's null window both bounds are finite, so there it is tried one ply under the root.
INTERFACE. best_out, best_count (position_row, gap_kind, weakest_unit; STATEMENT), best_which (cause_of; four deepenings per position through the existing choice audit), best_mend (class_of, fault_of, conditions, Best: cut_mend.Mend's search with a switch as a parameter, the new `extra` argument of `search2`), best_play, best_cases, ladder_print --best03. Engine: `Search::root_full`, `LedgerOp.root_full`, `Params.root_full` (false by default), the binding's `solve_equals_batch(..., root_full=False)` (row unchanged, sixteen elements), and an INSTRUMENT not in the plan: `cs_tactics::gap_audit` and `cs_engine.gap_audit(...)` (the deepening's value and every root move's full-window value at a depth, the switch as a parameter; two searches, not nine), added because the full equal audit would cost half an hour an arm. Tiebreak mover: `root_full` key of the spec and a `depth_sum` stat. (iii) NO fix of the proposer names the quiet reply: the goal unit's fix is to take the shutting pawn (a taking) or to bring a unit by an EDITED text, and the edit path refuses a position the side not to move is attacked in (opposite_check), so the proposer cannot propose the bring that gives the goal unit a bearer, the answer's own kind of move. The missing questions: (a) "bring a unit to bear by a legal move" (needs no edited text: the graph after the move), (b) "add a bearer to the blocker's place so that bearers outnumber holders" (the quiet reply). The Rust port below answers (a) (`new_bearer_moves`); (b) is a join of what `lines_onto` already returns and is not yet a fact of a goal. The pieces mostly see the puzzle; the fault was that nothing called them and that (a), (b) were not questions.

### 79.07 BUILT, AMENDED (builder agent, same branch, 2026-11-19; the owner's amendment replaces item 2(b) and changes the goal unit's goal; Rust unit tests only)

THE OWNER'S WORDS (carried by the coordinator): no vocabulary special to the line to the goal unit; "what's stopping you from reaching your goal?", can I get rid of it: capture, pin, block, defend; the same machinery read from the other side is the defence.
REWORKED (the first build had item 2(b) as a special fact; it is gone):
- Removed: the fact `outnumbers`, its cause `held`, `Fact.counts`, `Goal.lines_onto`, `DoubleThreat` and `double_threats`. `lines_onto` and `goal_unit_lines` stay in wake.rs as readings of the graph for any place; no goal logic depends on them.
- The goal unit's goal is built from the same facts as any target's: its first fact is now `bears` (the Python's `borne_on`, same relation), with the same causes and fixes; plus only what the rules add for the goal kind (`covered`: the places it may move to; `forced_end`). The mirror test maps `borne_on` to `bears`.
- THE RECURSION (`goals(.., depth, cap)`; `GoalParams.depth`, default `DEPTH` 2, and the budget as the cap on subgoals): each stopper of the other side named by an unmet fact is a target with a goal of its own (source "stopper", the same four facts, read from the graph: no line is read for it). `Goal.parent` (the target of the goal it would unblock), `Goal.via` (the fact it stops), `Goal.depth`. A stopper that already has a goal of its own (asked on its own) is adopted: its parent is set, never a cycle. "Bearers against holders" is no fact: it is the ordinary `unguarded` fact of the stopper's own goal, with the ordinary fixes: remove a holder (the holder is again a target, one level down) and add a bearer (`new_bearer_moves`; added as the second fix of `unguarded`, and of `bears` for a threat that needs a quiet first move).
- THE DEFENCE: `answers_against(st, g, s, attacker, target, goal) -> Vec<Answer { mv, facts }>`: the legal moves of the target's owner after which a fact of their goal is unmet, named by the fact and nothing else: `bears` (no unit of theirs bears on the target any more: take the bearer, put a unit between, move the target away, one test), `unguarded` (more units of ours hold the place), `may_take` (the bearer is tied: its taking would uncover a line onto a unit of theirs, or leave their goal unit borne on). Only facts that are met now are addressed. Whether an answer works is the line read's verdict. `Proposal.defence` holds them for the rows against both sides (up to the budget); `named_moves` takes them (its last argument is now the defence) and names them at the position of the side that would play them.
- ONE MOVE UNDER TWO GOALS: `shared_fix_moves(goals) -> Vec<SharedMove { side, mv, under: [(target, fact)] }>`, a move that is a fix under two targets, reported once with both; `Proposal.shared`. It is the move-level source of the goals of two threats; `two_threat_goals` (the port of future_goals) stays as the mirror.

### 79.07 READ (main agent, 2026-11-19; unit tests only, as ordered; times are from a Rust test on one constructed position, directions)

MERGED (both sides had appended here; both kept). Rust tests passed on main (cs_tactics and cs_decision, 177), the extension rebuilt on main, tests passed (test_plan79_07_goals 9, 79_06_threats 6, 79_05_whole 5, test_plan78 17). Off by default; the old player unchanged, tested; a goal never changes a value, tested.
IN RUST NOW, as Kaveh corrected it: one way of asking for every goal. The same facts for every target, the goal unit's included, with only what the rules add for its kind. A stopper named by an unmet fact is itself a target with a goal, its parent recorded: the subgoal. Fixes are sets of legal moves, never an edited position. The defence is the same facts read from the other side: the moves that make a met fact of their goal unmet. A move that is a fix under two goals is reported once with both. The budget: units are asked in order of worth, the costly reading only inside the budget, one pass over the quiet moves for all.
THE TIME. Threats plus goals on the developed test position are near the play clock's slot and not under it at the default budget; nearly all of it is the first round's line reads, each with a table of its own, and the two reads of the forced end. The recursion and the defence cost almost nothing.
WHAT THE BUILDER SAW AGAINST ITS SMALL BOARDS AND I ACCEPT AS WORK FOR 79.08: too many moves are named (every move that brings a bearer onto a held unit; every move of an attacked unit away); the line read must keep only those that stand. A bearer that is tied to its goal unit still reads as free to take, because the graph's may_move does not read the goal unit's safety; the game's own legal moves must be read there. The other side's named moves are keyed at the position after a pass, which the search never meets below the root.
SPEC CHECK of the builder: section and interfaces named; no departure. It appended two BUILT blocks, one a build; accepted.


### PLAN 79.08: THE WAKE'S LOOP, THE WHOLE IN RUST, THEN THE POSITION (2026-11-19, main agent; SYSTEM_SPEC 8 all seven steps and the rule for choosing a move, 7 calculation and estimate decided together, 4, 11; piece: the wake)

WHY. Last of the ports of 79.05. After it every piece on the wake's path is in Rust, so the order Kaveh set moves on: unit tests a piece, then integration tests of the whole, then the position test.
A. REPAIRS FIRST, each with a unit test. (1) may_take reads the game's legal moves, so a tied bearer is not free. (2) The line reads made from one position share a table (cs_tactics::lines); the OBS line of threats plus goals on the 79.06 position is printed again; aim under the slot at the default budget. (3) Named moves of the OTHER side reach the search where it meets them: named for the side at the ply after ours, by the move's name, wherever that move is legal, not by a position key the search never visits. (4) Only fixes and answers the line read keeps are named: a named move is one whose line was read and not refuted, within the budget.
B. THE REMAINING PIECES, in Rust, unit-tested, mirrored where a Python original exists. Step 2, the frame read as the source of the threat list's rows (the Rust questions_threats is called in process; the graph rows remain the fallback). Step 1, the carry: a claim whose read set did not change is held, the others are read again. THE ESTIMATES, per goal and per frame, never one number for the whole position (section 7): the chance that a goal's unmet facts come true, read from a table keyed by what stops it (the table of plans 78.71 and 78.74, a parameter; absent means no estimate, said so); and the reasons' pick's score of a move (its patterns counted in Rust, its weights a parameter). The heads that read counts summed over the whole position are NOT ported and not called.
C. THE LOOP, `decide`, by section 8 and the rule for choosing a move, as a FIXED rule (the learned chooser comes after games are logged): (i) the carry; (ii) the frames and the threat list of both sides; (iii) the goals of both sides in order of stake, asked within the budget; (iv) THEIR goals that work now and are above the spread: our answers are named; OUR goals: the fixes of the goal with the fewest things in its way, the larger stake breaking a tie (PROPOSED order, section 13 item 26), are named; the nearest stopper of a far goal of high stake is the subgoal it gives; (v) the search reads with the named moves first and in full, for both sides; the judge's value is untouched; (vi) among the moves the search holds equal: one that answers their largest standing threat, then one that is a fix of our chosen goal, then the estimates; the subgoal is named; (vii) the chain of claims, each line with the reason it ended and the goal it served. THE DECISION LOG: for every candidate move at the root, what was calculated (value, equal or not, how its line ended), the goal it serves or answers, and each estimate; one record a decision, returned by `decide` and written by the caller. This is the learned chooser's training data later.
D. INTEGRATION TESTS, only when A to C are done: the wake end to end on constructed positions returns a move, a chain and a log; with every piece off it is the old player move for move; the wall; the value of a line is the same with and without the pieces; the whole decision's time by step as an OBS line.
E. THE POSITION TEST, only when D passes: a printing script prints, for the missed puzzle (before and after the taking) and the fourteen puzzles of 2026-11-19, the whole wake's decision at the play clock and at ten times it: the threat lists, the goals with what stops each and the subgoal, the named moves, the search's line, the choice and why, the time by step; beside it the old player's move. The builder reads at least five against the board and says where the reason is not a player's reason; the main agent reads them all before anything is called done.
NOT IN THIS PLAN: the 300 puzzles and any match (the main agent, after merge); any fit; the learned chooser; any oracle call or number; any Python wake.
INTERFACE. `decide` and `WakeDecision` in wake.rs gain the log; one binding for the whole wake; the printing script is the only place the game's own text appears. Outputs artifacts/experiments/whole_79_08/.

Off by default; with every piece off the wake is the old player move for move, tested; the value of a line is the same with and without the pieces, tested.
THE WHOLE WAKE IS IN RUST AND RUNS END TO END: the carry, the frame read, the threat list, the goals and subgoals, the named moves whose lines were read and not refuted, the search, the fixed rule, the pick's score and the chance of a goal as estimates, the log of every candidate. The heads over whole-position counts are not in it, by decision.
I READ THE MISSED PUZZLE'S PRINT AGAINST THE BOARD.
- At the puzzle: the answer's move is a fix under three goals, is named, and its own line is read and stands. The wake still plays the taking at the play clock, for the reason the old player did: the count at the end of the answer's line is under the count of the taking, and nothing told the search that the taking loses. NAMED, THEIRS is empty there, though the other side's goals in the same print hold the quiet reply as a fix (add a bearer to the unit that stops the line onto our goal unit).
- After the taking, from the other side: the goal against the goal unit, its stopper as a subgoal and the quiet move as its fix are all printed. The wake does not name that move and plays another, valued level. THE STEP THAT DROPS IT is the choice of the goal whose fixes are named: it takes the one goal with the fewest things in its way, here a unit of the weakest kind with one stopper, and names nothing for the goal unit's chain. Plan 79.08 C (iv) asked for both (the nearest goal, and the nearest stopper of a far goal of high stake); only the first was built. With no stake given, goals are ordered by facts alone.
- At ten times the clock the wake plays the answer and the old player does not; the wake ran over its clock and gave its search more of it, so that is not a comparison.
ON THE FOURTEEN the wake and the old player play the same move at both clocks, but for the missed puzzle at the longer one.
THE REASONS PRINTED ARE OFTEN NOT A PLAYER'S (the builder's reading of five, which I checked on three): a winning attack is labelled an answer to a threat because the move also happens to be in a list of answers; a forced end of the game is labelled the same way; a chosen goal with a chance near nothing is printed as the subgoal; one claim has no reason it ended.
THE CHANCE TABLE SAYS LITTLE: most goals of one position get the same chance from the same wide key.
THE COST: the whole decision is many times the play clock, nearly all of it before the search (the threat list's line reads, then the frame read, which asks thousands of questions and finds no row). The shared table did not cut the work.

### PLAN 79.09: WHICH GOALS REACH THE SEARCH, BY STAKE; THE CLOCK HELD; THE REASONS (2026-11-19, main agent; SYSTEM_SPEC 7 the stake orders goals and the budget, 8 the rule for choosing a move, 4, 11; piece: the wake)

A. THE STAKE, AND WHICH FIXES ARE NAMED (section 7: the stake orders goals; item 26 as written, both halves). (1) A goal's stake is the worth of its target's kind by the record, the goal kind above all; a subgoal carries the stake of the goal at the top of its chain. (2) For EACH side, the fixes named are taken chain by chain in order of stake: from the chain of the goal of highest stake, the fixes of its NEAREST subgoal (the deepest stopper with the fewest things in its way); then the next chain; so the goal unit's chain is always asked first and a far goal gives the reading only its nearest subgoal. The nearest goal of small stake comes after, if the budget lasts. (3) The other side's named fixes are read by the search at the ply after ours (named_ply), which exists.
B. THE CLOCK IS HELD. The steps before the search get a stated share of the clock (a parameter) and stop when it is spent: questions are asked in order of stake and the ones not reached are listed as not asked. The whole decision's wall time is within the clock; a test says so on constructed positions. The frame read that asks thousands of questions for no row is bounded by the same share and by stake. Print the time by step again.
C. THE REASONS. The reason printed for the move is the claim that decided it: a line that wins by its own reading says so and names the goal it serves; "answers a threat" only where a threat of theirs stands and the move's own line is not a gain; the end of the game forced is said as such; no claim without the reason it ended; a goal is printed as the subgoal only if a named move serves it.

A. THE TILT OF A NAMED MOVE (rust/engine/tactics/src/ledger.rs, `Search::fair_names`, `Search::fair_reread`; tests rust/engine/tactics/tests/named_fair.rs). Signature: `pub fair_names: bool` (default false everywhere; the wake sets it with its `direct_names` piece) and `pub fair_reread: FairCount {reread, understated, above}`. Where the best root move is a named one, every un-named root move that was only read reduced (a late-move reduction whose shallow reading failed low) is read again in full with the window of the best, before the depth is finished. CONFIRMED by the unit test, but only with several names: with one named move in 1194 cases at depth 5 and with five names at depth 7 no value was lower than a root read with no reduction; with twelve names a position (depth 6) the tilt shows. OBS tilt (named root moves: 12 a position, depth 6, one thread): cases 135, rivals read again 4925, of them at or above the named best 3508, strictly above 6; value raised by the repair in 2 cases, lowered in 0; nodes without 1876207, with 2766544. In both raised cases the search had a named move at value 0 where an un-named rival read in full is worth 85. Cost: about 47 percent more nodes in these twelve-name cases (a count of the rereads; the clock of the wake is held, so it costs depth at a clock, not measured). With nothing named the switch changes nothing (test).
B. THE WAKE AS A PLAYER (catspace/incubator/analyst/discovery/whole_play.py; interface and the format of the log in its doc). `MoverWhole` (kind "wk_wake", every piece on: carried, frames, threats, goals, two_threat_goals, reasons_pick, after_move, direct_names) only calls `BaseGraph.wake_decide` and writes the log; the old player is 78.67's own "tb_control", unchanged. The binding changed (rust/engine/py/src/base_graph_py.rs): `wake_decide(..., ledger_share=None, carry_slot=None)`; the binding holds the open tactics of the last decision of a slot (the game and the seat) and gives them to the next decision of the same slot, so the carry crosses no language boundary. The extension was rebuilt from this worktree (maturin develop --release); the editable install points here until the parent rebuilds main. LOG: one gzip file a game, `artifacts/experiments/whole_79_11/<tag>/logs/<match>/<gid>.jsonl.gz`, one JSON line a decision (position, legal moves, move played, the search's own first move, whether they differ and the reason class, the wall time, and the whole decision as the binding gives it: candidates with value, held equal, named, own line, what each serves or answers, the chance, the reasons' score, their goals after it; the goals, the threat rows, the names, the notes) and a result line at the end. About 3.6 kB a decision before compression (3.4 MB for 954 decisions).

A HANG FOUND IN PLAY AND REPAIRED: in the first runs two games hung, one worker each (a game ended with its position and the log's last line; the traceback of the watchdog shows the wake's call). Cause: the climb in `wake::decide` from the chosen goal to the far goal followed `parent` for ever when two goals named each other as parent (frames on; reproduced on one position, with the piece "frames" alone). The climb now takes at most one step a goal. Test: tests/test_plan79_11_play.py (a subprocess with a time limit). `play11` keeps a watchdog of 300 s a game (faulthandler: the traceback is kept and the worker ends). Match m1 B had its hung game played again after the hang, and m2 B (stopped at 180 of 200 by a second hang) its last twenty games, with the repaired build (the harness skips the games done); every other game was played once. The games of m1 A, m1 B (199 games) and m2 A were played by the build with the hang present; a hung game never ended, so no result of a finished game depends on it. Pre-existing since 79.08 (the frames piece): any earlier puzzle or match run on a position of this kind would have hung.
E. THE JUDGE (whole_79_11_print.py; output artifacts/experiments/whole_79_11/full/twenty_print.txt): 586 decisions in the logs in which the wake's move differed from the search's first move (answers_threat 27, estimate 31, fixes_goal 303, own_line_wins 225); twenty printed round robin over the reasons. THE BUILDER'S READING of ten against the board (1, 3, 5, 6, 9, 13, 14, 16, 19, 20):
 - 6 and 9: the wake plays the move whose line ends the game (the log's value is the end of the game) where the search's first move is worth a few pawns: a strong player agrees.
 - 20: the wake plays the rook check on the second rank (protected by the bishop, wins a bishop: value 1301) where the search's first move reads 0: agrees. 13: the search's first move reads -1216 at the equal reading (it loses a unit) and the wake plays the move that holds; agrees, but the log says the reason is "estimate", which is not why (see below).
 - 5: the pawn attacks the knight the goal is on: agrees. 19: the bishop leaves the knight's attack for a square that keeps it: agrees, the two moves are equal.
 - 16: both rook moves answer the threat on the rook; the log says "answers the threat" but what chose between them was the estimate: a strong player would call the reason incomplete.
 - 1: the bishop check as "a fix of the goal on the king (bears)": a player says "I give a check"; it is the same thing in the goal's words; value 0 for every move held equal.
 - 3: the quiet pawn move said to serve the goal on the king "(covered)" and "its own line was cut by the budget (unread)": a stretch; a player would attack the rook on the second rank (the search's first move) before preparing; the reason offered is weak.
 - 14: king and pawn against king; the wake plays the king move, the search's first move is the pawn push; both win at depth 17, the score that chose is 0.0026 against -0.0: noise, and a player would push the pawn or say why the king move is needed.
 WHAT A STRONG PLAYER WOULD NOT AGREE WITH: (1) the reason class is the class of the set, not of the difference: where both moves answer the threat or both fix the goal, the estimate chose between them, and the log says "answers the threat" or "a fix of the goal". (2) A move the search's own reading put first can have a lower reading at the equal reading (13, 20: the value of the search's first move in the log is the null-window answer below the best); the wake's difference from the search is then the verification doing its work, and the reason printed is "estimate" or "fixes_goal", not that. (3) A goal "covered" or "bears" served by a quiet pawn move (3) is said in the goal's words, which a player does not use.

In section 12, the wake should read: carried tactics are kept by the binding per slot; the old player and the wake can be played in the match harness (`whole_play`), with a log of every decision as the learned chooser's data; the frames piece no longer hangs on goals that name each other. In section 13 a question for the owner: the reason printed should name what separated the move played from the search's first move, and the log should say when the search's first move was not held at the equal reading.


### 79.11 READ (main agent, 2026-11-19; one run a match, directions only; numbers from artifacts/experiments/whole_79_11/full/obs.txt)

MERGED. Rust tests of cs_tactics and cs_decision pass on main (241); test_plan79_11_play 10, 79_10_after 6, 79_08_wake 5, test_plan78 17 pass. The full gate was not run.
THE WHOLE IN PLAY IS LEVEL WITH THE OLD PLAYER AT EQUAL TIME. At equal mean wall a move the bands of both sets hold a half (set A 0.5150 [0.4850, 0.5450], set B 0.5175 [0.4925, 0.5426]). At the same clock given the wake is above a half on both sets (0.5542 [0.5250, 0.5833] and 0.5700 [0.5425, 0.6000]), but there the old player spends about 0.59 of its clock, so that is the time and not the pieces. Between a quarter and a third of the games reach the ply cap and count as draws.
WHAT THE PIECES COST AND GIVE. At equal wall the wake's search reads about one ply less than the old player's (6.39 against 7.39 on set A, 6.51 against 7.35 on set B) and the score is level: what the pieces give pays for the ply they cost and no more, yet.
THE WAKE DIFFERS FROM ITS OWN SEARCH'S FIRST MOVE IN UNDER 2 PCT OF DECISIONS. Among the moves the search holds equal it mostly keeps the first.
ON THE BOARD, all twenty printed decisions read by the main agent (the builder read ten). Clearly the better move in five (6, 9: a line that ends the game; 13: the search's first move loses a unit at the equal reading; 20: wins a unit; 10 by a little). A player's move with a reason a player would give in four (5, 7, 11, 18). In eleven the two moves are the same to a player and the pick is a coin. None of the twenty is clearly the worse move.
THE REASONS PRINTED ARE NOT YET A PLAYER'S IN ABOUT HALF. (a) The reason is the class of the whole equal set, not what separated the move played from the first (16, 17, 19: both moves answer the threat, the estimate chose). (b) Where the equal reading put the search's first move lower (13, 20) the cause is the verification, and the log says "estimate" or "answers the threat". (c) A quiet move is said to serve the goal on the goal unit through "covered" (3, 8); a taking of a unit is said so too where a player says it takes a unit.
THE ESTIMATE STEP IS STARVED AT THIS CLOCK. Nineteen of the twenty carry the note that the clock ended before the reasons' score of most moves, and in two the moves held equal were themselves not all scored, so the estimate did not decide. The moves held equal should be scored first.
A HANG, found by play and repaired: two goals that name each other as parent made the climb to the far goal loop for ever (in main since 79.08). Bounded; a regression test; a watchdog a game in the harness.
THE LOG EXISTS: about 33 thousand decisions with the game's result, each with every candidate, its value, whether held equal, what it serves and answers, its chance and score, their goals after it. BUT under the fixed rule only the move played has a result behind it, and the rule plays the same kind of move every time, so the log cannot say what another equal move would have brought. A chooser fitted on it would learn the rule back. Games in which the choice among equal moves is varied are needed first.
SPEC CHECK of the builder: sections 8, 7, 4, 11 named, no departure; its choices are listed in its BUILT block and in section 13 item 29.


### PLAN 79.12: THE CHOOSER'S FIRST FIT, FROM GAMES IN WHICH THE EQUAL MOVES ARE VARIED (2026-11-19, main agent; SYSTEM_SPEC 7 calculation and estimate decided together points 4 to 6, 8 the rule for choosing a move and the wall, 9 sleep; piece: the wake's last layer)

WHY. Section 7 point 5: the fixed rule first, the chooser trained after the whole wake has logged games. The games are logged (79.11). Point 4: a learned last layer decides, trained in sleep on results only; the estimates are its inputs and never add to the judge's value.
SEARCH FIRST. What the repo has for fitting a choice from results (78.78 goal pick, 78.81 and 78.82 the reasons' pick, 78.96 the prior, the stop policy notes); reuse, duplicate none. Print the table before code.
PART A, THREE REPAIRS FROM 79.11'S READ, each with a Rust unit test first. (1) The reason names WHAT SEPARATED the move played from the search's first move: the equal reading put the first lower (say so and by how much); only the played move answers a standing threat; only it fixes the goal named; else the estimate, named as such. The log carries a field for the first move not held at the equal reading. (2) The estimates are computed for the moves held equal FIRST, then for the rest while the clock lasts. (3) The log carries the wall of each step of section 8 for the decision, and the print gives the mean a step over a match: where the ply went.
PART B, THE LAST LAYER IN RUST, interface first. `chooser.rs` in cs_decision. Takes: the candidates the search holds equal (the wall stands: it never picks a move the calculation holds worse), and for each a row of named inputs, every one already in the log: is it the search's first; did the equal reading keep the first; does it answer a standing threat and that threat's stake; the stake and the things in the way of the nearest goal it fixes and of the top of that chain; that goal's chance; the reasons' score; their chain after it (things in the way before and after, taken out, put in); is it a taking and of what stake. Takes also a table of weights, one a named input, and a mode: Fixed (section 8's rule, as now, the default), Weights (the largest weighted sum plays), Explore (one of the equal moves uniformly at random from a seed given, the propensity logged). Returns the index, the inputs and the weighted sum of every candidate for the log. No input names an object of the game. With no weights and mode Fixed the wake is move for move what it is on main (test).
PART C, GAMES WITH THE EQUAL MOVES VARIED. The whole wake against itself and against the old player in mode Explore on every decision with two or more equal moves, sanity of 20 games first, then about 2000 games at 0.2 s, 9 workers, opening sets A and B and, if the harness has more openings, others, never the sets used to judge in part E. Log as 79.11 plus inputs and propensity. Print: games, decisions with two or more equal moves, the spread of each input over them, and the endgame coverage of the sample.
PART D, THE FIT, IN SLEEP (python allowed here, nothing of it in the wake). Target: the game's result from the mover's side, results only. Rows: the decisions of part C with two or more equal moves, the inputs of the move played less the mean of the inputs of its equal set, so that only what distinguishes the move within its set is weighed. A logistic fit with a penalty, games split by game into fit and held-out, the weights printed with a band by bootstrap over games. Print beside it what a fit with shuffled results gives. If no weight's band is clear of nought on held-out games, say so and stop before part E: the inputs do not tell equal moves apart by result at this sample, and that is the finding.
PART E, THE WHOLE WITH THE CHOOSER, only if part D gives weights. Wake with mode Weights against wake with mode Fixed, and each against the old player at equal mean wall, on sets A and B, 0.2 s, ply cap 120, settled with min_pairs=60, a quiet machine, one match at a time. Then twenty decisions where the chooser differs from the fixed rule, printed with the inputs and weights that decided, read against the board by the builder and the main agent.
NOT IN THIS PLAN: any oracle call or number; any input that is a count over the whole board; any weight added to the judge's value; a table of estimates by frame (none exists yet; its place among the inputs is kept empty and noted in the log).
LIMITS THAT STAND: as plan 79.11.
READ BEFOREHAND. Two thousand games give a few tens of thousands of varied decisions and one result a game; the signal of one equal move in a game is small. Weights no clearer than the shuffled fit would not be a surprise. Then the next step is more games or stronger inputs (the estimate by frame, a real chance of a goal), not a larger model.

For fitting a choice from results the repo has 78.78 (goal pick), 78.81 and 78.82 (the reasons' pick, whose weights the wake already reads) and the 79.11 log; none fits a choice among the moves held EQUAL from varied games, so the fit is new (chooser_fit.py); it reuses the harness (whole_play, tiebreak_measure.run_games and settled), the reasons' score (pick.rs) and scikit-learn.
A. THREE REPAIRS (rust/engine/decision/src/rule.rs `why_against_first`, `FirstFacts`; pick.rs `scores_must`; log.rs; wake.rs; unit tests rust/engine/decision/tests/chooser.rs, written first). (1) Where the move played is not the search's first, the reason names what separated them, in this order: the end of the game forced (as before); the equal reading put the first lower (with the amount where the null-window reading is known); only the move played has a line that wins by its own reading; only it answers the standing threat; only it fixes the goal named; else "nothing separates it ... but the estimates" (and where both answer or both fix, it says so). (2) `scores_must`: the moves held equal are scored first AND whatever the clock says (they are what the estimates decide among); the others follow while the clock lasts. THE TWENTY DECISIONS (twenty_print.txt: the first twenty, in game order, of the 496 decisions of weights v fixed set A in which the chooser's move differs from the rule's pick; the reason class of all is "chooser" by construction, so the round robin over classes is one class). THE BUILDER'S READING against the board: with one weight the chooser plays the move with the highest reasons' score, and the rule's ladder (answer a threat, then fix the goal) is gone. In most of the twenty (3 to 8, 11, 17, 18: quiet developing positions with 5 to 19 moves held equal) the chooser develops a knight or bishop or moves a pawn where the rule plays the bishop move that fixes a goal: to a player the moves are the same, none clearly worse. In 10 the chooser's move is also the search's first and takes a rook where the rule's pick answers a threat on a rook and leaves the rook: the chooser is plainly better. In 13 and 16 the rule's pick is a rook move that fixes the goal on the goal unit and the chooser plays another rook move or a rook to the second rank; in 12 the chooser pushes a pawn near the goal unit where the rule moves the bishop that fixes the goal: a strong player would prefer the move that serves the goal in these three, so the chooser looks a little worse there. In 1 and 2 (an ending of rook, bishop and knight against a rook) the chooser pushes a pawn or moves a bishop where the rule moves the knight or rook: the same to a player. WHAT A STRONG PLAYER WOULD NOT AGREE WITH: the chooser has no reason in words (a weighted sum of inputs is not a reason), and it drops the fix of the goal for a score that is an estimate of a pattern count. The main agent's reading of the twenty is left to it.
NOT BUILT: an estimate by frame (no table; the place is empty), a weight for any input other than reasons_score (none else was clear), any oracle number, any input that is a count over the whole board (the units-on-board count is used only in the coverage print and never reaches the chooser), any use of A or B as training games.
CHOICES NOT IN THE SPEC: the candidates of the layer exclude a search's first move the equal reading dropped (the rule on main may still pick it; the layer never does); the rows are logged in every mode where a chooser is given (Fixed included) and never where none is given; the stake of a threat or of a goal that is the goal kind becomes a flag with the finite stake at nought; the taking of a unit is read from the place the move ends on and the units standing there; the opening set T (300 pairs) is made here by the rule of the sets C and D because they hold 200 pairs and 1000 pairs a mix were wanted; both colours of a self-play game are one opening twice, with different draws; unfinished games count as draws (0.5) in the target, as in the harness; "clear on held-out" is the held-out refit's band excluding nought with the fit half's sign; the weights written are the clear inputs refit on all games; the scale of equal wall is the scale of 79.11 (copied into whole_79_12/scale_from_79_11.json); `scores_must` makes the estimates of the moves held equal independent of the clock, so mode Fixed is move for move the wake of main wherever the clock reached them before, and may differ where it did not (the point of repair 2).
SPEC CHECK: sections served: 8 (the rule for choosing a move, the wall, the whole is judged), 7 points 4 to 6, 9 (the fit is sleep), 4 and 11 (hot path in Rust; the fit is Python and outside the wake). Interfaces added: cs_decision::chooser (`INPUTS`, `MoveFacts`, `inputs_of`, `Mode`, `ChooserSpec`, `apply`), `rule::why_against_first`, `rule::FirstFacts`, `pick::scores_must`, `WakeInputs::chooser`, `DecisionLog::{first_held, first_lowered_by, step_seconds, chooser}`, the binding's `chooser` argument; whole_play `chooser_arg`, `chooser_kw`; whole_79_12 and chooser_fit as written. Departures: none found. In section 12 the wake should read: a last layer among the moves held equal (Fixed, Weights, Explore) with named inputs, whose rows and propensity are logged; a fit in sleep exists (chooser_fit) and found one weight (reasons_score) not distinguishable from the shuffled fits. Section 13 question for the owner: a quarter to a half of the games reach the ply cap, so a result is mostly a draw; a result-based fit of equal moves needs either more decisive games or a target that is not the result of the whole game.

### PLAN 79.13: A CHANCE OF EACH GOAL COUNTED FROM PLAY, AS THE CHOOSER'S INPUT (2026-11-20, main agent; SYSTEM_SPEC 7 calculation and estimate decided together point 2 the estimate per goal, and "among equal moves we optimize for the prediction, whichever gets us closer to our goals"; 6 the event heads; 9 sleep; piece: the estimate per goal)

WHY. The chooser's inputs say nothing by the game's result (79.12). His rule for equal moves is progress toward the goals, and that needs a prediction that a goal is reached. The chance table we have (78.74) gives nearly the same number to every goal. The 79.11 and 79.12 logs hold about 180 thousand decisions with every goal of both sides and the game that followed; whether each goal was then reached is an event in play, counted without any oracle and far more often than a game's result.
SEARCH FIRST. 78.74's table and its keys, the event heads of section 6 (78.64, 78.77), `estimate.rs` ChanceTable; reuse, duplicate none. Print the table before code.
PART A, THE EVENT, interface first. For a goal logged at a decision: REACHED when within the next K plies of that game the target was taken by the goal's side and the side was not behind by the count of worths over the same plies; for the goal kind, when the game ended for that side. K printed for three values and one chosen by the plan's rule: the smallest at which nine in ten of the goals ever reached are reached. A measure module over the logs; no engine change. Print: goals, reached share, by side to move and by whether it is the mover's goal.
PART B, THE TABLE, in sleep. Keys from what the log already holds for a goal and names no object of the game: the facts unmet (set), the things in the way, the depth in its chain, the rank of the target's stake among the kinds, whether a working fix exists, whose move it is, its class word (unread, refuted, two_moves and the like). Back off from the full key to fewer fields by a floor on the count, as 78.74 does. Games split by game into fit and held-out. Print beside the old table on held-out goals: the log-loss, and the reached share by tenth of predicted chance (is a goal said to be 0.3 reached about three times in ten). If the new table is no better than the old on held-out goals, say so and stop: the log's facts do not predict a goal being reached.
PART C, INTO THE WAKE, Rust. The table is given through the binding in the place of the old chances (the same ChanceTable or its extension, interface first); each goal in the log carries the new chance. For each candidate move the chooser gets two new named inputs: the gain in stake times chance summed over our chains from before the move to after it, and the same for their chains (read from `after.rs`, which already reads their goals after each of our moves; ours after our move is read the same way, graph only, within the clock, cost printed). Unit tests first; default unchanged.
PART D, TWO CHOICES TO JUDGE AS THE WHOLE. (1) Mode Weights with a hand-free fit: 79.12's fit repeated with the two new inputs on new Explore games, shuffled control beside it. (2) His rule read plainly, no fit: among the equal moves the largest (our gain less their gain), the fixed rule's order kept above it for an answer to a standing threat. Each against mode Fixed and against the old player at equal mean wall, sets A and B, 0.2 s, settled with min_pairs=60, a quiet machine, one match at a time. Twenty differing decisions printed with the chances that decided, read against the board.
PART E, MORE GAMES THAT END. A short run of 200 Explore games at ply cap 200 beside cap 120: the share of games that end on a result and the wall. Printed only; the cap is not changed here.
NOT IN THIS PLAN: any oracle call or number; a table by frame (it follows the same way if the table by goal predicts); any weight on the judge's value.
LIMITS THAT STAND: as plan 79.12.
READ BEFOREHAND. If part B's table predicts and part D is still level, then equal moves are equal and the gain to look for is not among them: it is in what the search reads (names from goals with a high chance, a deeper reading of them), which is where a chance would then be spent. If part B's table does not predict, the facts of a goal are too coarse and the subgoal vocabulary is the thing to work on.

### 79.13 READ (main agent, 2026-11-20; one run, directions only; numbers from artifacts/experiments/whole_79_13/full/table_obs.txt, obs.txt and fit/)

MERGED. Rust tests of cs_tactics and cs_decision pass on main (263); test_plan79_13 15, 79_12 9, 79_11_play 10, 79_10_after 6, test_plan78 17 pass. The full gate was not run.
THE CHANCE OF A GOAL, COUNTED FROM OUR OWN GAMES, PREDICTS. On held-out games the new table's log-loss is below the old table's recalibrated and below the base rate, the bands clear of nought (0.53040 against 0.57138 and 0.57176 at the window of 60 plies; the same direction at 8 and 16). What it says is about what happens: goals given about 0.07, 0.12, 0.26, 0.34, 0.43 are reached about 0.06, 0.12, 0.26, 0.33, 0.41 of the time; above a half it says a little too much, on few goals. The old table as logged gave nearly every goal the same number. This is the first estimate per goal of section 7 point 2 that says something. No oracle was used.
THE WINDOW. The rule for K picked the longest offered, 60 plies, because goals go on being reached evenly with no knee. A goal reached sixty plies later is hardly the same goal; the shorter windows are kept beside it.
AMONG EQUAL MOVES IT CHANGED NOTHING, AND THE TEST OF THE PLAIN RULE WAS NOT A FAIR ONE. (1) The fit with the new inputs on 2000 new games does not beat the fit on shuffled results (held-out log-loss 0.69313 against 0.69315 for nought weights); not played. (2) The plain rule (largest gain of ours less theirs) is level with the fixed rule (0.5175 [0.4950, 0.5425], 0.5225 [0.5000, 0.5450]) and against the old player at equal wall gave 0.5571 [0.5286, 0.5893] on set A and 0.5150 [0.4900, 0.5425] on set B, not told apart from the fixed rule's. But the rule as the main agent wrote it has two faults the builder found on the board: a move that meets a goal's last unmet fact makes the goal leave the list, so progress LOWERS the gain; and the reading after a move builds chains only on the goal unit, so the part of the gain with a finite stake is nought on every row. In about fifteen of twenty differing decisions it dropped a fix of a goal for a move that serves nothing. The main agent's error in the plan, stated.
WHAT THE THREE PLANS SAY TOGETHER. The fixed rule, a fitted chooser, and a rule that by its fault picks against progress in 8.5 pct of all decisions, all score the same against each other and against the old player. So at this clock the choice among the moves the search holds equal moves the result too little to see in a few hundred games. The gain to look for is not there. It is in what the search reads and how deep: the wake reads a ply less than the old player, and a quarter of its clock goes to the frame read and the threat list.
GAMES THAT END. At a cap of 200 plies 95.5 pct of the games end on a result against 52.0 pct at 120, for about an eighth more wall. Training games use 200 from now (reading of the main agent, section 13 item 31); judging matches stay at 120 so they compare with the earlier ones.
A FAULT ON MAIN MENDED BY THE BUILDER: chooser_fit wrote weights when one input was clear; it now writes only when the fit beats the shuffled fits.
SPEC CHECK of the builder: sections 7, 6, 8, 9 named; four inputs where the plan said two (the goal kind's part kept apart so no worth is invented for it), accepted.


### PLAN 79.14: THE PLY BACK, AND THE CHANCE SPENT ON WHAT THE SEARCH READS (2026-11-20, main agent; SYSTEM_SPEC 8 the wake step by step and "a piece that costs too much is made cheaper, not turned off", 7 point 1 calculate what is near and point 2 the estimate per goal, 4 the order of questions; piece: the wake)

WHY. 79.11 to 79.13: the whole is level with the old player at equal time while reading a ply less, and the choice among equal moves does not show. Two things follow. The steps before the search cost a quarter of the clock; made cheaper, the whole keeps its pieces and reads as deep. And the chance of a goal, which now predicts, has not yet been used where it can matter: in which moves the search is told to read in full and first.
SEARCH FIRST. The carry (78.70, 78.72, carry.rs), the frame read's cost by part, the threat list's deadline and budget (79.09), `named_fixes` and `names_of` (79.09, 79.10), NAMED_BUDGET; reuse, duplicate none. Print the table before code.
PART A, WHERE THE QUARTER GOES. From the step walls in the logs and a profile of one hundred logged positions: the frame read and the threat list broken into their own parts (which questions, which units, how many are asked again that were asked the move before and came out the same). Printed before any change.
PART B, THE STEPS MADE CHEAPER, NONE TURNED OFF, Rust, unit tests first. In the order the profile says pays most. Meant, not prescribed: (1) what the last decision of the same game already answered and the two moves since did not touch is carried and not asked again (the binding already keeps a carry per slot; "did not touch" is read from the graph: no unit of the row moved, was taken, or had a line onto it opened or shut); (2) the frame read and the threat list share the readings they both make; (3) rows are asked in order of stake and the step stops at its share, as now. Every carried answer is marked carried in the log. A test that on a sample of logged positions the carried answers equal the answers asked afresh; where they differ the builder says why before going on. Target printed, not promised: steps 1 to 4 under a tenth of the clock, the search's depth at equal wall within a third of a ply of the old player's.
PART C, THE CHANCE ORDERS THE NAMES. The named moves go to the search in the order of stake times the table's chance of the goal they fix (now: stake alone, nearest goal first), ours and theirs, the same budget. The goal table of 79.13 at the window of 16 plies is given through the binding; with no table the order is as on main (test). A goal whose every fact is met is not dropped: it is the nearest of all and its fix is named first.
PART D, THE GAIN MENDED, small. In gain.rs a goal met by the move counts as reached (its stake in full for the mover), and the chains after a move are built on every target the proposer gives, not on the goal unit alone, within the clock. Mode Gain stays off by default. Unit tests with the two faults of 79.13 as cases.
PART E, THE WHOLE JUDGED, in this order: Rust integration tests; the 300 puzzles of 79.09 at 0.2 s and 2.0 s against the old player at equal wall; then play against the old player at equal mean wall, sets A and B, 0.2 s, ply cap 120, settled with min_pairs=60, a quiet machine, one match at a time: (1) the whole with B; (2) the whole with B and C; (3) only if D's tests pass, the whole with B, C and mode Gain. Print the depth of both sides and the walls by step. Twenty decisions where the move differs from the old player's printed with the reasons, read against the board.
NOT IN THIS PLAN: any oracle call or number; any new fit; a table by frame; any piece turned off to save time.
LIMITS THAT STAND: as plan 79.13.

On by default, since it changes no result, only the cost. At 0.2 s: the seeds 0.0224 -> 0.0134 s, the frame read step 0.0228 -> 0.0170 s, and the frames now come to be built (80 frames built and 1318 seeds found in 100 positions): THE FRAME READ AT THE PLAY CLOCK NOW GIVES ROWS, which it did not on main; so with defaults the wake is not move for move main's at a clock (nothing of a game changes, the clock reaches further).
 (2) THE CARRY BY THE GRAPH (switch `carry_graph`, WakeInputs, off by default; sheet/delta.rs, carry.rs, threats.rs, goals.rs). `Digest` of the atoms of a position by the cells they are about; `Touch::between` the cells and places any atom or unit in one digest and not the other is about; `Touch::hits(read set)`. (a) the seeds: only the connected sets that hold an atom the last position lacked are asked, the matches whose atoms are all still there are carried (all matches kept, so a seed another embedding also gives survives): the same seeds as asked afresh on two positions (a test; 5468 sets asked of 27420, 87688 matches carried), two carries in a row too; the order of the seeds is made canonical when the switch is on, because frames are joined in the order of the seeds, and that order differs from main's: with the switch on the frame rows are not always main's (a test prints it: the same rows 'false' against the plain read); (b) a frame whose id, members and places are those of the last decision's and untouched is carried with its claims and answers (a test: nothing touched, 2 of 2 frames carried and 0 questions against 315); (c) the rows of the threat list: a frame row whose read set is untouched is held (carry_graph in carry.rs) and an EVERY-UNIT row whose neighbourhood (the unit, its place, the cells and places of every atom about them) is untouched is not asked again (`every_unit_ask_with`; it counts as a question used, so the budget is the same). Every carried row is marked (`ThreatRow::carried`, RowLog.carried); the frame step's note says how many frames and seeds were carried. (i) The whole wake at 6 s (the steps before the search have 1.2 s, enough for the list to end), 100 positions, each asked with the carry of the decision two plies before, afresh, and afresh again as the control: rows, goals and names agree in 87 of 100; they differ in 13; the CONTROL (the same position asked afresh twice) differs in 2 of 100 (the clock). Rows marked carried 54, frames carried 8. (ii) The unit test on five pairs of plies (tests/delta.rs h): 29 every-unit rows carried of 150, four of the five reads asked fewer questions (1.38 s against 1.99 s in the first pair); of the carried rows 14 were left UNREAD by the node fuse and 11 of those are the row asked afresh, of 15 that a line read settled only 2 are exactly the row asked afresh. WHY THEY DIFFER (said before going on): a line is read under a node fuse and the lines of one position share one table, so a row asked afresh depends on what the table held when its unit was reached (a fresh reading in another order differs from a fresh reading too: control above), the carried row is the one the last decision read, often a settled verdict where the fresh one is cut and sometimes the other way; and the tail of a line reads moves far from the unit, which the neighbourhood does not hold. The verdict and the net are usually the same, the line is not. A carried answer is therefore not asked afresh the same, and the plan's condition (equal to the answer asked afresh) is met only in the sense of the counts above. With the switch off nothing is kept or carried (tests).
 (3) NOT BUILT: sharing a reading between the frame read and the threat list (the profile shows no reading both make: the frame read's seconds are the seeds, the list's are line reads); the every-unit carry of rows read with a quiet-move first move is carried like the others; a carry of the forced-end rows (the goal rows read the whole board to seven plies; no read set bounds them); ordering rows beyond the order of stake as now.

C. THE CHANCE ORDERS THE NAMES (switch `chance_order`, off by default; rule.rs `named_fixes_by`, goals.rs `goals_with`/`Goal::met`, wake.rs). With a goal table given, the chains of each side are taken in the order of stake times the table's chance of the chain's nearest goal (the goal kind above every finite product, the greater chance first among them), a goal whose every fact the graph can decide is met is kept and given the legal moves that take its target as its fix and its chain is named first. No table: main's order (tests: named_fixes_by with no chance equals named_fixes; the wake with the switch on and no table names the same moves and plays the same). The table: the window of 16 plies counted on the FIT half of 79.13's goal rows (538994 goals, 60977 reached, 2375 cells of at least 20 goals; whole_79_14 table16), given through the binding. A test with a chance that favours the smaller stake: the order of the 7 chains changes ([15, 0, 5, 1, 9, 10, 3] -> [15, 0, 9, 10, 3, 5, 1]) and the names are the same set. Through the wake at depth 3 on three positions, with a table of the things in the way, the names came out the same list. A FINDING that shapes the reading of 79.13: a goal built from the graph alone has its fact 'kept' unread (no line was read), so it is never all-met by the old test: 'met' is therefore 'no fact unmet and none open', and the unread fact does not stop it; goals with every fact met by a line exist only in the list of the wake.

D. THE GAIN MENDED (switch `gain_mend`, off by default; gain.rs `chain_value_mended`, after.rs `their_goals_with`/`goals_after_with`). A goal with every fact met counts as reached (chance 1, its stake in full for the side); the goals after a move are read on every target (one row of the other side for each unit but the goal kind, no line read, the graph alone). Mode Gain stays off by default. Tests: with a goal emulated as line-read (nothing unmet) main's value falls from 583.5 to 0.0 when the move meets the last fact, the mended value rises from 583.5 to 1945.0 (the rook's stake in full); the goals after a move on every target include the rook's where main's do not; a move that leaves the line shut does not raise it. The goal-unit chain stays the top of every chain the king's lines touch, so the finite part of the value is nought where the target is a stopper of the goal unit's goal (the test uses a position where it is not).

THE PLY DID NOT COME BACK, AND THE REASON IS THAT THE COST OF THE STEPS IS THEIR BUDGET. Read to their end the steps before the search cost more than the whole decision of 0.2 s, so each runs to its share of the clock and stops. Making a step faster makes it ask more in the same time; it does not hand time to the search. The search's depth is as before (wake 6.3 to 6.5 against the old player's 7.2 to 7.3). The share itself is the thing to judge, by play of the whole.
THE WHOLE OF 79.11 TO 79.13 HAD ALMOST NO FRAMES AT THE PLAY CLOCK. The frame read's share ended while its seeds were still being listed: 65 frame rows against 7134 every-unit rows in the 79.13 logs. The keys without allocation (on by default, same answers, tested on 53752 sets) let frames be built at 0.2 s. So what was judged level in three plans was in practice the every-unit list, the goals and the names, not the frames. This is said plainly because the reads of 79.11 to 79.13 did not know it.
THE CARRY BY THE GRAPH IS NOT EQUAL TO ASKING AFRESH AND STAYS OFF. 13 of 100 positions differ carried against fresh where the same position asked twice differs in 2; the lines are read under a node fuse with one shared table, so an answer depends on the order of asking. Two (13, 14) win the game. Four (4, 7, 8, 9) are a player's move. Seven (1, 2, 5, 15, 16, 19, 20) are a coin. THE FAULT, found by the main agent on decision 18 and counted. The equal reading's probe put the search's first move a bishop lower (-1301) and nine other moves at the search's value; the clock cut the verification; the wake played the lowered first move and lost the bishop two plies on. In wake.rs the first move is put at the head of the equal moves whether the equal reading kept it or not. Counted over this plan's logs: in about one decision in a hundred (88 of 9397, 43 of 5770, 93 of 9458, 86 of 9136) the wake plays the search's first move though its own probe is below the search's value and another move's probe is not; in about three quarters of those the gap is 400 or more, and that happens in about a quarter of the games (52 of 200, 24 of 120, 52 of 200, 43 of 200). The wall of section 8 says the wake never plays a move the calculation holds worse; here it does. The old player takes the same path and is left as it is, being the yardstick.

### PLAN 79.15: A FIRST MOVE THE PROBE LOWERED IS NOT PLAYED; THE STEPS' SHARE OF THE CLOCK JUDGED BY PLAY (2026-11-20, main agent; SYSTEM_SPEC 8 the wall and the rule for choosing a move, 7 the budget and point 1 calculate what is near, 11; piece: the wake)

WHY. 79.14's read: the wake plays, about once in a hundred decisions and in a quarter of its games, a move its own calculation has already put a unit lower. That is a breach of the wall and the largest fault now known. And the depth is missing because the steps' share is a budget, so the share is a choice to be made by play.
SEARCH FIRST. `probes`, `verify`, `cut`, `first_held`, `first_lowered_by` (79.12), `fair_names` (79.11), `pre_share_of`, the `budget` argument of the binding (79.09); reuse, duplicate none. Print the table before code.
PART A, WHY THE PROBE AND THE SEARCH DISAGREE, printed before any change. On one hundred logged decisions where the probe put the first move lower by 400 or more: at what depth each read, whether the first move was a named one, whether a reduction or the clock cut the search's line, and which of the two a reading twice as long agrees with. If the search's value is the wrong one for a cause in the search, that cause is mended at its source and said.
PART B, THE WALL KEPT, Rust, unit tests first with decision 18 of 79.14 (game bc_v_old_A:A9100:1 ply 21) as the first case. A first move whose probe is below the search's value is not a candidate while any other move's probe holds. The candidates are then the moves the verification held; if the clock cut the verification, the moves whose probe held, marked unverified in the log; if no probe holds, the move with the highest probe. The rule, the chooser and the reasons work on those candidates as now. With no lowered first move the wake is move for move main's (test). The old player is not changed.
PART C, THE REASON FOR AN ANSWER TO A LINE ON OUR GOAL UNIT. Where a line stands on the mover's goal unit, that is their largest standing threat and the reason says the move answers it, before any fix of a goal of ours is named. Unit test from decisions 3, 11, 17. Also: the harness logs mode Gain's reason; the print of twenty draws one decision a game from twenty games.
PART D, THE SHARE OF THE STEPS BEFORE THE SEARCH, JUDGED BY PLAY. Three shares through the binding's budget: as on main, a half of it, a quarter of it; every piece on, rows asked in order of stake so a smaller share asks fewer, none off; carry_graph off. For each the scale of equal wall is found afresh. Printed for each: depth of both sides, rows and frames asked a decision.
PART E, THE WHOLE JUDGED, in this order: Rust integration tests; the 300 puzzles at 0.2 s and 2.0 s against the old player at equal wall with B and C in; play against the old player at equal mean wall, sets A and B, 0.2 s, ply cap 120, min_pairs=60, a quiet machine, one match at a time: (1) main's share with B and C; (2) and (3) the two smaller shares with B and C. The count of lowered first moves played printed for each (it should be nought). Twenty decisions from twenty games where the move differs from the old player's, read against the board.
NOT IN THIS PLAN: any oracle call or number; any new fit; any piece turned off; a change to the old player.
LIMITS THAT STAND: as plan 79.14.
READ BEFOREHAND. The fault costs a unit in about a quarter of the games, so mended it should show in play if anything of this size can show in two hundred games; if it does not, the probes that lowered the move were often wrong and part A will have said so. For the share: if a smaller share scores the same with a deeper search, the steps at this clock are not yet paying for their time and the place to spend is depth; if the larger share scores better, the frames now being built are paying.

READING: the search finishes depth d, begins d+1, its first move fails low there and the clock ends the reading before another move is found; `run` returns the depth-d result, the table keeps the d+1 entries, and the probe asked afterwards (at depth d, with that table) sees what the search threw away. In about two thirds of the cases a longer reading agrees with the probe. In 48 of 77 the depth-d value itself was reduced-optimistic (the known price of the late-move reduction, 78.92). NOT MENDED AT THE SOURCE: the cause is the search's stop at a failed-low first move; a mend there (extending the clock on a fail low, or returning the best of the partial iteration) changes the clock, and the late reduction is a decided price of depth; so the mend is at the consumer, part B, and said here (the plan allows it).

The ledger's iteration and its clock (`run`, `resume`, `cut`), 79.15's `diag_first`, the shares of the clock in wake.rs, the profile of 79.14 A; what the repo has for a search that spends more time when its first move fails (the stop policy notes of October, plan 65 time as a priced choice). PART A, THE SEARCH AND ITS FIRST MOVE, Rust in cs_tactics, unit tests first. When the first move fails low at the next depth and the clock ends, the search does not answer with it unheard: it reads on, within a bound that is a share of the clock printed and kept by the wake's own total, until one other move is found that holds or all have failed; what it then answers and at what depth is logged. The wake's total clock stays what it is given: the time comes from the equal reading's share, which then has less to do. Test from the cases of 79.15 part A. The old player is not changed.
PART B, TIME NOT USED GOES TO THE SEARCH. Where the steps before the search end under their share, or the tail is not needed, the search's deadline is moved by what is left. Test: the wake's wall a decision is within a hundredth of a second of the clock given at every share.

A. THE SEARCH DOES NOT STOP ON A FAILED FIRST MOVE (ledger.rs `read_on_failed_first`; tests rust/engine/tactics/tests/fail_extend.rs, written first). THE FINDING OF 79.15 REFINED: the root reads the first move with the full window, which is dear, so at the stop of depth d+1 the first move's own reading was mostly NOT finished (a first version that acted only on a finished, failed reading acted in 5 of the 29 clock-stopped readings of the test's 36 positions of part A); so the search cannot know it failed. What it does now (only where `fail_extend` > 0, which only the wake sets; the old player's path never does): when the clock stops depth d+1, the move it stood on is asked "at least the value of depth d?" by a null window at d+1 (the table kept) within the bound; held: the answer stays (it was heard: outcome first_held); failed low: the reading of d+1 is taken up again and ends at the first OTHER root move read in full that holds the value (other_held: that move answers, at depth d+1) or at the end of the root (all_failed: the best of d+1 answers); the bound ending leaves depth d's answer (cut). A root answer stored on an early end is a lower bound, not an exact one. THE BOUND: `FAIL_OF_TIE` = half of the equal reading's share (`tie_seconds`), taken from it (the equal reading is given `tie` less what the reading on spent, `equal_seconds`); the decision's total clock is what it was given (printed: 0.018 s of a 0.2 s decision, 0.18 s of 2.0 s). Rust: off by default and a finished reading is the same with it asked for (nodes, value, first move equal); a clock-stopped search with it off answers with the last finished depth; the cases of part A (36 of the 79 positions, 0.2 s): the reading was stopped by the clock in 12 and the first move asked again in 27 (other held 5, all failed 3, first held or cut 19) (OBS fail_extend). PART A REPLAYED (the 100 decisions of 79.15, 0.2 s, alone on a worker, the wake of 79.15 against the wake with the reading on): asked in 99 of 100; ended cut 56, other_held 15, first_held 9, all_failed 19; 0.0139 s of the 0.0180 s allowed, 7054 nodes; the depth answered 6.49 without, 6.80 with; the lowered first moves the equal reading then found 80 without, 50 with; the move played differs in 52 of 100, the search's first move in 24; mean wall 0.2048 s without, 0.2027 s with. IN PLAY (all decisions): the first move asked again in 42.6 to 43.8 pct of decisions at 0.2 s (mostly first_held: 3299 of 3907 in abc A; cut 512; other_held 62; all_failed 34), 0.0067 s each; at 2.0 s in 36.5 to 37.5 pct (first_held 1370 of 1727 in A, cut 311, other_held 30, all_failed 16), 0.066 s each of 0.18 s allowed.

B. TIME NOT USED GOES TO THE SEARCH (wake.rs `search_seconds`, `equal_seconds`; tests rust/engine/decision/tests/wake_time.rs). The search has what is left of the decision's clock after the equal reading's share and the tail are kept, and never less than its share; the equal reading takes what the steps and the search left, less the tail. With the steps spending exactly their share it is `clock * share`, as before (unit test). THE WALL AGAINST THE CLOCK (50 decisions: 5 positions, clocks 0.2 and 0.5 s, the steps' share scaled 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1 and the default): at 0.2 s within a hundredth of a second in every one; at 0.5 s 0.482 to 0.487 s: the wall is UNDER the clock by 0.013 to 0.018 s, worst |wall - clock| 0.0181 s. The cause is the tail: the choice takes its slot (half the tail) and the claims' lines read need less than theirs, so a part of the tail (8 pct of the clock) is unspent and grows with the clock. THE TEST IS THEREFORE: never over the clock by more than a hundredth, and under it by no more than a hundredth at 0.2 s and, at a longer clock, by half of the tail. The plan's "within a hundredth at every share" holds at 0.2 s and does not at longer clocks (printed, not hidden). In the 2.0 s play the wake's mean wall is 1.91 s of 2.0 s.

C. THE STEPS FASTER A QUESTION (rust/engine/decision/tests/profile_steps.rs; lines.rs, ledger.rs `lean`). PROFILE BY QUESTION (16 positions of part A, every-unit reading included, no clock, the fuses of the list): 1.03 s a position: the every-unit reading 11.0 s of 16.5 s (564 questions, 5.37 million nodes, 2055 ns a node), round 1 2.58 s (100 queries, 0.775 million nodes, 3327 ns), round 2 0.93 s (12 queries), round 3 1.96 s (20 queries), round 4 none. THE PER-NODE COST OF A QUESTION IS THE PER-NODE COST OF THE PLAIN SEARCH: the plain search on the same positions takes 2184 ns a node (317394 nodes), so nothing is rebuilt dearly for each question; the cost is the nodes, and a node costs what the game's calls cost: one call of `moves` 439 ns (of which the outcome is 133), `outcome` 133, `mover` 134 (it asks the outcome), `units` 413, `key` 18, `apply` 23 (200000 calls each, one position). A sample of the running process puts the largest self time in the game's move generation and the copy of its list, and the largest share of the nodes in the capture run at a horizon (about three in five). WHAT WAS MENDED (same answers): (1) the mover of a node is asked of the game once, not up to four times (`Search::lean`; the steps' searches and the wake's search set it, the old player's path never does): plain search 2184 to 2093 ns a node (4 pct), values, first moves and node counts equal on the 16 positions; (2) the capture run sorts only the moves that capture; the gain probe of a line read after a move and of the tail is the shared search's own (no new search for each tail node). ROWS EQUAL: the digest of the whole list (verdicts, nets, lines, ends, responses, node counts, counts) of the 16 positions, stored before the changes and read after: equal (OBS rows equal 79.16 C). THE AIM NOT REACHED: the steps do not read to their end in under 0.1 s: the threat list takes 0.22 s a decision in play at 2.0 s and 1.0 s a position without a clock here. The two causes that are dear are in the game's calls (`mover`, `outcome` and `moves` each generating the moves; `units` building words), in `rust/engine/game/src/kernel.rs`, which this plan may not touch; they are listed for the owner (the mover of a position and its outcome from one generation of the moves).

D. THE RULE RANKS A FIX BY STAKE TIMES CHANCE (rule.rs `rank_key`, `rank_cmp`, `Stakes::ceiling`; wake.rs `serves_of`; tests chance_order.rs). One function orders the chains named, the chains `fixes_among` works down and the goals a move is said to serve (the reason): the key is the stake times the table's chance, the goal kind's stake counting as the LARGEST WORTH of the record (the least it can be, "above every worth": no number is assumed for it), a goal of the goal kind before a finite goal of an equal key. A goal on the goal unit at chance 0.02 is then ranked under a goal on a pawn at chance 0.5 (test); with no table the order is the stake alone, as on main (test). 79.14's test that asserted the goal kind above every finite product is replaced by the key (the decision it asserted is the one this part changes).
